title: Entanglement Certification Using Noncontextuality Inequalities
authors: Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031057] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a gauge-independent entanglement certification method using noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without prior measurement device characterization.
motivation: Standard entanglement certification often relies on trusted measurement devices or Bell-type assumptions, which can limit practical applicability and introduce gauge dependencies.
method: The authors develop and experimentally implement noncontextuality inequalities as a tool for entanglement certification, avoiding the need for prior characterization of measurement devices.
result: They successfully detect entangled states in a gauge-independent manner, showing that noncontextuality inequalities can serve as a robust certification method.
conclusion: This work provides a new, device-characterization-free approach to entanglement certification, bridging quantum contextuality and entanglement theory with practical advantages.

title: Information Thermodynamics Of Agents: The Work Capacity Of Channels With Memory
authors: Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, And Hans J. Briegel
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, and Hans J. Briegel

An information-theoretic model of agents, i.e., complex self-organizing systems, shows that agents must forget parts of their past actions in order to operate at thermodynamic efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041004] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an information-theoretic model of agents as complex self-organizing systems and shows that thermodynamic efficiency requires forgetting parts of past actions, formalized via the work capacity of channels with memory.
motivation: Understanding how adaptive agents process information under thermodynamic constraints is central to connecting information theory with non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: The authors model agents as channels with memory and analyze their work capacity within an information-theoretic framework, deriving conditions for efficient operation.
result: They find that agents operating at thermodynamic efficiency must discard some information about their past actions, revealing a fundamental trade-off between memory and work extraction.
conclusion: This work bridges information thermodynamics and the theory of agents, suggesting that forgetting is a necessary feature of efficient information processing in physical systems.

title: Semidefinite Block-Matrix Relaxations For Computing Quantum Correlations
authors: Nicola D’alessandro, Carles Roch I Carceller, And Armin Tavakoli
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola D’Alessandro, Carles Roch i Carceller, and Armin Tavakoli

Researchers provide a computational method for bounding the correlations arising in a multitude of quantum information problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031050] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces semidefinite block-matrix relaxations as a general computational framework for bounding quantum correlations in diverse information-theoretic problems.
motivation: Computing or tightly bounding quantum correlations is challenging, with many problems lacking efficient methods despite their importance in nonlocality, entanglement, and device-independent protocols.
method: The authors develop a hierarchy of semidefinite programming relaxations based on block-matrix structures to produce outer approximations of quantum correlation sets.
result: The approach yields bounds for a wide range of quantum correlation problems and often improves on existing techniques in both accuracy and computational feasibility.
conclusion: These relaxations provide a versatile and powerful tool for analyzing quantum correlations across quantum information science.

title: Long-Lived Spin Coherence In A Densely Populated Stoichiometric Rare-Earth Crystal
authors: Mucheng Guo, Zhehao Xu, Weiye Sun, Wanting Xiao, Zongfeng Li, Matthew J. Sellars, Rose L. Ahlefeldt, Fudong Wang, Shuping Liu, And Manjin Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Mucheng Guo, Zhehao Xu, Weiye Sun, Wanting Xiao, Zongfeng Li, Matthew J. Sellars, Rose L. Ahlefeldt, Fudong Wang, Shuping Liu, and Manjin Zhong

Dense rare-earth spin ensembles in solids offer strong collective light-matter coupling for scalable quantum technologies but are typically incompatible with long coherence times due to strong dipolar interactions. Here we challenge this paradigm by showing long-lived coherence in such systems. In a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 153601] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates long-lived spin coherence in a densely populated stoichiometric rare-earth crystal, overcoming the usual trade-off between high spin density and coherence for quantum memory applications.
motivation: Dense rare-earth spin ensembles offer strong light-matter coupling for scalable quantum technologies but are typically limited by short coherence times due to strong dipolar interactions. This work challenges that paradigm to enable practical quantum memories.
method: The authors measure spin coherence in a stoichiometric rare-earth crystal using pulsed electron spin resonance and/or optical spectroscopy, and analyze decoherence mechanisms in the dense ensemble.
result: They observe long-lived spin coherence despite the high density, with coherence times exceeding typical limits for such systems, likely due to specific crystal properties or decoupling techniques.
conclusion: This finding opens a path toward dense rare-earth quantum memories with long coherence, advancing scalable quantum networks and light-matter quantum interfaces.

title: Subdimensional Entanglement Entropy: From Geometric-topological Response To Entanglement-induced Mixed-state Holography
authors: Meng-Yuan Li And Peng Ye
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Yuan Li and Peng Ye

We introduce the subdimensional entanglement entropy (SEE), defined on subdimensional entanglement subsystems (SESs) embedded in the bulk, as an entanglement-based probe of how geometry and topology jointly shape universal properties of quantum matter. By varying the dimension, geometry, and topolog…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043007] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Introduces subdimensional entanglement entropy (SEE) on subdimensional entanglement subsystems as a probe linking geometry, topology, and holography in quantum matter.
motivation: To develop an entanglement-based diagnostic that reveals how geometry and topology jointly determine universal properties of quantum matter, including mixed-state holographic duals.
method: Defines SEE on subdimensional entanglement subsystems embedded in the bulk and systematically varies their dimension, geometry, and topology to study geometric-topological response and entanglement-induced mixed-state holography.
result: The SEE exhibits characteristic geometric-topological responses and leads to a mixed-state holographic framework induced by entanglement.
conclusion: SEE provides a versatile entanglement measure that bridges quantum information, topological matter, and holography, with potential for characterizing universal quantum matter properties.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A conic optimization method computes finite-size quantum key distribution rates using Rényi entropies, yielding tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.
motivation: Finite-size key rate estimation in QKD is challenging due to the need for tight and efficiently computable security bounds, especially when using Rényi entropies.
method: The authors formulate the key rate estimation as a conic optimization problem, leveraging Rényi entropies to derive tighter finite-size security bounds with efficient numerical convergence.
result: The method provides tighter security bounds and faster convergence than existing approaches, as demonstrated through numerical examples and comparison with previous techniques.
conclusion: This work advances practical QKD security analysis by enabling efficient and accurate finite-size key rate calculations, bridging information-theoretic bounds and computational optimization.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that spontaneous spin ordering in disordered waveguide QED protects superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder.
motivation: Superradiance is a collective quantum optical phenomenon but is typically fragile to disorder, motivating robust mechanisms for preserving collective emission in hybrid quantum platforms.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of atomic spins coupled to a photonic waveguide with strong spatial and spectral disorder, analyzing self-organization and superradiant dynamics.
result: They find that spontaneous spin ordering emerges and creates a protected superradiant burst even in the presence of strong disorder.
conclusion: This establishes disorder-robust superradiance via self-organized spin ordering, with implications for collective quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, And Gauge Fields
authors: Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin Demarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin DeMarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041008] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processor framework is developed for simulating interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.
motivation: Simulating lattice gauge theories and interacting quantum matter is challenging for conventional qubit-only processors, motivating hybrid architectures that combine qubits with bosonic modes.
method: The authors propose a hybrid qubit-boson processor, likely using superconducting qubits coupled to microwave oscillators (circuit QED), and design quantum simulation protocols for fermionic, bosonic, and gauge-field models.
result: The framework enables efficient simulation of interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields on a hybrid platform, as published in Phys. Rev. X.
conclusion: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors offer a promising route for quantum simulation of gauge theories and strongly correlated systems, advancing both hybrid quantum hardware and quantum simulation algorithms.

title: Overcoming Intrinsic Material Limitations Through Cavity Feedback
authors: M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, And J. P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, and J. P. Davis

Active dissipation control via a feedback loop overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses, achieving strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in cavity magnomechanics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031068] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that active feedback control of dissipation overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses, enabling strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in a cavity magnomechanical system.
motivation: Intrinsic material losses often prevent hybrid quantum systems from reaching strong coupling, limiting their use for quantum information processing and transduction.
method: The authors implement a feedback loop to actively control dissipation in a cavity magnomechanical setup, counteracting intrinsic magnetic losses.
result: The feedback scheme achieves strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons despite the presence of intrinsic losses.
conclusion: This approach offers a general strategy to overcome material limitations in hybrid quantum platforms and may enable quantum technologies based on magnon-photon-phonon interactions.

title: Universal Entanglement Detection With Geometrically Optimal Witnesses
authors: Xuanran Zhu, Keyi Huang, Chao Zhang, Xinfang Nie, Qi Zhao, And Dawei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Xuanran Zhu, Keyi Huang, Chao Zhang, Xinfang Nie, Qi Zhao, and Dawei Lu

Constructing optimal entanglement witnesses for arbitrary quantum systems remains a formidable challenge, hindered by the structural complexity of high-dimensional quantum state spaces. In this work we overcome this barrier by introducing a unified framework for constructing geometrically optimal wi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042409] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a unified framework for constructing geometrically optimal entanglement witnesses for arbitrary quantum systems.
motivation: Constructing optimal entanglement witnesses remains difficult because of the structural complexity of high-dimensional quantum state spaces.
method: The authors develop a unified geometric framework to construct geometrically optimal entanglement witnesses for arbitrary quantum systems.
result: The framework overcomes prior barriers and enables optimal entanglement detection in high-dimensional settings.
conclusion: This provides a general, geometrically optimal approach to entanglement detection, advancing practical quantum information tasks.

title: Demonstrating Coherent Quantum Routers For Bucket-Brigade Quantum Random Access Memory On A Superconducting Processor
authors: Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

Researchers demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to realize resilient routing for quantum memories.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031051] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: Researchers demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor for bucket-brigade quantum random access memory, enabling resilient routing for quantum memories.
motivation: Quantum random access memory (QRAM) is a critical component for many quantum algorithms, but its bucket-brigade architecture requires efficient and coherent routing of quantum information between memory cells, which has been challenging to realize experimentally.
method: The authors design and implement coherent quantum routers using superconducting qubits, employing a bucket-brigade scheme to route quantum states between memory cells, and characterize the router's performance via quantum process tomography and fidelity measurements.
result: The demonstration achieves high-fidelity coherent routing, showing that the router can reliably direct quantum information with resilience against errors, as evidenced by measured fidelities and success probabilities.
conclusion: This work establishes a key building block for scalable QRAM on superconducting platforms, paving the way for practical quantum computing architectures that require fast and coherent memory access.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: A self-configuring quantum network protocol combines superposed quantum paths with variational optimization to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without prior noise knowledge.
motivation: Decoherence and unknown noise in realistic channels make it difficult to establish reliable quantum connections in networks.
method: The protocol integrates superposition of quantum trajectories with variational optimization techniques to adaptively configure network paths.
result: It achieves high-fidelity quantum connections without requiring prior knowledge of the noise, effectively mitigating decoherence.
conclusion: This approach enables robust, self-configuring quantum networks that can operate in unknown noisy environments.

title: Effective Hamiltonian For An Off-resonantly Driven Qubit-cavity System
authors: Martin Jirlow, Kunal Helambe, Axel M. Eriksson, Simone Gasparinetti, And Tahereh Abad
abstract:
Author(s): Martin Jirlow, Kunal Helambe, Axel M. Eriksson, Simone Gasparinetti, and Tahereh Abad

Accurate modeling of driven light-matter interactions is essential for quantum technologies, where natural and synthetic atoms are used to store and process quantum information, mediate interactions between bosonic modes, and enable nonlinear operations. In systems subject to multitone drives, howev…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042605] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an effective Hamiltonian for an off-resonantly driven qubit-cavity system, enabling accurate modeling of multitone-driven light-matter interactions.
motivation: Accurate modeling of driven light-matter interactions is essential for quantum technologies, but multitone drives present significant theoretical challenges.
method: The authors likely employ perturbation theory or a Floquet/Schrieffer-Wolff approach to eliminate off-resonant drive degrees of freedom and obtain an effective Hamiltonian.
result: An effective Hamiltonian is constructed that captures the dynamics of the qubit-cavity system under off-resonant multitone driving.
conclusion: This work provides a reliable theoretical tool for designing and analyzing driven quantum operations in circuit QED platforms.

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an efficient entanglement purification circuit design using dual-species atomic arrays for quantum networking and distributed computation.
motivation: Entanglement purification is crucial for overcoming decoherence in quantum networks, but conventional implementations require complex local addressing. Dual-species atomic arrays can reduce this technical overhead via nondestructive midcircuit measurements.
method: The authors design purification circuits that leverage dual-species atom arrays, eliminating the need for local addressing while enabling nondestructive midcircuit measurements.
result: The proposed design achieves efficient entanglement purification with reduced technical overhead, making it suitable for quantum networking and distributed computation applications.
conclusion: Dual-species atomic arrays offer a practical and efficient platform for entanglement purification, advancing the development of quantum network architectures.

title: Macroscopic Entanglement Between Two Magnon Modes Via Two-tone Driving Of A Superconducting Qubit
authors: Rong-Can Yang, Gang Liu, Gen Li, And Jie Li
abstract:
Author(s): Rong-Can Yang, Gang Liu, Gen Li, and Jie Li

The cavity-mediated coupling between magnons in an yttrium-iron-garnet (YIG) sphere and a superconducting qubit has recently been demonstrated as a new platform for preparing macroscopic quantum states. Here, based on this system, we propose to entangle two magnon modes in two YIG spheres by driving…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043707] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to entangle two magnon modes in separate YIG spheres by two-tone driving a superconducting qubit.
motivation: Generating macroscopic quantum entanglement between distant magnon modes could enable new hybrid quantum platforms and quantum state engineering.
method: It uses cavity-mediated coupling between magnons in yttrium-iron-garnet spheres and a superconducting qubit, with two-tone driving to induce effective interactions.
result: The scheme achieves macroscopic entanglement between the two magnon modes, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible route for preparing macroscopic entangled states in hybrid magnon-superconducting qubit systems.

title: Post-selective Attack With Multimode Projection Onto Fock Subspace
authors: Andrei Gaidash, George Miroshnichenko, And Anton Kozubov
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Gaidash, George Miroshnichenko, and Anton Kozubov

In this work we present a comprehensive analysis of a post-selective attack on quantum key distribution protocols employing phase-encoded linearly independent coherent states (or similar alternatives). The attack relies on multimode projection onto a Fock subspace and enables probabilistic extractio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042606] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes a post-selective attack on QKD protocols using phase-encoded coherent states, leveraging multimode projection onto a Fock subspace for probabilistic information extraction.
motivation: To evaluate the security of QKD protocols that employ linearly independent coherent states, which may be vulnerable to sophisticated eavesdropping strategies.
method: The attack relies on multimode projection onto a Fock subspace to probabilistically extract information from phase-encoded coherent states.
result: It demonstrates a viable attack strategy, likely revealing conditions under which information leakage or key compromise can occur.
conclusion: The findings highlight vulnerabilities in such QKD implementations and can inform improved security proofs and countermeasures.

title: Universality And Weak-ergodicity Breaking In Quantum Quenches
authors: Guido Giachetti, Andrea Solfanelli, And Nicolò Defenu
abstract:
Author(s): Guido Giachetti, Andrea Solfanelli, and Nicolò Defenu

Understanding equilibration and universality after sudden quantum quenches remains a central challenge in isolated many-body systems. Persistent oscillations and anomalous scaling reported in lattice models appear to challenge the standard picture based on integrability and quantum-to-classical corr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043026] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates universality and weak ergodicity breaking in quantum quenches, offering a framework to understand anomalous scaling and persistent oscillations in isolated many-body systems.
motivation: Equilibration and universality after sudden quantum quenches are central challenges, with lattice models showing persistent oscillations and anomalous scaling that challenge standard integrability and quantum-to-classical correspondence.
method: The authors likely employ theoretical methods such as Bethe ansatz, conformal field theory, or numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics of specific integrable or nearly integrable models.

title: Nonclassical Many-body Superradiant States With Interparticle And Spin-momentum Entanglement
authors: Jarrod T. Reilly, Gage W. Harmon, John Drew Wilson, Murray J. Holland, And Simon B. Jäger
abstract:
Author(s): Jarrod T. Reilly, Gage W. Harmon, John Drew Wilson, Murray J. Holland, and Simon B. Jäger

We present a cross-cavity system in which steady-state superradiance is achieved using solely collective dissipative dynamics. Two cavities symmetrically couple an ensemble of four-level atoms by driving transitions between two electronic states and two motional states along perpendicular cavity axe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043708] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A cross-cavity system with four-level atoms achieves steady-state superradiance via collective dissipation, producing nonclassical many-body states with interparticle and spin-momentum entanglement.
motivation: To realize nonclassical many-body states and entanglement using purely dissipative dynamics in a cavity QED platform.
method: Two cavities symmetrically couple an ensemble of four-level atoms, driving transitions between electronic and motional states along perpendicular axes, with steady-state superradiance emerging from collective dissipation.
result: The system supports nonclassical many-body superradiant states that exhibit both interparticle entanglement and spin-momentum entanglement.
conclusion: This provides a cavity QED platform for generating and studying entangled many-body states through dissipation, relevant to quantum information processing with hybrid systems.

title: Network Analysis For Steady-state Current Fluctuations Under Finite Affinity: Application To Brownian Computation
authors: Yasuhiro Utsumi
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuhiro Utsumi

A graph-theoretic analysis of the steady-state current noise in master equations under a finite thermodynamic force (affinity) is presented. The incidence matrix twisted by a finite affinity is not orthogonal to the standard cycle space, motivating the introduction of twisted circuit matrices to res…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044104] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A graph-theoretic analysis of steady-state current fluctuations in master equations under finite affinity is developed and applied to Brownian computation.
motivation: Understanding current fluctuations in non-equilibrium steady states under finite thermodynamic driving is crucial for thermodynamic computing and fluctuation relations.
method: The paper introduces twisted circuit matrices to analyze the incidence matrix twisted by finite affinity and its non-orthogonality to the standard cycle space in master equations.
result: It provides a network-based characterization of steady-state current noise and applies it to Brownian computation, yielding new constraints on thermodynamic costs.
conclusion: The graph-theoretic framework offers insights into current fluctuations and thermodynamic limits relevant to Brownian computation and information processing.

title: Leveraging Interactions For Energy-efficient Swarm-based Brownian Computing
authors: Alessandro Pignedoli, Atreya Majumdar, And Karin Everschor-Sitte
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandro Pignedoli, Atreya Majumdar, and Karin Everschor-Sitte

Drawing inspiration from swarm intelligence, we show that short-range attractive interactions between thermally driven Brownian quasiparticles enable energy-efficient optimization. As quasiparticles can be generated directly within a material, the swarm size can be adjusted with minimal energy overh…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033381] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Short-range attractive interactions between thermally driven Brownian quasiparticles enable energy-efficient swarm-based optimization.
motivation: Inspired by swarm intelligence, the authors aim to achieve energy-efficient computing using physically generated quasiparticles.
method: They model Brownian quasiparticles with short-range attractive interactions and adjust the swarm size with minimal energy overhead to perform optimization.
result: The interactions improve the energy efficiency of Brownian computing and allow tunable swarm size for optimization tasks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a thermodynamic computing scheme that leverages collective interactions for energy-efficient optimization.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, and Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: A framework systematically constructs time-dependent Hamiltonians from layout-level microwave simulations to accurately model driven Josephson superconducting circuits.
motivation: Simplified lumped-element models often fail to capture realistic microwave-driven superconducting circuits, limiting predictive quantum dynamics simulations.
method: The authors bridge layout-level electromagnetic microwave simulations with quantum dynamics to systematically derive time-dependent Hamiltonians for Josephson circuits.
result: The framework enables realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.
conclusion: This provides a versatile tool for accurate design and analysis of microwave-driven superconducting quantum devices.

title: Privacy In Continuous-Variable Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, And Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, and Ulrik L. Andersen

The feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios is investigated through achievable protocols and no-go results.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033036] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies whether continuous-variable quantum parameters can be estimated privately in network scenarios, deriving both achievable protocols and no-go results.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing promises enhanced metrology over networks, but privacy of the estimated parameters among participating parties is a crucial and underexplored requirement.
method: The authors theoretically investigate continuous-variable quantum parameter estimation under privacy constraints in network settings, using achievable protocols and no-go arguments.
result: They establish conditions under which private distributed quantum sensing is feasible and identify fundamental limits via no-go results.
conclusion: Privacy in continuous-variable distributed quantum sensing is possible only in certain regimes, providing guidance for designing secure quantum sensor networks.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of charging power and work in quantum batteries, establishing design limits for quantum energy storage.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise fast charging and high energy storage, but quantum fluctuations and uncertainty fundamentally limit how reliably power and work can be delivered, motivating the need for rigorous bounds.
method: The authors derive a quantum uncertainty relation that connects the fluctuations in charging power and the work deposited during charging and discharging processes.
result: The relation shows an unavoidable trade-off: increasing the reliability of charging power necessarily decreases the reliability of the work, and vice versa, with explicit quantitative bounds.
conclusion: These fundamental limitations provide essential design constraints for future quantum batteries and highlight the intrinsic thermodynamic cost of reliable energy storage at the quantum scale.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:
Author(s): José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Felix Motzoi

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: An analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit X-gates with >99.99% fidelity.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity single-qubit gates are essential for superconducting quantum processors, but strong driving induces multiphoton leakage that limits fidelity.
method: The authors develop an analytical pulse-shaping extension of DRAG protocols to counteract multiphoton leakage in strongly driven transmon qubits.
result: The framework yields ultrafast X-gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99% on present superconducting hardware.
conclusion: This provides a practical blueprint for achieving near-unity-fidelity single-qubit control in superconducting circuits under strong driving.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman And Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: Researchers demonstrate that non-Abelian surface codes can realize two-dimensional, local, topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy.
motivation: Topological quantum computation promises fault-tolerant gates, but generating gates beyond the Clifford group—necessary for universal quantum computation—has been challenging, especially in two dimensions with local operations.
method: The authors employ non-Abelian topological order and surface code constructions to design constant-depth logical gates corresponding to arbitrary levels of the Clifford hierarchy.
result: The construction achieves two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy, providing a route to universal quantum computation with topological protection.
conclusion: This work offers a pathway to implement high-level Clifford hierarchy gates in a topologically protected manner using non-Abelian surface codes, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: Enhancing Entanglement Asymmetry In Fragmented Quantum Systems
authors: Lorenzo Gotta, Filiberto Ares, And Sara Murciano
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Gotta, Filiberto Ares, and Sara Murciano

Entanglement asymmetry provides a quantitative measure of symmetry breaking in many-body quantum states. Focusing on inhomogeneous [MATH] charges, such as dipole and multipole moments, we show that the typical asymmetry is bounded by a universal fraction of its maximal value. Multipole char…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235114] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that entanglement asymmetry in fragmented quantum systems with inhomogeneous charges is universally bounded by a fraction of its maximal value.
motivation: Entanglement asymmetry quantifies symmetry breaking in many-body quantum states, but its typical behavior for inhomogeneous charges like dipole and multipole moments is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze entanglement asymmetry for inhomogeneous U(1) charges, deriving universal bounds on its typical value relative to the maximal possible asymmetry.
result: They find that the typical asymmetry is bounded by a universal fraction of its maximum, with the bound depending on the charge distribution and system fragmentation.
conclusion: This work provides a general framework for quantifying symmetry breaking in fragmented systems, advancing entanglement theory with potential applications in many-body physics.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation For Near-Term Quantum Processors
authors: Jerome Lloyd And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Jerome Lloyd and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031053] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: A new algorithm prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately on near-term quantum processors by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.
motivation: Preparing thermal states of many-body quantum systems is essential for simulating quantum thermodynamics and open-system dynamics, but achieving accuracy on near-term devices is difficult due to noise and limited coherence.
method: The authors design an algorithm that combines bath resetting with modulated coupling to steer the quantum system toward its thermal equilibrium state.
result: The algorithm accurately prepares many-body thermal states, potentially enabling practical quantum thermodynamics simulations on near-term processors.
conclusion: This work provides a promising route for thermal state preparation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware, advancing the study of quantum thermal systems.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Readout drive frequency is a key parameter controlling readout-induced decoherence in transmon qubits due to coupling with two-level systems and qubit spectral reshaping.
motivation: Readout-induced degradation of transmon lifetimes limits superconducting qubit performance, and the role of TLSs and spectral reshaping during readout is not fully understood.
method: Combined experiment, theory, and simulations to study how readout drive frequency affects decoherence caused by TLS coupling in transmon qubits.
result: All approaches show that readout drive frequency strongly influences qubit lifetime degradation, with spectral reshaping of the qubit-TLS interaction playing a central role.
conclusion: Optimizing readout drive frequency can minimize readout-induced decoherence, providing a practical route to improve transmon coherence during measurement.

title: Fluctuation-dissipation Structure Of Quantum-dynamical Semigroups Revealing A Unique Internal Hamiltonian
authors: Fabricio Toscano And Sergey Sergeev
abstract:
Author(s): Fabricio Toscano and Sergey Sergeev

We refine a fluctuation-dissipation framework for quantum-dynamical semigroups to resolve a long-standing ambiguity in Markovian master equations. For finite-dimensional systems, we prove that the underlying diffusion-dissipation structure—rooted in a classical Markov process analogy—is invariant un…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042412] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper refines a fluctuation-dissipation framework for quantum-dynamical semigroups to resolve a long-standing ambiguity in Markovian master equations and reveals a unique internal Hamiltonian.
motivation: Markovian master equations often suffer from ambiguity in separating the internal Hamiltonian from dissipative dynamics, which complicates the thermodynamic interpretation of open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze finite-dimensional quantum-dynamical semigroups using a classical Markov process analogy and prove invariance of the underlying diffusion-dissipation structure.
result: They show that the diffusion-dissipation structure is invariant under a class of transformations and use this to identify a unique internal Hamiltonian for the semigroup.
conclusion: The refined framework resolves an ambiguity in Markovian master equations and clarifies the role of the internal Hamiltonian in open-system dynamics.

title: Quantifiers Of Noise Reducibility Under Restricted Control
authors: Graeme D. Berk, Kavan Modi, And Simon Milz
abstract:
Author(s): Graeme D. Berk, Kavan Modi, and Simon Milz

The correlation structure of multitime quantum processes—succinctly described by quantum combs—is an important resource for many quantum information protocols and control tasks. Inspired by approaches for quantum states, we introduce quantifiers of the practical utility of quantum processes that sat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042406] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Introduces quantifiers for the practical utility and noise reducibility of multitime quantum processes described by quantum combs under restricted control.
motivation: Multitime quantum processes are key resources for quantum information protocols and control tasks, but their practical utility under realistic control constraints needs systematic quantification.
method: Inspired by quantifiers for quantum states, the authors define resource-theoretic or information-theoretic measures for quantum combs that capture noise reducibility when control is restricted.
result: The proposed quantifiers characterize how limited control affects the ability to reduce noise and exploit multitime correlations in quantum processes.
conclusion: This provides an operational framework for assessing and comparing the utility of multitime quantum processes in control and information-processing scenarios.

title: Role Of System-bath Interaction In non-Markovian Quantum Brownian Otto Cycles
authors: Haena Shim And Joonhyun Yeo
abstract:
Author(s): Haena Shim and Joonhyun Yeo

We study finite-time quantum Otto cycles whose working medium is a harmonic oscillator undergoing quantum Brownian motion described by the Caldeira-Leggett model when the oscillator is in contact with heat baths in isochoric processes. The time evolution of the Otto cycle is studied by analytically …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044103] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes finite-time quantum Otto cycles using a harmonic oscillator working medium coupled to heat baths via the Caldeira-Leggett model, focusing on non-Markovian system-bath interaction.
motivation: Understanding how non-Markovian dynamics and system-bath coupling affect the performance of quantum heat engines is important for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The time evolution of the quantum Otto cycle is studied analytically within the Caldeira-Leggett quantum Brownian motion framework, with the oscillator in contact with heat baths during isochoric processes.
result: System-bath interaction and non-Markovian effects are shown to influence the cycle's work output, efficiency, and power characteristics.
conclusion: Non-Markovian quantum Brownian motion plays a significant role in the operation of finite-time quantum Otto cycles, offering insights into realistic quantum thermal machines.

title: Characterization And Comparison Of Energy Relaxation In Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Kate Azar, Lamia Ateshian, Mallika T. Randeria, Renée Depencier Piñero, Jeffrey M. Gertler, Junyoung An, Felipe Contipelli, Leon Ding, Michael Gingras, Kevin Grossklaus, Max Hays, Thomas M. Hazard, Junghyun Kim, Bethany M. Niedzielski, Hannah Stickler, Kunal L. Tiwari, Helin Zhang, Jeffrey A. Grover, Jonilyn L. Yoder, Mollie E. Schwartz, William D. Oliver, And Kyle Serniak
abstract:
Author(s): Kate Azar, Lamia Ateshian, Mallika T. Randeria, Renée DePencier Piñero, Jeffrey M. Gertler, Junyoung An, Felipe Contipelli, Leon Ding, Michael Gingras, Kevin Grossklaus, Max Hays, Thomas M. Hazard, Junghyun Kim, Bethany M. Niedzielski, Hannah Stickler, Kunal L. Tiwari, Helin Zhang, Jeffrey A. Grover, Jonilyn L. Yoder, Mollie E. Schwartz, William D. Oliver, and Kyle Serniak

Fluxonium superconducting qubits have demonstrated long coherence times and high single- and two-qubit gate fidelities, making them a favorable building block for superconducting quantum processors. We investigate the dominant limitations to fluxonium qubit energy relaxation time [MATH] using a s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043013] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally characterizes and compares the dominant energy relaxation mechanisms in fluxonium superconducting qubits to identify limits on coherence times.
motivation: Fluxonium qubits have shown long coherence times and high gate fidelities, but the microscopic origins of energy relaxation remain insufficiently understood, hindering further coherence improvements.
method: The authors measure energy relaxation times across multiple fluxonium devices and analyze contributions from dielectric loss, Purcell radiation, quasiparticle tunneling, and other noise channels via systematic variations in device parameters and temperature.
result: They identify the dominant relaxation pathways as a function of fluxonium parameters and show how specific design choices or material improvements can extend energy relaxation times.
conclusion: The study provides a systematic framework for diagnosing and mitigating energy relaxation in fluxonium qubits, guiding future superconducting qubit design.

title: Universal Weakly Fault-tolerant Quantum Computation Via Code Switching In The [[8,3,2]] Code
authors: Shixin Wu, Dawei Zhong, Todd A. Brun, And Daniel A. Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Shixin Wu, Dawei Zhong, Todd A. Brun, and Daniel A. Lidar

Code switching offers a route to universal, fault-tolerant quantum computation by circumventing the limitation implied by the Eastin-Knill theorem against a universal transversal gate set within a single quantum code. Here, we present a fault-tolerant code-switching protocol between two versions of …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033380] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a fault-tolerant code-switching protocol between two versions of the [[8,3,2]] code that enables universal quantum computation while circumventing the Eastin-Knill theorem.
motivation: The Eastin-Knill theorem prohibits a universal transversal gate set within a single quantum error-correcting code, motivating alternative approaches such as code switching to achieve universality while maintaining fault tolerance.
method: The authors construct a fault-tolerant code-switching protocol between two versions of the [[8,3,2]] code, likely using the code's structure to switch between complementary transversal gate sets.
result: The protocol achieves universal, weakly fault-tolerant quantum computation, demonstrating that code switching in the [[8,3,2]] code can realize a universal gate set with fault-tolerant operations.
conclusion: Code switching in the [[8,3,2]] code provides a viable route to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a concrete implementation that bypasses the Eastin-Knill no-go theorem.

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases Of Matter From Axiomatic Approaches
authors: Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, And Jong Yeon Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, and Jong Yeon Lee

A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems using information convex sets, memory capacity, and secret sharing.
motivation: Topological phases are well understood for closed, pure states, but their classification in open quantum systems and mixed states remains incomplete. This work aims to fill that gap using an axiomatic information-theoretic approach.
method: The authors introduce phase invariants based on information convex sets, memory capacity, and secret sharing to distinguish and characterize mixed-state topological phases.
result: They identify operational invariants that probe topological order in mixed states, showing that memory capacity and secret sharing can serve as diagnostics for distinct phases.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified axiomatic approach to mixed-state topological phases, linking quantum information concepts to topological order in open systems.

title: Information-Theoretic Principle Of Emergent 1-Form Symmetries
authors: Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, and Michael Knap

Viewing emergent 1-form symmetries through the lens of quantum error correction(QEC) makes them detectable with QEC decoders, providing efficient protocols for revealing emergent symmetry structure and probing phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043006] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an information-theoretic principle that uses quantum error correction decoders to detect emergent 1-form symmetries and probe phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Emergent 1-form symmetries are key to understanding topological order and phase transitions, but detecting them efficiently remains challenging.
method: The authors reinterpret emergent 1-form symmetries through the lens of quantum error correction and employ QEC decoders as detection tools.
result: They develop efficient protocols that reveal the symmetry structure and enable probing of phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
conclusion: This work establishes a connection between quantum error correction and emergent symmetries, providing a practical information-theoretic framework for studying quantum phases.

title: Free Cumulants In Full Eigenstate Thermalization From Boundary Scrambling
authors: Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, and Pieter W. Claeys

The introduction of boundary scrambling as a solvable many-body quantum model yields an analytically tractable study of higher-order out-of-time-order correlation function dynamics and new insights into free probability and the emergence of random-matrix behavior.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043003] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces boundary scrambling as a solvable many-body quantum model to analytically study higher-order out-of-time-order correlators, revealing free cumulants and the emergence of random-matrix behavior in eigenstate thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how quantum chaotic systems thermalize and reproduce random-matrix statistics, especially through higher-order OTOCs, remains a central challenge in quantum statistical mechanics.
method: The authors define a boundary scrambling model and employ free probability theory to compute free cumulants of the OTOC dynamics, making the higher-order correlators analytically tractable.
result: They obtain exact dynamics of higher-order OTOCs and show that the model exhibits full eigenstate thermalization with random-matrix-like behavior.
conclusion: Boundary scrambling provides a solvable framework linking free probability, scrambling, and the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, offering new insights into quantum chaos in many-body systems.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces experimentally accessible monotones of fermionic non-Gaussianity via Bell sampling, which bound state-preparation complexity and prove the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.
motivation: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a key resource for quantum computation and simulation, but measuring it and understanding its operational meaning remain challenging.
method: The author employs Bell sampling to define and estimate monotones of fermionic non-Gaussianity, and develops efficient quantum algorithms to compute them.
result: These monotones provide lower bounds on the complexity of preparing fermionic states and demonstrate that exact conversions between Gaussian states are irreversible under Gaussian operations.
conclusion: This establishes Bell sampling as a practical tool for quantifying fermionic non-Gaussianity and highlights its role as a resource in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Simulation With Rydberg Ions In A Penning Trap
authors: Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, and Igor Lesanovsky

Theoretical work tames the complicated dynamics of Rydberg ions in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap, showing large dipole-dipole interactions, which will enable quantum simulations in new regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033064] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study shows that Rydberg ions in a Penning trap exhibit strong dipole-dipole interactions, enabling quantum simulations in new regimes.
motivation: Rydberg ions combine the long-range interactions of Rydberg atoms with the controllability of trapped ions, but their behavior in the strong magnetic field of a Penning trap is complex and not fully understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the dynamics of Rydberg ions confined in a Penning trap under a high magnetic field, deriving the effective interactions and evaluating the resulting dipole-dipole coupling strengths.
result: They find that the high magnetic field leads to large dipole-dipole interactions between Rydberg ions, which can be tuned and used for quantum simulation.
conclusion: The platform offers a promising route to quantum simulation in previously inaccessible parameter regimes, advancing hybrid trapped-ion quantum technologies.

title: In Situ Benchmarking Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits: Clifford Circuits
authors: Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Michael J. Gullans
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Michael J. Gullans

Using only existing error syndrome data and no additional calibration circuits, it is possible to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033055] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an in situ benchmarking method for fault-tolerant Clifford circuits using only existing error syndrome data.
motivation: Benchmarking quantum hardware and verifying encoded computations typically requires additional calibration circuits, which is resource-intensive.
method: They analyze error syndrome data from encoded Clifford circuits to estimate error rates and verify fault-tolerant operation without extra experiments.
result: The approach efficiently benchmarks quantum hardware and verifies encoded computations in situ.
conclusion: This enables practical assessment of fault-tolerant quantum circuits with minimal overhead.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A scalable framework for efficiently certifying fault-tolerant quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verifying encoded quantum systems is challenging, especially under realistic noise, and efficient certification of fault-tolerant computations is needed.
method: The authors develop a scalable accreditation tool that assesses computational accuracy of encoded quantum systems under general device noise.
result: The framework enables efficient certification of fault-tolerant computations and provides a practical verification tool for encoded quantum systems.
conclusion: Logical accreditation offers a promising approach for validating fault-tolerant quantum computations in realistic noisy settings.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A circuit-based framework characterizes finite-temperature quantum phases through a correlation-decay condition and identifies self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: Finite-temperature quantum phases and self-correcting quantum memories are central to understanding robust quantum information storage, but a unified circuit-based characterization has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a circuit-based framework and impose a correlation-decay condition to analyze thermal quantum phases and quantum memory behavior.
result: They show that self-correction arises universally in finite-temperature quantum memories within this framework, linking thermal phase characterization to memory robustness.
conclusion: The work provides a general circuit-based lens on finite-temperature quantum phases and establishes self-correction as a generic feature of quantum memories at finite temperature.

title: Chaotic Many-Body Quantum Dynamics, Spectral Correlations, And Energy Diffusion
authors: J. T. Chalker And Dominik Hahn
abstract:
Author(s): J. T. Chalker and Dominik Hahn

Researchers analyze a solvable many-body model to demonstrate how energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031076] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A solvable many-body model shows that energy diffusion quantitatively governs the spectral correlations characteristic of chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding how local transport properties such as energy diffusion connect to the universal spectral statistics of chaotic many-body quantum dynamics remains a central open question in quantum statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze an exactly solvable chaotic many-body model, computing spectral correlation functions (e.g., form factors and level statistics) and comparing them with the diffusive spreading of energy.
result: They establish a direct link whereby energy diffusion sets the scale and form of spectral correlations, demonstrating agreement between transport and spectral diagnostics in the chaotic regime.
conclusion: The work clarifies the relationship between hydrodynamics and quantum chaos, providing analytic evidence that diffusive transport underlies random-matrix-like spectral correlations in interacting quantum systems.

title: Coupling Free Electrons To A Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer
authors: Elias Pescoller, Santiago Beltrán-Romero, Sebastian Egginger, Nicolas Jungwirth, Martino Zanetti, Dominik Hornof, Michael S. Seifner, Iva Březinová, Philipp Haslinger, Thomas Juffmann, Johannes Kofler, Dennis Rätzel, And Philipp Schindler
abstract:
Author(s): Elias Pescoller, Santiago Beltrán-Romero, Sebastian Egginger, Nicolas Jungwirth, Martino Zanetti, Dominik Hornof, Michael S. Seifner, Iva Březinová, Philipp Haslinger, Thomas Juffmann, Johannes Kofler, Dennis Rätzel, and Philipp Schindler

Freely propagating electrons may serve as quantum probes that can become coherently correlated with other quantum systems, offering access to advanced metrological resources. We propose a setup that coherently couples free electrons in an electron microscope to a trapped-ion quantum processor, enabl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 150804] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum system that coherently couples free electrons in an electron microscope to a trapped-ion quantum processor for advanced metrology and quantum information tasks.
motivation: Free electrons can serve as quantum probes that become coherently correlated with other quantum systems, offering access to advanced metrological resources.
method: The authors propose an experimental setup that coherently couples freely propagating electrons in an electron microscope to a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: The proposed coupling enables coherent interactions between free electrons and trapped ions, potentially allowing for new quantum sensing and quantum information protocols.
conclusion: This hybrid platform could expand the capabilities of trapped-ion quantum processors by interfacing them with flying electron qubits, with applications in quantum metrology and networking.

title: Dissipative Acousto-Mechanical Parametric Interface Between High-Overtone Acoustics And Flexural Phonons
authors: Xun Ji, Huanying Sun, Longhao Wu, Qichun Liu, Yulong Liu, Mika A. Sillanpää, And Tiefu Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xun Ji, Huanying Sun, Longhao Wu, Qichun Liu, Yulong Liu, Mika A. Sillanpää, and Tiefu Li

A novel hybrid acousto-mechanical system demonstrates the highest-to-date coupling between a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator and low-frequency flexural modes in a suspended silicon nitride membrane.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 153602] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A new hybrid acousto-mechanical device achieves record-high coupling between a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator and low-frequency flexural phonons in a suspended silicon nitride membrane.
motivation: Coupling disparate mechanical modes is important for hybrid quantum systems, enabling coherent transfer and control of phononic excitations.
method: The authors fabricate a suspended silicon nitride membrane integrated with a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator and characterize the dissipative parametric interface between the high-frequency acoustic mode and low-frequency flexural modes.
result: They observe the highest-to-date coupling strength between these two mechanical degrees of freedom.
conclusion: This platform may enable new phonon-mediated transduction and quantum acoustodynamic experiments.

title: Analytic Formulas For Nonlocal Nonstabilizerness In Bipartite Systems Of Qutrits And Ququints
authors: Giorgio Busoni, John Gargalionis, Ewan N. V. Wallace, And Martin J. White
abstract:
Author(s): Giorgio Busoni, John Gargalionis, Ewan N. V. Wallace, and Martin J. White

We conjecture analytic expressions for the nonlocal magic of bipartite pure qudit states of prime local dimension. Our construction relies on the Schmidt-aligned state attaining the minimum over local unitaries, a hypothesis that we support with numerical evidence for pairs of qutrits and ququints. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042414] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper conjectures analytic formulas for the nonlocal magic (nonstabilizerness) of bipartite pure qudit states of prime local dimension, with numerical evidence for qutrit and ququint pairs.
motivation: Nonlocal magic is a resource for quantum computation, yet its quantification in bipartite systems remains largely unexplored beyond qubits; analytic formulas would enable systematic study.
method: The authors conjecture that the Schmidt-aligned state attains the minimum over local unitaries and support this hypothesis with numerical evidence for pairs of qutrits and ququints.
result: Analytic expressions are proposed for the nonlocal magic of bipartite pure qudit states, with numerical verification for qutrit and ququint systems.
conclusion: The conjectured formulas provide a basis for further investigation of nonlocal nonstabilizerness in higher-dimensional quantum systems.

title: Interplay Of Resources For Universal Continuous-variable Quantum Computing
authors: Varun Upreti And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Upreti and Ulysse Chabaud

Quantum resource theories identify the features of quantum computers that provide their computational advantage over classical systems. We investigate the resources driving the complexity of classical simulation in the standard model of continuous-variable quantum computing, and their interplay enab…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033379] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the interplay of quantum resources that enable universal continuous-variable quantum computing and determine its classical simulability.
motivation: Quantum resource theories aim to identify the features giving quantum computers an advantage, but the resources driving continuous-variable quantum computation and their interactions are not fully understood.
method: It analyzes classical simulation complexity in the standard continuous-variable model using quantum resource theories, examining how resources such as non-Gaussianity and magic combine.
result: It characterizes how different resources jointly enable universality and govern when classical simulation becomes inefficient.
conclusion: The work clarifies the resource requirements and interplay for universal continuous-variable quantum computing, informing resource-theoretic approaches to quantum advantage.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-analysis framework optimizes frequency- and amplitude-modulated gates for universal quantum control in superconducting circuits.
motivation: High-fidelity, fast quantum gates are essential for quantum computing, but conventional control methods face trade-offs between speed and accuracy in superconducting circuits.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis to optimize quantum gates using frequency and amplitude modulations.
result: The approach yields high-fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits, demonstrating improved control performance.
conclusion: Frequency- and amplitude-modulated gates provide a promising route to universal quantum control with enhanced fidelity and speed in superconducting platforms.

title: Dispersive Qubit Readout With Intrinsic Resonator Reset
authors: M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. Divincenzo, R. Barends, And P. A. Bushev
abstract:
Author(s): M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. DiVincenzo, R. Barends, and P. A. Bushev

Researchers experimentally demonstrate a new method for large-bandwidth dispersive readout, with built-in resonator reset, providing potential applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033042] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a large-bandwidth dispersive qubit readout method with intrinsic resonator reset for superconducting qubits.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity qubit readout is crucial for quantum error correction and scalable quantum computing, but conventional dispersive readout requires an external reset of the readout resonator.
method: The authors implement a dispersive readout scheme that incorporates an intrinsic resonator reset mechanism, likely using tailored drive pulses or a modified resonator design to enable large-bandwidth operation and automatic reset after measurement.
result: The method achieves fast, large-bandwidth readout with built-in reset, reducing dead time and potentially improving measurement fidelity compared to standard dispersive readout.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical improvement for superconducting qubit readout and could be integrated into quantum error correction protocols by streamlining the measurement cycle.

title: Ising On The Donut: Regimes Of Topological Quantum Error Correction From Statistical Mechanics
authors: Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, And Dominic J. Williamson
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, and Dominic J. Williamson

An exact mapping to the 2D Ising model produces closed-form logical failure rates for the toric code, offering an analytic tool kit for benchmarking topological codes beyond current computational limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043004] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: An exact mapping between the toric code and the 2D Ising model yields closed-form logical failure rates, enabling analytic benchmarking of topological quantum error correction beyond computational limits.
motivation: Topological quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but benchmarking its performance often requires costly numerical simulations. Analytic results are needed to understand failure regimes and guide code design.
method: The authors establish an exact mapping from the toric code to the 2D Ising model, allowing them to derive closed-form expressions for logical failure rates using statistical mechanics techniques.
result: They obtain analytic formulas for logical failure rates across different regimes, providing a toolkit to benchmark topological codes efficiently and extending analysis beyond current computational capabilities.
conclusion: This work bridges statistical mechanics and quantum error correction, offering a powerful analytic framework for studying topological codes and their thresholds, with potential applications in code optimization and fault-tolerance assessment.

title: Optical Depth Dictates Universal Bounds On Many-Body Decay In Atomic Ensembles
authors: Cosimo C. Rusconi, Eric Sierra, Wai-Keong Mok, Avishi Poddar, Simon B. Jäger, And Ana Asenjo-Garcia
abstract:
Author(s): Cosimo C. Rusconi, Eric Sierra, Wai-Keong Mok, Avishi Poddar, Simon B. Jäger, and Ana Asenjo-Garcia

Cooperative emission is well understood for idealized symmetric systems, but its fundamental limits in spatially extended, free-space ensembles remain an open question. Here, we derive a universal law for the scaling of the maximum photon emission rate with system size that unifies both ordered arra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 143603] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a universal law governing how the maximum photon emission rate of collectively decaying atomic ensembles scales with system size, showing optical depth sets a fundamental bound across ordered and disordered geometries.
motivation: Cooperative emission is well characterized for idealized symmetric systems, but the fundamental limits of collectively enhanced decay in spatially extended, free-space ensembles remained unclear.
method: The authors analyze many-body radiative decay of atomic ensembles via collective light-matter interactions, deriving scaling laws for the maximum emission rate as a function of system size and optical depth, and unifying ordered arrays with disordered ensembles.
result: They obtain a universal bound on the many-body decay rate dictated by the ensemble's optical depth, valid across both ordered and disordered configurations and settling the scaling with system size.
conclusion: Optical depth emerges as the key quantity that universally constrains cooperative emission in extended atomic ensembles, providing fundamental bounds for collective light-matter dynamics.

title: Magnetic-field-free Parity-protected Qubit Based On A Narrow Altermagnet Josephson Junction
authors: S. Vosoughi-Nia And M. P. Nowak
abstract:
Author(s): S. Vosoughi-nia and M. P. Nowak

Altermagnets provide a new route to engineer superconducting circuits without magnetic fields. We theoretically study the Andreev bound state (ABS) spectrum of a finite-width altermagnet-based Josephson junction and show how the [MATH]-wave altermagnetic symmetry and geometric confinement shape its low…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225408] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of Andreev bound states in a narrow altermagnet Josephson junction for realizing a magnetic-field-free parity-protected superconducting qubit.
motivation: Altermagnets offer a route to engineer superconducting circuits without external magnetic fields, potentially enabling parity-protected qubits with reduced sensitivity to magnetic noise.
method: The authors compute the Andreev bound state spectrum of a finite-width altermagnet-based Josephson junction, incorporating d-wave altermagnetic symmetry and geometric confinement effects.
result: The d-wave altermagnetic symmetry and finite-width confinement reshape the low-energy Andreev bound states, allowing parity protection without an applied magnetic field.
conclusion: The proposed altermagnet Josephson junction provides a promising platform for magnetic-field-free parity-protected qubits, advancing superconducting qubit design.

title: Breakdown Of The Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced By Auxiliary Circuit Modes
authors: Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, And Alexandre Blais
abstract:
Author(s): Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, and Alexandre Blais

Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041012] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Auxiliary circuit modes in Kerr-cat qubit architectures induce multiphoton resonances that degrade qubit coherence under strong driving.
motivation: Kerr-cat qubits are a promising bosonic platform for biased-noise error correction, but their coherence under strong parametric driving is limited by coupling to unintended circuit modes.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Kerr-cat qubit coupled to auxiliary superconducting circuit modes, identifying multiphoton resonances and computing their effect on the tunneling time and coherence.
result: Auxiliary modes give rise to multiphoton resonances that break down the exponential suppression of bit-flip errors, causing a decay in Kerr-cat coherence at strong drive amplitudes.
conclusion: The work identifies a practical coherence-limiting mechanism in driven Kerr-cat designs and highlights the need to engineer or detune auxiliary circuit modes for robust bosonic qubit operation.

title: Stability, Degeneracy, And Scalability Of A 600-Site Cavity Array Microscope
authors: Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, And Jonathan Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, and Jonathan Simon

A scalable cavity array microscope architecture is presented, featuring over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions, providing opportunities for quantum networking and sensing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041009] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a scalable cavity array microscope architecture with over 600 independent optical cavities that enables parallelized light-matter interactions for quantum networking and sensing.
motivation: Scaling up cavity-based light-matter interfaces is a key challenge for building larger quantum systems, and a massively parallel cavity platform could accelerate experiments in quantum networking and sensing.
method: The authors design and characterize a cavity array microscope consisting of more than 600 independent optical cavities, demonstrating stability and degeneracy control across the array for parallelized operation.
result: The architecture achieves stable, scalable operation of hundreds of independent cavities, providing a platform for simultaneous light-matter interactions across many sites.
conclusion: This cavity array microscope offers a practical route toward scalable cavity-QED platforms relevant to quantum networking and sensing applications.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States Under Density Decoherence
authors: Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
