Author(s): Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, and Ehud Altman

Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031074] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Density dephasing robustness of quantum information in fractional quantum Hall states depends qualitatively on the topological phase, with Moore-Read non-Abelian anyons resisting arbitrary dephasing while Laughlin states require a filling factor above a critical value.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information encoded in topological phases survives realistic decoherence is crucial for topological quantum computation and for assessing the practical value of non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors use statistical mechanics mappings to analyze the effect of density dephasing on the quantum information stored in fractional quantum Hall states, specifically Moore-Read and Laughlin states.
result: They find that quantum information in Moore-Read non-Abelian anyons is infinitely robust against arbitrary density dephasing, whereas Laughlin states exhibit infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
conclusion: The resilience of topological quantum information under density decoherence is strongly state-dependent, with non-Abelian anyons offering a qualitatively stronger protection than Abelian Laughlin states.

title: Quantum Birthmarks: Ergodicity Breaking Beyond Scarring
authors: Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, And Joonas Keski-Rahkonen
abstract:
Author(s): Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, and Joonas Keski-Rahkonen

Researchers develop a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, in defiance of classical expectations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031063] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework reveals that quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, demonstrating ergodicity breaking that goes beyond conventional quantum scarring.
motivation: To understand how isolated quantum systems can evade thermalization and preserve information about their initial conditions, challenging classical expectations.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework, likely analyzing eigenstate properties, dynamical correlations, or out-of-time-order correlators in isolated quantum systems.
result: They find that quantum systems exhibit a persistent memory of initial states and early dynamics, constituting ergodicity breaking beyond known scarring mechanisms.
conclusion: This work suggests new fundamental constraints on quantum thermalization and information retention, with implications for quantum chaos and non-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Generation Of Large Coherent-State Superpositions In Free-Space Optical Pulses
authors: Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, And Rosa Tualle-Brouri
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, and Rosa Tualle-Brouri

Researchers generate large-amplitude optical cat states in free space, establishing a vital building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031047] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Researchers experimentally generate large-amplitude coherent-state superpositions (cat states) in free-space optical pulses, providing a key resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Large cat states are essential for continuous-variable quantum computing and error correction, but their generation with high amplitude in free space has been challenging.
method: The authors use a scheme based on photon subtraction or homodyne conditioning to create cat states from squeezed vacuum states in free-space optical pulses.
result: They successfully generate large-amplitude cat states, demonstrating the feasibility of creating such non-classical states in free space.
conclusion: This work establishes a building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing with continuous variables and could enable scalable optical quantum technologies.

title: Hole Spin Resilient To Dipole-Induced Thermal Effects
authors: V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. de Franceschi, B. Martinez, And B. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. De Franceschi, B. Martinez, and B. Brun

A silicon hole spin unveils an electric origin of thermal frequency shifts and exhibits a magnetic-field sweet-spot immune to those, guiding the design of thermally robust semiconductor qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043005] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A silicon hole spin qubit reveals an electric origin of thermal frequency shifts and exhibits a magnetic-field sweet spot immune to these shifts, guiding the design of thermally robust semiconductor qubits.
motivation: Thermal fluctuations cause frequency shifts that degrade qubit coherence, and the microscopic origin of such shifts in hole spin qubits was unclear.
method: The authors perform temperature-dependent spectroscopy of a silicon hole spin qubit and analyze the dependence of its resonance frequency on electric and magnetic fields.
result: They identify an electric dipole-induced mechanism for thermal frequency shifts and find a magnetic-field sweet spot where the qubit frequency is insensitive to thermal effects.
conclusion: The results provide a strategy to engineer semiconductor spin qubits with enhanced thermal stability, relevant for scalable silicon quantum processors.

title: Complexity Of Quantum Trajectories
authors: Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, and Rosario Fazio

An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, while new results on autonomous chaos are discussed.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033049] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories detects integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime.
motivation: Detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems is challenging, especially beyond transient dynamics, necessitating robust probes.
method: The authors use an unsupervised, data-driven approach based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories to analyze open quantum systems and autonomous chaos.
result: The framework robustly detects integrability and ergodicity breaking beyond transient regimes and provides new insights into autonomous chaos.
conclusion: The intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories serves as a powerful probe for non-equilibrium dynamics and chaos in open quantum systems.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: A randomized compilation method enables exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems with minimal ancilla qubits for early fault-tolerant devices.
motivation: Accurate simulation of open quantum systems is resource-intensive and challenging for near-term fault-tolerant quantum computers.
method: The authors develop a random compilation technique that approximates dissipation using randomized quantum channels while requiring only a minimal number of ancilla qubits.
result: The method achieves exponentially accurate simulation of open-system dynamics and is shown to be viable for early fault-tolerant hardware.
conclusion: This work provides a resource-efficient route to simulating open quantum systems on near-term quantum devices.

title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance Quantization And Gate-Tunable Induced Superconducting Gap In Germanium
authors: Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, And Silvano de Franceschi
abstract:
Author(s): Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, and Silvano De Franceschi

Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033043] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Experiments on Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts reveal gate-tunable proximity-induced superconductivity and near-ideal Andreev-enhanced conductance quantization.
motivation: Hybrid semiconductor-superconductor systems are promising for quantum devices, but achieving controllable superconducting coupling in group-IV platforms like germanium remains challenging.
method: The authors fabricate and measure Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts with superconducting contacts, analyzing conductance versus gate voltage and temperature to extract the induced gap and quantization.
result: They observe a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal conductance quantization, in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: These results establish Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts as a viable platform for tunable superconducting hybrid quantum devices, potentially useful for Andreev qubits or Majorana-based architectures.

title: Holographic Duality Between Bulk Topological Order And Boundary Mixed-State Order
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order provides a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033041] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a holographic duality between bulk topological order and boundary mixed-state order, offering a framework for strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
motivation: Open quantum systems and mixed-state phases are difficult to characterize, and mapping them to higher-dimensional topological order may provide new theoretical tools.
method: The authors use holographic duality to relate a bulk topological order to a boundary mixed-state order, likely via a path-integral or tensor-network mapping.
result: They show that bulk topological order corresponds to boundary mixed-state order, capturing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
conclusion: This duality gives a new perspective on mixed-state quantum phases and topological order in open quantum systems.

title: Microwave Spectroscopy Of Few-Carrier States In Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, And Klaus Ensslin
abstract:
Author(s): Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, and Klaus Ensslin

Circuit quantum electrodynamics enables high-resolution spectroscopy of Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, paving the way for advanced qubit control and readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033037] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: Circuit-QED microwave spectroscopy resolves Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, enabling high-resolution readout of few-carrier states.
motivation: Bilayer graphene quantum dots are promising hosts for spin and valley qubits, but their few-carrier excited states and blocking mechanisms require sensitive spectroscopic tools.
method: The authors couple bilayer graphene quantum dots to a microwave resonator and perform circuit-QED spectroscopy of charge transitions and spin/valley blockade in the few-electron regime.
result: They observe high-resolution microwave signatures of Pauli spin blockade and valley blockade, revealing the energy structure and selection rules of few-carrier states.
conclusion: The work demonstrates circuit-QED spectroscopy as a route to advanced control and readout of graphene-based qubit platforms.

title: Scrambling Without Chaos In Random Free-fermionic Systems
authors: Ali Mollabashi And Mohammad-Javad Vasli
abstract:
Author(s): Ali Mollabashi and Mohammad-Javad Vasli

We study the role of randomness in the scrambling of quantum information within integrable free-fermionic systems. Considering quadratic Hamiltonians with varying degrees of randomness, we analyze entanglement-based measures to characterize the scrambling structure. We show that the memory effect in…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044110] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum information scrambling in random integrable free-fermionic systems using entanglement-based measures, showing that scrambling can arise from randomness even without chaos.
motivation: To clarify whether randomness alone can drive scrambling in integrable systems, separating scrambling from chaotic dynamics.
method: They consider quadratic Hamiltonians with varying degrees of randomness and quantify scrambling via entanglement-based measures.
result: They characterize the scrambling structure and demonstrate a memory effect, indicating scrambling without chaos.
conclusion: Randomness in free-fermionic integrable systems can generate scrambling, providing insight into information dynamics beyond chaotic models.

title: Fock-space Fragmentation In Quenches Of Disordered Interacting Fermions
authors: Ishita Modak, Rajesh Narayanan, Ferdinand Evers, And Soumya Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Ishita Modak, Rajesh Narayanan, Ferdinand Evers, and Soumya Bera

Fock-space fragmentation, as it is currently investigated, primarily originates from specific kinematic constraints or emergent conservation laws in many-body systems with translation invariance. It leads to nonergodic dynamics and possible breakdown of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Here…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043030] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Fock-space fragmentation in quenches of disordered interacting fermions, showing that disorder-induced fragmentation leads to nonergodic dynamics and breakdown of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
motivation: Fock-space fragmentation has mostly been studied in translation-invariant systems, but this work extends it to disordered systems and demonstrates its impact on thermalization and quantum dynamics.

title: Readout Failures In Superconducting Qubits Due To Two-level System Defects In Tunnel Junctions
authors: Jürgen Lisenfeld, Alexander K. Händel, Alexander Bilmes, And Alexey V. Ustinov
abstract:
Author(s): Jürgen Lisenfeld, Alexander K. Händel, Alexander Bilmes, and Alexey V. Ustinov

Material defects give rise to parasitic two-level systems (TLS) that present a major source of decoherence in superconducting qubits. Here, we study a strongly coupled TLS that resides in the tunnel barrier of transmon qubit. We use multiphoton spectroscopy and TLS strain tuning to explore the rich …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033382] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: A strongly coupled two-level system (TLS) defect in the tunnel barrier of a transmon qubit is identified as a cause of readout failures, characterized via multiphoton spectroscopy and strain tuning.
motivation: Material defects such as TLS are major sources of decoherence in superconducting qubits, and their specific impact on qubit readout remains to be understood.
method: The authors use multiphoton spectroscopy and TLS strain tuning to probe a strongly coupled TLS residing in the tunnel barrier of a transmon qubit.
result: The measurements reveal rich behavior of the TLS and demonstrate its role in inducing readout failures, likely through strong coupling to the qubit.
conclusion: Mitigating TLS defects in tunnel junctions is important for improving readout fidelity and overall superconducting qubit performance.

title: Active Interference Suppression In Frequency-division-multiplexed Quantum Gates Via Off-resonant Microwave Tones
authors: Haruki Mitarai, Yukihiro Tadokoro, And Hiroya Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Haruki Mitarai, Yukihiro Tadokoro, and Hiroya Tanaka

The increasing number of control lines connecting quantum processors to external electronics constitutes a major bottleneck in the realization of large-scale quantum computers. Frequency-division multiplexing is expected to enable control of multiple qubits through a single microwave cable; however,…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033376] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using off-resonant microwave tones to actively suppress interference in frequency-division-multiplexed quantum gates, aiming to reduce control-line overhead in scalable quantum processors.
motivation: The growing number of control lines connecting quantum processors to external electronics is a major bottleneck for large-scale quantum computers. Frequency-division multiplexing can control multiple qubits through a single cable, but inter-channel interference degrades gate performance.
method: The authors introduce off-resonant microwave tones to actively cancel unwanted interference between frequency-multiplexed control signals, likely applied to superconducting qubit gates in a circuit QED architecture.
result: The technique suppresses interference in multiplexed quantum gates, improving gate fidelity and enabling reliable simultaneous control of multiple qubits via a shared microwave line.
conclusion: Active interference suppression with off-resonant tones offers a practical route to scalable qubit control with fewer control lines, relevant to superconducting quantum processor engineering.

title: Disambiguating Pauli Noise In Quantum Computers
authors: Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, And Alireza Seif
abstract:
Author(s): Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, and Alireza Seif

The unavoidable “gauge” ambiguity in learning a quantum computer’s noise does not hinder error mitigation, and this remaining degree of freedom can even be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033045] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The gauge ambiguity in learning Pauli noise on quantum computers does not prevent error mitigation and can be optimized to greatly improve mitigation efficiency.
motivation: Learning a quantum computer's noise is essential for error mitigation, but gauge ambiguities in Pauli noise characterization make the learned model non-unique.
method: The authors analyze the gauge degrees of freedom in Pauli noise learning and optimize them specifically for error mitigation tasks.
result: They show that the gauge ambiguity does not hinder error mitigation and that optimizing the remaining gauge can dramatically increase mitigation efficiency.
conclusion: Gauge ambiguity should be viewed as an opportunity rather than an obstacle, enabling more efficient error mitigation on near-term quantum devices.

title: Defect-Free Arrays At The Thousand-Atom Scale In A 4-k Cryogenic Environment
authors: Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, And Bruno Ximenez
abstract:
Author(s): Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, and Bruno Ximenez

Cryogenic operation and high optical access combine to enable creation of perfect neutral-atom arrays with single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds, a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033032] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates defect-free neutral-atom arrays containing thousands of atoms in a 4 K cryogenic environment, with single-atom trapping lifetimes of thousands of seconds, advancing large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.
motivation: Large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing requires scalable, defect-free atom arrays with long coherence and trapping times, which are limited by vacuum quality, laser cooling, and environmental disturbances.
method: The authors combine cryogenic operation at 4 K with high optical access to create and maintain defect-free arrays of thousands of single atoms, likely using optical tweezers and improved vacuum conditions.
result: They achieve perfect filling of thousand-atom-scale arrays and single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds, a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum information processing.
conclusion: Cryogenic neutral-atom arrays provide a promising platform for scalable quantum computing, enabling long-lived, defect-free atom arrays with high optical access.

title: Heralded Generation Of A Three-Mode Noon State
authors: Sukhjit P. Singh, Elnaz Bazzazi, Diego N. Bernal-García, Simon J. U. White, Hassan Jamal Latief, Alison Goldingay, Sven Rogge, Sergei Slussarenko, Farzad Ghafari, Emanuele Polino, And Nora Tischler
abstract:
Author(s): Sukhjit P. Singh, Elnaz Bazzazi, Diego N. Bernal-García, Simon J. U. White, Hassan Jamal Latief, Alison Goldingay, Sven Rogge, Sergei Slussarenko, Farzad Ghafari, Emanuele Polino, and Nora Tischler

Entangled states of photons form the foundation of quantum communication, computation, and metrology. Yet their generation remains fundamentally constrained: in the absence of intrinsic photon-photon interactions, the generation of such states is inherently probabilistic rather than deterministic. T…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 150802] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a heralded scheme for generating a three-mode NOON state, an entangled multipartite photonic state, overcoming the intrinsic probabilistic nature of linear-optics photon entanglement.
motivation: Entangled photonic states underpin quantum communication, computation, and metrology, but lack of intrinsic photon-photon interactions makes their generation inherently probabilistic, limiting practical scalability and reliability.
method: A heralded generation protocol is implemented (using linear-optics/measurement-based techniques) to produce a three-mode NOON state, with the success event flagged by a heralding detection signal.
result: The authors demonstrate heralded generation of the three-mode NOON state, verifying its multipartite entangled character through the heralding signature and state characterization.
conclusion: Heralded generation of multipartite NOON states provides a practical resource for multipartite quantum communication and metrology, advancing photonic entanglement distribution.

title: Analysis Of Self-thermalization Dynamics In The Bose-Hubbard Model By Using The Pseudoclassical Approach
authors: Andrey R. Kolovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Andrey R. Kolovsky

We analyze the self-thermalization dynamics of the [MATH]-site Bose-Hubbard model in ring geometry using the single-particle density matrix calculated via the pseudoclassical approach. We show that a weak interparticle interaction, which has a negligible effect on the thermal state given by the Bose-Ei…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042204] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes self-thermalization dynamics in the Bose-Hubbard model using a pseudoclassical approach to compute the single-particle density matrix.
motivation: Understanding how isolated quantum many-body systems reach thermal equilibrium is central to quantum statistical mechanics and the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
method: The author studies an M-site Bose-Hubbard ring with weak interparticle interactions by evolving an ensemble of classical trajectories in a pseudoclassical phase-space approach and extracting the single-particle density matrix.
result: Weak interactions that have negligible effect on the equilibrium Bose-Einstein thermal state can nonetheless drive self-thermalization of the single-particle density matrix in the Bose-Hubbard dynamics.
conclusion: The pseudoclassical method captures the self-thermalization dynamics and suggests that thermalization can occur even when interaction effects on equilibrium properties are small.

title: Universal Squeezing-enhanced Readout Approach For Bosonic Qubits
authors: Yuan Qiu, Yiming Yu, Ye-Hong Chen, And Yan-Xia
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan Qiu, Yiming Yu, Ye-Hong Chen, and Yan-Xia

In this article, we propose a squeezing-enhanced protocol for the efficient readout of bosonic qubits, whose encoding states can be first mapped onto a multilevel atom and then read out via dispersive coupling. We demonstrate that by simultaneously applying intracavity and external squeezing for the…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033365] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: A squeezing-enhanced readout protocol is proposed for bosonic qubits by mapping their encoded states onto a multilevel atom read out via dispersive coupling in circuit QED.
motivation: High-fidelity, fast readout of bosonic qubits (e.g., cat/GKP codes) is a bottleneck for superconducting quantum computing, and squeezing offers a route to boost the signal-to-noise ratio of dispersive measurement.
method: The bosonic logical states are first mapped onto a multilevel atom, and both intracavity and external squeezing are simultaneously applied to enhance the dispersive readout of the encoded qubit.
result: The authors show that combining intracavity and external squeezing improves the readout fidelity/efficiency relative to conventional dispersive readout for bosonic qubits.
conclusion: The scheme provides a universal, platform-compatible approach to squeezing-enhanced readout that could be extended to a range of bosonic encoding architectures.

title: Tunable Dephasing-induced non-Hermitian Jumps In Quasiperiodic Lattices
authors: Ping Chen, Shan-Zhong Li, And Zhi Li
abstract:
Author(s): Ping Chen, Shan-Zhong Li, and Zhi Li

We investigated the dynamical properties of one-dimensional quasiperiodic lattices under dephasing modulation. The results show that by manipulating the dephasing period, the corresponding dynamics will shift from ballistic transport to non-Hermitian jumps. Non-Hermitian jumps in quasiperiodic latti…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043302] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how dephasing modulation in a one-dimensional quasiperiodic lattice induces a transition from ballistic transport to non-Hermitian jumps.
motivation: To understand the interplay between dephasing and non-Hermitian dynamics in quasiperiodic systems, which is relevant to open quantum systems and transport phenomena.
method: The authors study the dynamics of a 1D quasiperiodic lattice under a dephasing modulation with a tunable period, likely using a Lindblad master equation or non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approach.
result: By tuning the dephasing period, the dynamics shift from ballistic transport to non-Hermitian jumps, revealing a controllable transition between transport regimes.
conclusion: Dephasing can be used to control transport regimes and induce non-Hermitian effects in quasiperiodic lattices, offering insights into open quantum system dynamics.

title: Experimentally Accessible Measurement Of Irreversibility In Stochastic Systems By Categorizing Single-Molecule Displacements
authors: Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, And Stefano Bo
abstract:
Author(s): Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, and Stefano Bo

A model-free method that infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings offers a versatile and accessible tool to characterize the nonequilibrium behavior of small, time-dependent, continuous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031052] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: A model-free method categorizes single-molecule displacements to experimentally measure irreversibility in stochastic nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: Characterizing nonequilibrium behavior and irreversibility in small, time-dependent continuous systems is challenging, often requiring detailed models that may not be available.
method: The authors develop a model-free approach that infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings by categorizing displacements, avoiding the need for a full dynamical model.
result: The method provides a versatile and accessible tool to quantify nonequilibrium behavior, likely demonstrated on experimental single-molecule data, yielding estimates of irreversibility.
conclusion: This technique offers a broadly applicable way to measure irreversibility in stochastic systems without detailed modeling, facilitating experimental studies of nonequilibrium dynamics.

title: Ultra-Slow Orbital And Spin Dynamics In An Electrically Tunable Quantum Dot Molecule
authors: Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, And Jonathan Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, and Jonathan Finley

A new study demonstrates the optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, while keeping the tunability of its parameter, which can become an important building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033056] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: This study demonstrates optical charging of spins in an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule, revealing ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics with potential for photonic cluster state generation.
motivation: Quantum dot molecules are promising platforms for spin-based quantum technologies, but understanding and controlling their charge and spin dynamics under electrical tunability is essential for applications like photonic cluster state generation.
method: The authors use optical spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to investigate charging dynamics and spin/orbital relaxation in a gate-tunable quantum dot molecule.
result: They observe ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics, enabling optical charging while maintaining electrical tunability of the molecular parameters.
conclusion: These results establish quantum dot molecules as a versatile building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation and advanced quantum photonic devices.

title: Moments Of Quantum Channel Ensembles
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, and M. Cerezo

A general framework for the study of statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles is introduced, providing new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033050] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a general framework for statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles, offering new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Understanding noise and ensemble statistics in quantum channels is crucial for analyzing and optimizing near-term quantum algorithms and circuits.
method: The authors develop a framework to compute and analyze statistical moments of ensembles of quantum channels, likely using tools from random matrix theory or channel representation theory.
result: The framework provides new insights into the behavior of noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms, potentially enabling better noise characterization and algorithm design.
conclusion: The work advances quantum channel theory with practical implications for noisy intermediate-scale quantum computing and variational quantum algorithms.

title: Observation Of The Transition From Reversible To Irreversible Decoherence Of Mesoscopic Quantum Superpositions
authors: Ri-Hua Zheng, Jia-Hao Lü, Fan Wu, Yan Xia, Li-Hua Lin, Zhen-Biao Yang, And Shi-Biao Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Ri-Hua Zheng, Jia-Hao Lü, Fan Wu, Yan Xia, Li-Hua Lin, Zhen-Biao Yang, and Shi-Biao Zheng

The decoherence of superpositions of classically distinguishable states (cat states) is crucial for understanding quantum-to-classical transitions and quantum measurements. So far, irreversible decoherence processes of mesoscopic cat states have been demonstrated in several experiments. We here repo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 150201] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally observes the transition from reversible to irreversible decoherence of mesoscopic cat states, shedding light on the quantum-to-classical transition.
motivation: Understanding how quantum superpositions of classically distinguishable states lose coherence is central to quantum measurement and the emergence of classicality, yet the crossover between reversible and irreversible decoherence had not been directly observed.
method: The authors prepare mesoscopic cat states in a controllable quantum system and monitor their decoherence dynamics as the environment interaction is tuned, likely using tomographic or interference techniques.
result: They observe a clear transition from reversible (coherent) to irreversible (incoherent) decoherence as the effective environment size or coupling increases, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The experiment provides direct evidence for the reversible-to-irreversible decoherence crossover in mesoscopic superpositions, advancing foundational understanding of open quantum systems and decoherence control.

title: Multiband Dispersion And Warped Vortices Of Strongly Interacting Photons
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, And Ofer Firstenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, and Ofer Firstenberg

A new study develops an analytical framework to understand and control nonlinear multiphoton processes in strongly interacting Rydberg media.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: An analytical framework is developed to understand and control nonlinear multiphoton processes in strongly interacting Rydberg media, revealing multiband dispersion and warped vortices.
motivation: Strongly interacting Rydberg media provide a promising platform for photon-photon interactions, but controlling nonlinear multiphoton dynamics remains a theoretical and experimental challenge.
method: The authors construct an analytical model for nonlinear multiphoton propagation in Rydberg media, deriving effective equations that capture multiband dispersion and vortex formation.
result: The framework predicts multiband dispersion relations and warped vortex structures for strongly interacting photons, offering new ways to manipulate nonlinear optical responses.
conclusion: This work advances the understanding and control of strongly interacting photons in Rydberg media, with potential applications in quantum nonlinear optics and hybrid light-matter systems.

title: Finite-size Clocks In Quantum Field Theory And The Twin Paradox
authors: Matheus H. Zambianco And T. Rick Perche
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus H. Zambianco and T. Rick Perche

Vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory impose fundamental limitations on our ability to measure time at arbitrarily short scales. To investigate the impact of universal quantum field theory effects on observer-dependent time measurements, we introduce a clock model based on the vacuum decay pro…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a finite-size clock model in quantum field theory to study fundamental limitations on time measurement from vacuum fluctuations and their implications for the twin paradox.
motivation: Vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory are expected to limit time measurement at short scales, motivating an investigation of observer-dependent time and relativistic effects like the twin paradox.
method: The authors develop a clock model based on the vacuum decay process of a finite-size quantum system coupled to a quantum field, analyzing its timekeeping accuracy in different reference frames.
result: They find that vacuum fluctuations impose fundamental bounds on clock precision and that these effects modify the twin paradox scenario for quantum clocks.
conclusion: Universal quantum field theory effects must be accounted for in any fundamental description of time measurement and relativistic clock synchronization.

title: Temperature-enhanced Quantum Sensing For The Cutoff Frequency Of Ohmic-family Environments
authors: Ji-Bing Yuan, Ya-Ju Song, Shi-Qing Tang, Xin-Wen Wang, And Le-Man Kuang
abstract:
Author(s): Ji-Bing Yuan, Ya-Ju Song, Shi-Qing Tang, Xin-Wen Wang, and Le-Man Kuang

The authors examine the performance of a single dephasing qubit probing the cutoff frequency of Ohmic-family environments across varying temperatures and coupling strengths. They find that elevated temperatures accelerate decoherence to shorten the optimal measurement time, demonstrating that thermal noise can serve as a resource to improve sensing precision by nearly two orders of magnitude compared to zero-temperature conditions for certain weakly coupled environments.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042407] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: A single dephasing qubit can probe the cutoff frequency of Ohmic-family environments, and elevated temperatures can enhance sensing precision by shortening the optimal measurement time.
motivation: To improve quantum sensing of environmental spectral properties, particularly the cutoff frequency, by exploiting thermal noise rather than treating it solely as a detrimental effect.
method: The authors model a dephasing qubit coupled to Ohmic-family environments and analyze decoherence dynamics and sensing precision across varying temperatures and coupling strengths.
result: Higher temperatures accelerate decoherence, which reduces the optimal measurement time and improves sensing precision by up to two orders of magnitude compared to zero-temperature conditions for certain weakly coupled environments.
conclusion: Thermal noise can serve as a resource for quantum sensing of cutoff frequency, offering a counterintuitive enhancement in precision.

title: Hierarchical Approach To Quantum Many-body Systems In non-Markovian Environments
authors: Kai Müller, Kimmo Luoma, And Christian Schäfer
abstract:
Author(s): Kai Müller, Kimmo Luoma, and Christian Schäfer

Quantum many-body systems in cavities combine the rich physics of condensed matter systems or quantum chemistry with strong coupling to the surrounding electromagnetic field. In these systems, large Hilbert spaces, many-body interactions, and strong system-environment coupling are all fundamental, p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204301] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a hierarchical approach for simulating quantum many-body systems in cavities coupled to non-Markovian environments.
motivation: Quantum many-body systems in cavities combine large Hilbert spaces, many-body interactions, and strong system-environment coupling, making accurate theoretical treatment challenging.
method: The authors employ a hierarchical expansion or equations-of-motion framework to capture non-Markovian dynamics for many-body cavity systems.
result: The approach is expected to enable efficient and accurate simulations of open quantum many-body dynamics beyond Markovian approximations.
conclusion: This provides a practical tool for studying cavity-based many-body physics in realistic non-Markovian environments.

title: Theory Of Out-of-Time-Ordered Transport
authors: Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, And Luca V. Delacrétaz
abstract:
Author(s): Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, and Luca V. Delacrétaz

Researchers establish an effective field theory capturing late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041010] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an effective field theory for late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) that extracts otherwise hidden transport parameters of quantum many-body systems.
motivation: OTOCs are powerful diagnostics of quantum chaos and information scrambling, but their late-time behavior and connection to hydrodynamic transport coefficients have remained poorly understood.
method: The authors construct an effective field theory description of late-time OTOC dynamics, deriving how universal transport parameters emerge from the structure of the correlators.
result: The framework reveals hidden transport coefficients encoded in late-time OTOC behavior, providing a systematic link between chaos diagnostics and hydrodynamics.
conclusion: OTOCs serve as a universal probe of transport in quantum many-body systems, opening a route to characterize transport from chaos-based observables.

title: Universal Sample Complexity Bounds In Quantum Learning Theory Via Fisher Information Matrix
authors: Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, and Liang Jiang

A framework shows that the sample complexity of general quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033063] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes universal sample-complexity bounds for general quantum learning problems, showing they are governed by the inverse quantum Fisher information matrix.
motivation: Sample complexity is a central resource in quantum learning and estimation, but a general information-theoretic characterization of how many samples are needed across arbitrary quantum learning tasks was lacking.
method: The authors develop a framework relating the sample complexity of general quantum learning protocols to the inverse Fisher information matrix, deriving universal bounds.
result: They prove universal sample-complexity bounds governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix, providing both lower and upper limits for general quantum learning tasks.
conclusion: Fisher information emerges as the fundamental quantity controlling the sample efficiency of quantum learning, unifying disparate learning and estimation settings.

title: Few-Electron Spin Qubits In Quantum Dots Probed Through Nuclear Spin Magnetism
authors: Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Armando Rastelli, And Evgeny A. Chekhovich
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, and Evgeny A. Chekhovich

A new strategy for detecting the charging energies of quantum dots exploits the response of nuclear spins.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033028] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: A new method detects charging energies of quantum dots by exploiting the response of nuclear spins.
motivation: Charging energies are crucial parameters for few-electron spin qubits in quantum dots, but probing them directly remains challenging.
method: The authors use nuclear spin magnetism as a probe to measure charging energies in quantum dot devices.
result: They demonstrate a strategy that reveals charging energies through the nuclear spin response.
conclusion: This technique offers a new characterization tool for few-electron spin qubits in quantum dots.

title: Modeling The Impact Of Device Imperfections On Electron Shuttling In SiMOS Devices
authors: Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices are presented, identifying operating regimes resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033054] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional simulations reveal how device imperfections and charge defects affect electron shuttling in SiMOS devices, identifying operating regimes that remain robust.
motivation: Electron shuttling is crucial for scaling silicon spin qubits, but real device imperfections can disrupt transport and reduce fidelity.
method: The authors perform three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS device geometries, introducing common imperfections and charge defects.
result: They map out operating regimes that are resilient to these imperfections, offering guidelines for robust device design.
conclusion: The study supports the development of reliable SiMOS-based architectures for quantum computing by highlighting shuttling conditions tolerant to defects.

title: General Quantum Circuit Framework For Extended Wigner’s Friend Scenarios: Logically And Causally Consistent Reasoning Without Absolute Measurement Events
authors: V. Vilasini And Mischa P. Woods
abstract:
Author(s): V. Vilasini and Mischa P. Woods

Researchers develop a quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner’s friend scenarios, resolving logical paradoxes by tracking Heisenberg cuts.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031062] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: A general quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner's friend scenarios that resolves logical paradoxes by tracking Heisenberg cuts without assuming absolute measurement events.
motivation: Extended Wigner's friend paradoxes challenge the consistency of quantum theory and the notion of observer-independent measurement events, motivating a rigorous circuit-based treatment of nested measurements and causality.
method: The authors develop a general quantum circuit formalism for extended Wigner's friend scenarios, explicitly tracking Heisenberg cuts between observers and avoiding any assumption of absolute measurement events.
result: The framework provides logically and causally consistent reasoning across nested Wigner's friend experiments, clarifying how paradoxes arise from inconsistent treatment of measurement events and cuts.
conclusion: This work offers a consistent foundation for analyzing extended Wigner's friend scenarios and their implications for quantum causality, measurement, and no-go theorems.

title: Direct Characterization Of Classical Dephasing Noise For A Qubit
authors: Yuan-De Jin, Zheng-Fei Ye, And Wen-Long Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-De Jin, Zheng-Fei Ye, and Wen-Long Ma

The authors propose a simple method to directly characterize classical stochastic noise causing qubit dephasing through repetitive Ramsey interferometry measurements (RIMs) on the qubit. They demonstrate that each RIM with a short evolution time and suitably chosen control pulses directly samples the noise field, and the
[Phys. Rev. A 114, L040401] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a direct method to characterize classical stochastic dephasing noise on a qubit using repetitive Ramsey interferometry measurements (RIMs), showing that outcome correlations map onto noise correlation functions.
motivation: Understanding and characterizing dephasing noise is essential for improving qubit coherence and control, yet existing noise spectroscopy methods typically require assumptions about the noise spectrum or are indirect.
method: Each Ramsey interferometry measurement with a short evolution time and suitably chosen control pulses directly samples the classical noise field, and the correlations of the RIM outcomes are shown to be proportional to the correlation functions of the noise process.
result: The outcome correlations of the RIM protocol directly yield the noise correlation functions, enabling characterization of classical stochastic dephasing noise without spectral reconstruction.
conclusion: The proposed repetitive Ramsey interferometry scheme offers a simple, direct route to access classical noise correlations affecting qubits, with potential utility for noise-aware quantum control and decoherence mitigation.

title: Charge Dynamics At Nitrogen Impurities And Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond
authors: Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma, J. K. Nangoi, Mark E. Turiansky, And Chris G. van de Walle
abstract:
Author(s): Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma, J. K. Nangoi, Mark E. Turiansky, and Chris G. Van de Walle

The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond is the prototype quantum defect that enables a variety of diamond-based quantum technologies. However, charge-state instability and spectral diffusion, often induced by substitutional nitrogen impurities ([MATH]), remain key challenges…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194104] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of charge-state dynamics at substitutional nitrogen impurities and NV centers in diamond, clarifying mechanisms of charge instability and spectral diffusion that limit NV-based quantum technologies.
motivation: The NV center is a leading quantum defect platform, but charge-state instability and spectral diffusion induced by nearby substitutional nitrogen (P1) impurities degrade its performance in quantum sensing and networking applications.
method: Atomistic first-principles (DFT) calculations of charge transition levels, defect formation energies, and charge capture/emission dynamics for nitrogen impurities and NV centers in diamond, including impurity-NV interaction channels.
result: The calculations identify the electronic processes by which P1 centers exchange charge with NV centers, quantifying transition levels and barriers that drive charge-state fluctuations and spectral diffusion.
conclusion: Understanding these charge dynamics provides microscopic guidance for mitigating NV charge instability, informing materials engineering and device design for diamond quantum technologies.

title: Energy-Efficient Control Of Interacting Microscopic Systems: When Longer Paths Save Energy
authors: Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, And Clemens Bechinger
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, and Clemens Bechinger

Harnessing hydrodynamic interactions offers a route to control multiparticle systems efficiently, enabling substantial reductions in the energetic cost of microscopic transport.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031079] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Exploiting hydrodynamic interactions between microscopically interacting particles allows energetically cheaper transport along deliberately longer paths.
motivation: Microscopic transport of interacting particles typically incurs large energetic costs, and finding strategies to reduce dissipation is central to small-scale thermodynamics and control.
method: The authors analyze the energetics of controlling multiple hydrodynamically coupled microscopic particles, comparing direct trajectories with longer detours that harness the interaction to lower total energy expenditure.
result: Counterintuitively, longer transport paths can reduce the overall energetic cost when hydrodynamic coupling is exploited, yielding substantial energy savings compared with naive direct transport.
conclusion: Interaction-aware (rather than per-particle) control strategies provide a route to energy-efficient manipulation of microscopic systems, with implications for optimal control and dissipation bounds in small stochastic systems.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Motzkin Spin Chains With Rydberg Atoms
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Hatem Barghathi, Adrian Del Maestro, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Hatem Barghathi, Adrian Del Maestro, and Rick Mukherjee

The Motzkin spin chain is a well-known mathematical model with connections to symmetry-protected topological phases, such as the Haldane phase, as well as to concepts in the AdS/CFT correspondence. They exhibit highly entangled ground states that violate the area law and are exceptionally difficult …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 150601] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes a Rydberg-atom platform for quantum-simulating Motzkin spin chains, whose highly entangled ground states violate the area law.
motivation: Motzkin spin chains are mathematically important models connecting to symmetry-protected topological phases and AdS/CFT, but their area-law-violating ground states are exceptionally hard to simulate classically.
method: The authors design a Rydberg-atom array implementation of the Motzkin spin chain Hamiltonian and analyze its ground-state properties and simulability using the platform's native interactions.
result: A concrete Rydberg-based scheme is presented that can access the highly entangled Motzkin ground states, with characterization of how well the Rydberg platform captures the target physics.
conclusion: Rydberg arrays offer a viable route to quantum-simulate Motzkin spin chains and probe their area-law-violating entanglement, though the work leans toward condensed-matter simulation rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Phase-Space Bosonic Dynamics Via Automatic Differentiation
authors: Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, And Cristiano Ciuti
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, and Cristiano Ciuti

Researchers introduce a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method combining analytical techniques with automatic differentiation to reveal the critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031077] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method with automatic differentiation is developed to simulate the critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.
motivation: Large open quantum bosonic lattices are challenging to simulate due to high dimensionality and non-equilibrium critical phenomena, requiring scalable and accurate computational methods.
method: The authors combine a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space ansatz with automatic differentiation to optimize and evolve the dynamics of open bosonic lattice master equations.
result: The method captures critical dynamics in large open bosonic lattices, enabling scalable simulations that would be intractable with exact or conventional approaches.
conclusion: This approach provides a versatile computational tool for studying non-equilibrium critical phenomena in open bosonic many-body systems.

title: Interaction-Assisted Topological Pumping In Few- And Many-Atom Rydberg Arrays
authors: Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, And Bryce Gadway
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, and Bryce Gadway

Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays are found to be able to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031075] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays bind atoms into correlated pairs and clusters that exhibit efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.
motivation: Topological pumping is a robust way to transport quantum states, and understanding how interactions modify it could enable new quantum simulation and state-transfer protocols in neutral-atom platforms.
method: The authors use few- and many-atom Rydberg arrays with strong dipolar (Van der Waals) interactions and drive a synthetic dimension, combining experiment and theory to study interaction-assisted Thouless pumping.
result: Interactions are found to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that are transported with high efficiency, with interaction strength tuning the pumping behavior and renormalizing the topological response.
conclusion: Interaction-assisted topological pumping in Rydberg arrays offers a controlled route to correlated transport in synthetic dimensions, relevant to neutral-atom quantum simulation and hardware for state transfer.

title: Second-order Sideband Generation And Slow-fast Light Control In Coupled Exciton-optomechanical Cavities Via A Parametric Amplifier
authors: Abdul Wahab And Fahhad H. Alharbi
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Wahab and Fahhad H. Alharbi

We theoretically investigate second-order sideband generation (SSG) and tunable slow-fast light propagation via strong nonlinear coupling among photons, phonons, and excitons in two coupled microcavities, consisting of an active (gain) cavity and a passive (loss) cavity that contains a quantum well …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043706] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies second-order sideband generation and tunable slow-fast light propagation in coupled exciton-optomechanical cavities containing a quantum well and a parametric amplifier.
motivation: To explore strong nonlinear coupling among photons, phonons, and excitons in active-passive microcavities for controlling nonlinear optical effects such as sideband generation and light propagation.
method: The authors solve coupled quantum Langevin equations for two coupled microcavities (one gain, one loss) with a quantum well and a parametric amplifier to analyze the system's nonlinear response.
result: They demonstrate enhanced second-order sideband generation and tunable switching between slow and fast light by adjusting system parameters such as cavity detuning and parametric gain.
conclusion: The proposed scheme could be useful for optical buffers, switches, and nonlinear photonic devices, but its relevance to quantum information processing is limited.

title: Exponential Entanglement Advantage In Sensing Correlated Noise
authors: Yu-Xin Wang (王语馨), Jacob Bringewatt, Alireza Seif, Anthony J. Brady, Changhun Oh, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Xin Wang (王语馨), Jacob Bringewatt, Alireza Seif, Anthony J. Brady, Changhun Oh, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

Correlated noise naturally arises in quantum systems due to, e.g., phase and amplitude fluctuations in global control or long-range correlations generated by a many-body sensing target near criticality. In this Letter, we propose a new form of exponential quantum advantage in the context of sensing …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 150803] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The authors show that entangled sensors can achieve an exponential advantage over separable sensors when estimating parameters in the presence of spatially correlated noise.
motivation: Correlated noise is ubiquitous in practical quantum sensing setups, arising from global control fluctuations or many-body targets near criticality, yet most quantum-advantage analyses assume uncorrelated noise.
method: They analyze metrological estimation of parameters encoded by long-range correlated noise and compare the scaling of entanglement-enhanced protocols against unentangled strategies, deriving fundamental bounds on the achievable precision.
result: A new form of exponential quantum advantage is identified, where entangled probe states outperform separable ones exponentially in the system size for sensing correlated-noise parameters.
conclusion: The work expands the regimes in which entanglement provides dramatic metrological gains, motivating entanglement-based sensing of correlated and critical many-body noise sources.

title: Grassmann Time-evolving Matrix Product Operators For Superconducting Quantum Impurity Problem
authors: Chu Guo, Wei Wu, Xiansong Xu, Ping-Xing Chen, Changming Yue, Tian Jiang, And Ruofan Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Chu Guo, Wei Wu, Xiansong Xu, Ping-Xing Chen, Changming Yue, Tian Jiang, and Ruofan Chen

The Grassmann time-evolving matrix product operator (GTEMPO) method, which represents the Feynman-Vernon influence functional as a temporal matrix product state, has been shown to be a flexible and potentially scalable solution for fermionic quantum impurity problems. In this work, we extend GTEMPO …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225115] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the Grassmann time-evolving matrix product operator (GTEMPO) method to tackle superconducting quantum impurity problems, representing the Feynman-Vernon influence functional as a temporal matrix product state.
motivation: Fermionic quantum impurity problems are central to understanding strongly correlated open quantum systems, and scalable numerical methods capable of handling non-Markovian dynamics with superconducting environments are needed.
method: GTEMPO expresses the Feynman-Vernon influence functional as a temporal matrix product state and is extended to superconducting impurity settings, providing a numerically tractable tensor-network-based treatment of the fermionic dynamics.
result: The extended GTEMPO approach is shown to be a flexible and potentially scalable solution for simulating fermionic quantum impurity problems arising in superconducting contexts.
conclusion: The method offers a promising computational tool for open-system and impurity physics, though its contribution is primarily methodological rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.

title: Universal Sensitivity Bound For Thermal Quantum Dynamic Sensing
authors: Rui Zhang, Yang Yang, Xin-You Lü, Wenkui Ding, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Zhang, Yang Yang, Xin-You Lü, Wenkui Ding, and Xiaoguang Wang

We unify the equilibrium and dynamic sensing frameworks of quantum metrology within the context of many-body systems. We investigate dynamic sensing schemes to derive an upper bound on the quantum Fisher information for probe states in thermal equilibrium with their environment. By identifying that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042608] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a universal upper bound on the quantum Fisher information for many-body probe states in thermal equilibrium, unifying equilibrium and dynamic sensing frameworks.
motivation: Quantum metrology typically assumes idealized, zero-temperature or pure probe states, but realistic probes are in thermal equilibrium with their environment, limiting achievable sensitivity. A comprehensive bound on sensitivity for thermal probes is needed.
method: The authors analyze dynamic sensing schemes for many-body systems and prove an upper bound on the quantum Fisher information attainable by probe states that are in thermal equilibrium with their environment.
result: A universal sensitivity bound is established that applies across equilibrium and dynamic sensing regimes, exposing how temperature and thermalization constrain achievable parameter estimation precision.
conclusion: The bound provides a general limit on thermal quantum sensing and connects quantum metrology with thermodynamic constraints, guiding realistic sensing protocol design.

title: Deeply Nonlinear Magnon-photon Hybrid Excitation
authors: Dinesh Wagle, Anish Rai, And M. Benjamin Jungfleisch
abstract:
Author(s): Dinesh Wagle, Anish Rai, and M. Benjamin Jungfleisch

We investigate the microwave-power dependence of magnon-photon coupling in a yttrium iron garnet-sphere/split-ring resonator hybrid system at room temperature and demonstrate that nonlinear spin-wave interactions suppress the coupling through power-induced dissipation of magnetostatic modes. At low …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L200402] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The microwave power dependence of magnon-photon coupling in a room-temperature YIG-sphere/split-ring resonator hybrid is studied, showing that nonlinear spin-wave interactions suppress coupling via power-induced dissipation of magnetostatic modes.
motivation: Magnon-photon hybrid systems are promising platforms for coherent information transduction, but the coupling strength generally degrades at higher drive powers; understanding this nonlinear degradation is needed for practical device operation.
method: The authors measure microwave-power-dependent magnon-photon coupling in a yttrium iron garnet sphere coupled to a split-ring resonator at room temperature, analyzing dissipation and nonlinear spin-wave effects on the magnetostatic modes.
result: Increasing microwave power induces nonlinear spin-wave interactions that dissipate magnetostatic modes and suppress the magnon-photon coupling strength, revealing a strongly nonlinear coupling regime.
conclusion: The observed power-induced suppression of coupling illustrates the limits imposed by nonlinear spin-wave dynamics on magnon-photon hybrid systems, which must be accounted for in high-power or strongly driven applications.

title: Mixed Eigenstates In Spin-boson Systems With One-photon And Two-photon Interactions
authors: David Villaseñor And Marko Robnik
abstract:
Author(s): David Villaseñor and Marko Robnik

Spin-boson systems have attracted increasing attention as accessible experimental platforms and for their potential applications in designing quantum technologies. One characteristic of these systems is the transition from regular to completely chaotic behavior when certain control parameters are va…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044206] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes mixed (regular/chaotic) eigenstates in spin-boson systems with one- and two-photon interactions as control parameters drive the transition to chaos.
motivation: Spin-boson systems are experimentally accessible platforms for quantum technologies, and understanding their regular-to-chaotic transition is important for predicting their behavior under varying control parameters.
method: The authors numerically study the eigenstate statistics and structure of spin-boson models with one-photon and two-photon couplings, analyzing the mixing of regular and chaotic eigenstates using spectral and eigenstate-based diagnostics.
result: The transition from regular to chaotic dynamics is revealed through the properties of mixed eigenstates, showing how the degree of chaos depends on the control parameters and the photon-interaction type.
conclusion: The findings clarify how mixed eigenstates emerge in spin-boson systems, providing insight into the onset of quantum chaos in these platforms relevant for quantum technology design.

title: Low-Depth Quantum Symmetrization
authors: Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, and Daniel Gottesman

Researchers develop low-depth quantum symmetrization algorithms that enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031056] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops low-depth quantum algorithms for symmetrization, enabling efficient bosonic simulation, Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.
motivation: Symmetrization (projection onto the symmetric subspace) underlies many bosonic and permutation-invariant quantum tasks, but existing procedures are often too deep for near-term or fault-tolerant devices.
method: The authors construct low-depth quantum circuits that approximate or exactly implement the symmetrization operator using techniques from quantum algorithm design and representation theory of the symmetric group.
result: The resulting algorithms achieve efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and applications to multiphoton interferometric imaging.
conclusion: Low-depth symmetrization provides a practical primitive with applications spanning bosonic sampling, entangled symmetric-state preparation, and photonic imaging.

title: Asymptotically Solvable Quantum Circuits
authors: Samuel H. Pickering And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel H. Pickering and Bruno Bertini

A new family of quantum circuits gives rise to correlations that are chaotic at short scales yet exactly solvable at long scales.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum circuits yields chaotic correlations at short scales yet is exactly solvable at long scales.
motivation: To understand how chaotic quantum dynamics can coexist with analytic tractability in many-body systems.
method: Constructs and analyzes a family of quantum circuits, likely using dual-unitary or integrable structures, to compute correlation functions across time scales.
result: The circuits display chaotic short-scale correlations but admit exact asymptotic solutions for long-scale behavior.
conclusion: This provides a tractable model for studying the interplay of chaos and solvability in quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Quantum State Designs From Minimally Random Quantum Circuits
authors: Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, and Bruno Bertini

For quantum circuits that generate complex dynamics, a single, one-site operation is sufficient to produce randomness, showcasing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033047] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A single one-site random operation in a quantum circuit can generate quantum state designs, revealing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.
motivation: Understanding how minimal randomness in quantum circuits can lead to complex dynamics and state designs is key to characterizing quantum chaos and randomness generation.
method: The authors analyze quantum circuits with minimal randomness, likely using random matrix theory, design criteria, and measures of chaos to study the emergence of state designs.
result: They find that a single one-site operation suffices to produce randomness, demonstrating that minimal randomness can yield maximal state designs and highlighting a trade-off with dynamical chaos.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental connection between dynamical chaos and randomness generation, showing that state designs can emerge from minimally random quantum circuits.

title: Electrically Tunable Orbital Coupling And Quantum Light Emission From O-Band Quantum Dot Molecules
authors: P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, And J. J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, and J. J. Finley

Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules exhibit electrically tunable orbital coupling, opening a route toward 2D photonic cluster states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033070] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules are shown to have electrically tunable orbital coupling, a step toward generating 2D photonic cluster states.
motivation: Photonic cluster states are a resource for measurement-based quantum computing and quantum networking, but scalable, on-demand generation at telecom wavelengths remains challenging.
method: The authors fabricate and electrically bias InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules in the O-band, tuning the inter-dot orbital coupling via gate voltage and characterizing the resulting quantum light emission.
result: Electrical control over orbital coupling is demonstrated together with quantum light emission in the telecom O-band from the dot-molecule states.
conclusion: The electrically tunable dot-molecule platform is proposed as a route toward generating 2D photonic cluster states for telecom-compatible quantum photonics.

title: Multioutcome Circuit Optimization For Enhanced non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: S. Ismailzadeh And B. Abedi Ravan
abstract:
Author(s): S. Ismailzadeh and B. Abedi Ravan

Photonic quantum computing has gained significant interest in recent years due to its potential for scaling to large numbers of qubits. A critical requirement for fault-tolerant quantum computation is the reliable generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, typically achieved using Gaussian operation…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043511] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a multioutcome circuit optimization method to enhance the generation of non-Gaussian states for fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.
motivation: Reliable generation of non-Gaussian quantum states is a critical requirement for fault-tolerant photonic quantum computation, but achieving high fidelity and success probability with Gaussian operations and measurements remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize multioutcome photonic circuits, likely using numerical optimization over circuit parameters and measurement outcomes, to improve non-Gaussian state generation.
result: The optimized multioutcome circuits are shown to enhance the generation of non-Gaussian states compared to standard approaches, improving key metrics such as success probability or fidelity.
conclusion: Multioutcome circuit optimization offers a practical route to better non-Gaussian resources for photonic quantum computing, though the work remains platform-specific and does not address broader information-theoretic questions.

title: Robustness And Optimization Of NOON-state Interferometry
authors: Romain Dalidet, Anthony Martin, Louis Bellando, Matthieu Bellec, Nicolas Fabre, Sébastien Tanzilli, And Laurent Labonté
abstract:
Author(s): Romain Dalidet, Anthony Martin, Louis Bellando, Matthieu Bellec, Nicolas Fabre, Sébastien Tanzilli, and Laurent Labonté

Quantum-enhanced interferometry is often discussed in terms of ideal resources and asymptotic scalings, whereas in practice its performance is set by a delicate interplay between losses, state imbalance, and photon number. We address this interplay in a folded Franson interferometer fed with partial…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043709] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes and optimizes the robustness of NOON-state interferometry in a folded Franson interferometer under realistic losses, state preparation and detection inefficiencies.

title: Shaping Of The Finite-size Chaos Crossover In Floquet Circuits By Coherent-mismatch Architecture
authors: Xiangjun Tan, Wenqi Liu, Hanjie Zhu, Wenkai Bai, And Zhanning Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangjun Tan, Wenqi Liu, Hanjie Zhu, Wenkai Bai, and Zhanning Wang

We study how the spatial profile of a deterministic coherent gate perturbation affects finite-size quasienergy statistics and operator dynamics in [MATH]-symmetric XXZ Floquet circuits. Using a shared homogeneous reference, we compare a single modified bond with an alternating perturbation ap…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042408] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how the spatial profile of deterministic coherent gate perturbations shapes the finite-size crossover to chaos in U(1)-symmetric XXZ Floquet circuits.
motivation: Understanding how local coherent imperfections influence the onset of quantum chaos and operator spreading in driven many-body systems is relevant for characterizing realistic Floquet devices.
method: Quasienergy level statistics and operator dynamics are computed for XXZ Floquet circuits with a single modified bond versus an alternating perturbation pattern, benchmarked against a shared homogeneous reference.
result: The spatial architecture of the coherent mismatch qualitatively changes the finite-size chaos crossover and the operator spreading behavior.
conclusion: Coherent-mismatch architecture provides a tunable knob for controlling the approach to chaos in Floquet circuits, but the setting is largely a driven-chaos/random-circuit study.

title: Measuring Physical Entropy Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Haim Diamant And Gil Ariel
abstract:
Author(s): Haim Diamant and Gil Ariel

Measuring entropy in nonequilibrium physical systems poses challenges that go far beyond conventional entropy estimation. Recent physics-informed approaches are overcoming these challenges and providing new ways to detect and understand nonequilibrium transitions in systems ranging from jammed packings to swarming bacteria.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041002] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: A perspective on physics-informed methods for measuring entropy in nonequilibrium classical systems, with applications to jammed packings and swarming bacteria.
motivation: Measuring entropy in nonequilibrium physical systems is fundamentally challenging and goes beyond conventional entropy estimation techniques.
method: The paper reviews recent physics-informed approaches that overcome these challenges by leveraging physical constraints and system-specific insights.
result: These approaches enable the detection and understanding of nonequilibrium transitions in diverse systems ranging from jammed packings to swarming bacteria.
conclusion: New entropy measurement techniques provide a practical route to characterize nonequilibrium transitions in classical many-body systems.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
motivation: Trotterization is a key technique for digital quantum simulation, but rigorous error bounds for time-dependent Hamiltonians and multiproduct formulas remain less developed, limiting resource estimates for simulating driven and adiabatic dynamics.
method: The authors use Floquet theory to analyze the error of product and multiproduct formulas applied to time-dependent Hamiltonians, deriving bounds that scale with nested commutators.
