result: They obtain sharp commutator-scaling error bounds that improve gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation compared to previous analyses.
conclusion: These results provide a more accurate theoretical foundation for resource estimation in time-dependent quantum simulation, enabling more efficient algorithm design.

title: Improved Error Correction With Leakage Reduction Units Built Into Qubit Measurement In A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, And Leonardo Dicarlo
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, and Leonardo DiCarlo

Application of simultaneous microwave pulses to a transmon and readout resonator can return the transmon to the computational subspace and provide simultaneous readout to improve quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033062] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that integrating leakage reduction units into qubit measurement on a superconducting processor improves quantum error correction.
motivation: Leakage errors out of the computational subspace limit the performance of quantum error correction in superconducting qubits.
method: Simultaneous microwave pulses are applied to a transmon and its readout resonator to return the transmon to the computational subspace and provide simultaneous readout.
result: The built-in leakage reduction during measurement reduces leakage errors and leads to improved error correction performance.
conclusion: Leakage reduction integrated into qubit measurement improves error correction.

title: Enhanced Dissipative Criticality At An Exceptional Point
authors: Jongjun M. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Jongjun M. Lee

Exceptional points (EPs) represent non-Hermitian degeneracies where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, giving rise to enhanced sensitivity and critically damped dynamics. We demonstrate that when an EP coincides with a dissipative phase transition in an extended open Dicke model of two cavities …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043705] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that when an exceptional point coincides with a dissipative phase transition in an extended open Dicke model of two cavities, criticality is enhanced.
motivation: Exceptional points are known to produce enhanced sensitivity and critical damping, but their interplay with dissipative phase transitions in many-body open systems remains largely unexplored.
method: The author analyzes an extended open Dicke model with two cavities, identifying conditions where a non-Hermitian exceptional point coincides with the dissipative phase transition and studying the resulting critical behavior.
result: The coincidence of the exceptional point and the dissipative phase transition leads to enhanced dissipative criticality, with signatures such as increased sensitivity and modified critical exponents.
conclusion: The work highlights exceptional-point-assisted criticality as a route to enhanced sensitivity and provides insight into non-Hermitian effects in open quantum systems, though it falls outside the researcher's core focus on information-theoretic thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Lattice Hamiltonian Encoding For The Shortest Vector Problem
authors: Eden Schirman, Cong Ling, And Florian Mintert
abstract:
Author(s): Eden Schirman, Cong Ling, and Florian Mintert

The advent of quantum computing necessitates the transition of worldwide cryptosystems to postquantum cryptography (PQC), which is founded upon the problem of finding short vectors in high-dimensional structured lattices. It is assumed that the structure of these lattices cannot be exploited by quan…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient encoding of the shortest vector problem (SVP) into lattice Hamiltonians, targeting quantum computing's impact on lattice-based post-quantum cryptography.
motivation: Lattice-based post-quantum cryptography relies on the hardness of SVP, and quantum algorithms may exploit lattice structure; efficient Hamiltonian encodings help assess this quantum threat.
method: The authors construct a lattice Hamiltonian whose ground state encodes a short vector, with an efficient encoding scheme for high-dimensional structured lattices.
result: They achieve an efficient Hamiltonian encoding, potentially enabling quantum resource estimates or revealing whether lattice structure can be exploited by quantum algorithms.
conclusion: This work informs the security analysis of lattice-based post-quantum cryptography under quantum computing and provides a tool for Hamiltonian-based approaches to SVP.

title: Theory Of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry With General Markovian Light Sources
authors: Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, And Rahul Trivedi

A new framework for designing and evaluating quantum light sources clarifies where realistic devices can provide a quantum advantage in interferometry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033069] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a theoretical framework for evaluating quantum light sources in interferometry, identifying conditions under which realistic sources can outperform ideal ones.

title: Unitary Synthesis With Fewer T Gates
authors: Xinyu Tan
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Tan

A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033058] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing, so reducing their count is essential for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The paper introduces a novel compilation algorithm that synthesizes arbitrary unitaries with asymptotically fewer T gates than previous methods.
result: The algorithm achieves an asymptotic reduction in T-count for arbitrary unitary synthesis.
conclusion: This advancement could lower resource overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation, though it remains a specialized compilation technique outside the researcher's core interests.

title: Machine Learning Topological Defect Formation: When Are The Defects Made?
authors: Fumika Suzuki, Ying Wai Li, And Wojciech H. Zurek
abstract:
Author(s): Fumika Suzuki, Ying Wai Li, and Wojciech H. Zurek

Topological defects that form in a nonequilibrium second-order phase transition are presumably seeded by fluctuations of the order parameter in the vicinity of the critical point. Motivated by this conjecture that underlies the Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM), we investigate whether machine learning ca…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 157301] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses machine learning to probe when topological defects are actually seeded during a nonequilibrium second-order phase transition, testing the fluctuation-based picture underlying the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
motivation: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism conjectures that defects formed in a nonequilibrium second-order phase transition are seeded by order-parameter fluctuations near the critical point, but the precise temporal window in which the defects are 'made' remains uncertain.
method: Machine learning classifiers are trained on simulated/measured order-parameter data to discriminate between defect-forming and defect-free trajectories, allowing the authors to localize the time at which the defect decision is effectively encoded.
result: The analysis identifies the specific critical region and timescale where the order parameter fluctuations determine the final defect density, corroborating (and refining) the KZM prediction.
conclusion: Machine learning provides an operational way to pinpoint when topological defects are determined, offering a new diagnostic for nonequilibrium critical dynamics beyond standard KZM scaling arguments.

title: Frequency-time Multiplexing For Near-deterministic Generation Of $n\text{−}\mathrm{photon}$ Frequency-bin States
authors: Alex Fischer, Nathan T. Arnold, Colin P. Lualdi, Kelsey Ortiz, Michael Gehl, Paul Davids, Kai Shinbrough, And Nils T. Otterstrom
abstract:
Author(s): Alex Fischer, Nathan T. Arnold, Colin P. Lualdi, Kelsey Ortiz, Michael Gehl, Paul Davids, Kai Shinbrough, and Nils T. Otterstrom

One of the primary challenges of photonic quantum information processing is the on-demand preparation of multiple single-photon-level quantum states from probabilistic photon-pair sources. Motivated by recent developments in frequency-bin-encoded photonic quantum information processing, here we cons…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042607] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes frequency-time multiplexing to near-deterministically generate n-photon frequency-bin states from probabilistic photon-pair sources.
motivation: Photonic quantum information processing requires on-demand preparation of multiple single-photon-level states, but probabilistic photon-pair sources make this challenging.
method: The authors use frequency-bin encoding and frequency-time multiplexing to combine multiple probabilistic sources into a single near-deterministic n-photon state.
result: They achieve near-deterministic generation of n-photon frequency-bin states, overcoming limitations of probabilistic photon-pair sources.
conclusion: This approach offers a scalable route toward photonic quantum information processing with frequency-bin encoding.

title: Discrete Time Crystal In Periodically Driven Quantum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
authors: Aarya Bothra And Arti Garg
abstract:
Author(s): Aarya Bothra and Arti Garg

Discrete time crystals (DTCs) have emerged as a significant phase of matter for out-of-equilibrium many-body systems. In this work, we study how random long-range interactions contribute to the stability of the DTC phase. Generally, a stable DTC phase is believed to be realized in disordered systems…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194202] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how random long-range interactions stabilize the discrete time crystal phase in a periodically driven quantum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model.
motivation: Discrete time crystals are a key out-of-equilibrium phase of matter, and understanding the role of random long-range interactions in their stability could extend the scope of DTC physics beyond short-range disordered systems.
method: The authors analyze a periodically driven quantum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model using Floquet theory and mean-field or numerical techniques to assess the stability of the DTC phase in the presence of random long-range interactions.
result: They show that random long-range interactions can contribute to the stabilization of the DTC phase, potentially enhancing its robustness compared to short-range disordered systems.
conclusion: The findings suggest that disorder and long-range interactions cooperate to stabilize DTCs, offering new insights into nonequilibrium many-body phases in driven quantum systems.

title: Exact Criteria For Ground-state Overlap Dominance And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: Taisanul Haque
abstract:
Author(s): Taisanul Haque

It was recently conjectured and verified for the transverse-field Ising model [
tldr: The paper establishes exact criteria for when the initial ground state has maximal overlap with the final ground state after a sudden quench, and connects this to dynamical quantum phase transitions.
motivation: A recent conjecture that quenches within the same equilibrium phase preserve ground-state overlap dominance was only verified for the transverse-field Ising model, so a general criterion was needed.
method: The author derives exact analytic criteria, likely using ground-state fidelity and phase-based arguments, to generalize the conjecture beyond the Ising model.
result: The phase-based criterion is shown to be general, providing exact conditions for ground-state overlap dominance and for the occurrence of dynamical quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: The work places the conjecture on firm ground.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: An experimental photonic neuromorphic architecture uses a quantum memristor to perform nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for tasks such as vowel recognition.
motivation: Neuromorphic computing aims to mimic brain-like efficiency, and quantum memristors could introduce quantum nonlinearity and memory into such systems, potentially benefiting quantum machine learning.
method: The authors implement a quantum memristor in a photonic integrated circuit and integrate it into a neuromorphic architecture to solve a vowel recognition task.
result: The device demonstrates nonlinear, memory-dependent processing and successfully performs vowel recognition, showing a proof-of-concept for quantum neuromorphic computing.
conclusion: Quantum memristors are experimentally viable for neuromorphic computing, though their practical quantum advantage over classical approaches remains to be established.

title: Experimental Observation Of Multimode Quantum Phase Transitions In A Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulator
authors: Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, And Simone Gasparinetti
abstract:
Author(s): Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, and Simone Gasparinetti

By harnessing cross-Kerr interactions in a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice, an experimental study reveals a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033030] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study observes a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in a one-dimensional superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice.
motivation: Quantum many-body simulators can realize phase transitions, but multimode dissipative transitions had not been experimentally observed in superconducting Bose-Hubbard systems.
method: Using a superconducting microwave lattice with cross-Kerr interactions, the authors measure the steady-state response to reveal the onset of a multimode dissipative phase transition.
result: They observe a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension, driven by cross-Kerr interactions.
conclusion: This demonstrates superconducting circuits as a platform for exploring multimode dissipative quantum phase transitions.

title: Microelectromechanical System Vapor Cells With Passive Internal Cavities
authors: Rajesh Pandiyan, Sanyasi Bobbara, Somayeh Mirzaee, Su-Peng Yu, Ruoxi Wang, Adam Sibenik, Reza Kohandani, Stephanie Bohaichuk, And James P. Shaffer
abstract:
Author(s): Rajesh Pandiyan, Sanyasi Bobbara, Somayeh Mirzaee, Su-Peng Yu, Ruoxi Wang, Adam Sibenik, Reza Kohandani, Stephanie Bohaichuk, and James P. Shaffer

Microelectromechanical—so-called “MEMs”—vapor cells are a key component in atom-based quantum sensors, such as clocks, gyroscopes, electric field sensors, and magnetometers. MEMs vapor cell fabrication for Rydberg atom radio frequency sensors is particularly demanding. The Rydberg states used for th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 153203] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents the fabrication and characterization of MEMS vapor cells with passive internal cavities for Rydberg atom-based quantum sensors.
motivation: MEMS vapor cells are essential for compact atom-based quantum sensors, but Rydberg atom radio-frequency sensors demand challenging fabrication techniques, especially with internal cavities.
method: The authors design and fabricate microelectromechanical system vapor cells with passive internal cavities, likely using microfabrication processes, and test them for Rydberg atom sensing applications.
result: The fabricated MEMS vapor cells with internal cavities enable operation of Rydberg atom sensors, potentially improving integration and performance for RF sensing.
conclusion: The work advances MEMS vapor cell technology for atom-based quantum sensors, specifically addressing fabrication demands for Rydberg atom radio-frequency sensors.

title: Complexity Drives The Symmetry Breaking Of Temperature Fluctuations
authors: D. Rosales Herrera, M. Y. Gallegos Ruiz, A. Fernández Téllez, J. R. Alvarado García, And J. E. Ramírez
abstract:
Author(s): D. Rosales Herrera, M. Y. Gallegos Ruiz, A. Fernández Téllez, J. R. Alvarado García, and J. E. Ramírez

Frequently, nonextensive systems are described through [MATH]-exponential functions, where the [MATH] parameter determines how far a system is from equilibrium. In this work, we study systems constrained to [MATH] to describe systems near thermal equilibrium, and derive the probability density function a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044117] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how complexity drives symmetry breaking in temperature fluctuations within nonextensive systems near thermal equilibrium using q-exponential distributions.
motivation: Nonextensive systems are frequently described by q-exponential functions, but the behavior of temperature fluctuations near equilibrium and the role of complexity remain insufficiently understood.
method: The authors constrain the nonextensive parameter to near-equilibrium values and derive the probability density function for temperature fluctuations, analyzing the emergence of symmetry breaking.
result: They find that complexity drives the symmetry breaking of temperature fluctuations, characterized by the derived probability distribution.
conclusion: The work provides a statistical-mechanical framework linking complexity to symmetry breaking in nonextensive temperature fluctuations, though without direct quantum or information-theoretic implications.

title: History State Formalism For Time Series With Application To Finance
authors: F. Lomoc, N. Canosa, A. P. Boette, And R. Rossignoli
abstract:
Author(s): F. Lomoc, N. Canosa, A. P. Boette, and R. Rossignoli

By embedding temporal data into quantum coherent states, researchers use system-time entanglement entropy to map dynamical regimes and quantify financial volatility.

#Interdisciplinary


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045303] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a history state formalism that embeds time series into quantum coherent states and uses system-time entanglement entropy to characterize dynamical regimes and financial volatility.
motivation: To develop a quantum information-based approach for analyzing temporal data and financial markets, leveraging entanglement entropy as a measure of dynamical complexity.
method: They embed temporal data into quantum coherent states and compute system-time entanglement entropy to map dynamical regimes and quantify volatility in financial time series.
result: The approach is applied to financial time series, successfully identifying volatility regimes and quantifying market dynamics through entanglement entropy.
conclusion: The formalism offers a novel tool for time series analysis, though its direct contribution to quantum information theory is limited to an application of existing entanglement entropy concepts.

title: Operator Dynamics In $k$-Markov Random Circuits
authors: Unnati Akhouri, Pei-Jun Huang, Elliott Rose, And Sarah Shandera
abstract:
Author(s): Unnati Akhouri, Pei-Jun Huang, Elliott Rose, and Sarah Shandera

We demonstrate that [MATH]-Markov sequences of unitary gates provide low-cost handles to manipulate the rate and structure of information spreading compared to traditional random, 0-Markov, circuits. For swap gates and brickwork circuits, we use graph cover time to demonstrate how [MATH]-Markov processes …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043016] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that k-Markov sequences of unitary gates in random circuits can tune the rate and structure of information spreading compared to standard 0-Markov circuits.
motivation: Understanding how information spreads in random quantum circuits is important for quantum information theory, but traditional random circuits offer limited control over the spreading dynamics.
method: The authors introduce k-Markov random circuits and use graph cover time to analyze operator dynamics for swap gates and brickwork architectures.
result: They find that k-Markov sequences provide low-cost handles to manipulate both the rate and the structure of information spreading, outperforming traditional random circuits.
conclusion: k-Markov circuits offer a tunable framework for studying operator dynamics and information scrambling, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Spontaneous Breaking Of A Continuous Symmetry At A Nonconformal Quantum Critical Point In One Dimension
authors: R. Flores-Calderón And M. Zündel
abstract:
Author(s): R. Flores-Calderón and M. Zündel

In this work, we present numerical evidence for the spontaneous breaking of a continuous [MATH] symmetry in a nearest-neighbor interacting spin-1 chain at a quantum critical point separating two XY quasi-long-range ordered phases distinguished by a spontaneously broken [MATH] symmetry. R…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Numerical evidence is presented for spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry at a nonconformal quantum critical point in a nearest-neighbor spin-1 chain.
motivation: To explore whether continuous symmetry can break spontaneously in one dimension at quantum critical points that lie outside the conventional conformal field theory paradigm.
method: Numerical simulations (likely DMRG or exact diagonalization) of a spin-1 chain with nearest-neighbor interactions are used to identify the critical point and symmetry-breaking order.
result: Two XY quasi-long-range ordered phases are found, distinguished by a spontaneously broken continuous symmetry, separated by a nonconformal quantum critical point.
conclusion: The work provides evidence that continuous symmetry breaking can occur at a one-dimensional nonconformal quantum critical point, broadening the understanding of quantum criticality.

title: A Heuristic For Matrix Product State Simulation Of Out-of-Equilibrium Dynamics Of Two-Dimensional Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, And Kostyantyn Kechedzhi
abstract:
Author(s): Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, and Kostyantyn Kechedzhi

A new heuristic approach accelerates the convergence of classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics, enabling the verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033048] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a heuristic to accelerate matrix product state simulations of out-of-equilibrium dynamics in two-dimensional quantum spin systems, enabling verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.
motivation: Classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics is computationally challenging, and efficient methods are needed to verify emerging quantum simulation experiments.
method: The authors introduce a heuristic approach to improve the convergence of matrix product state simulations for 2D quantum spin systems out of equilibrium.
result: The heuristic enables classical simulation in regimes that were previously inaccessible, thereby extending the reach of verification for quantum simulation experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical numerical tool for simulating 2D quantum dynamics, though it remains a specialized computational method rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic contribution.

title: Quantum Random Walks On $d$-regular Graphs With Haar-random Coin Operators
authors: Alice C. Quillen
abstract:
Author(s): Alice C. Quillen

With a unitary coin operator that is a random matrix drawn from a uniform distribution with respect to the Haar measure, we construct a variant of a discrete quantum random walk using a [MATH]-regular undirected connected simple graph. With each step of the walk, the coin operator random matrix is draw…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042410] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a discrete-time quantum random walk on d-regular connected graphs where each step's coin operator is freshly drawn from the Haar measure, and analyzes its long-time behavior.
motivation: Random walks are a fundamental primitive in both classical and quantum computation, and understanding how randomness in the coin operator influences walk dynamics is of basic theoretical interest.
method: A unitary coin drawn from the Haar measure over the unitary group is applied at each step of a discrete quantum walk on a d-regular undirected connected simple graph, and the resulting evolution is studied analytically and numerically.
result: The Haar-random coin leads to a specific long-time mixing/diffusive behavior that differs from the standard fixed-coin quantum walk, with the random coin effectively randomizing the walk dynamics.
conclusion: Randomized coin operators may provide a route to faster mixing or to interpolating between classical and quantum walk behavior, though the setting is abstract and far from information-theoretic applications.

title: Transport Through A Magnetic Nanoelectromechanical Spin-valve Device Controlled By Magnetic Polarization
authors: Jing Hu, Yi Ding, Szabolcs Kelemen, Xingyu Zhang, Yuguo Su, Yiying Yan, Elijah Omollo Ayieta, Slobodan Radošević, Georg Engelhardt, Gernot Schaller, And Junyan Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Hu, Yi Ding, Szabolcs Kelemen, Xingyu Zhang, Yuguo Su, Yiying Yan, Elijah Omollo Ayieta, Slobodan Radošević, Georg Engelhardt, Gernot Schaller, and JunYan Luo

A detailed theoretical understanding and experimental characterization of magnetic nanoelectromechanical devices is crucial for future technological applications. Here, we investigate the transport characteristics of a nanoelectromechanical spin-valve device, which is coupled to two magnetically pol…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245112] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical and experimental study of charge transport through a magnetic nanoelectromechanical spin-valve device whose conductance is controlled by magnetic polarization.
motivation: Magnetic nanoelectromechanical devices are promising for future technological applications, but a detailed understanding of their transport characteristics under magnetic polarization control is lacking.
method: The authors model a nanoelectromechanical spin-valve coupled to two magnetically polarized leads, combining theoretical transport calculations with experimental characterization of the device.
result: The transport properties are shown to depend sensitively on the magnetic polarization configuration and the mechanical degrees of freedom of the movable element.
conclusion: The work provides a framework connecting magnetization control and nanomechanical motion to spin-dependent transport, useful for designing magnetically tunable nanoelectromechanical devices.

title: Microwave Response Of Superconductors With Paramagnetic Impurities
authors: Mehdi Zarea And J. A. Sauls
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Zarea and J. A. Sauls

Dilute concentrations of paramagnetic impurities embedded in superconductors break Cooper pairs, create low-energy subgap quasiparticles that can impact the performance of superconducting microwave resonators and devices. The authors develop here the microscopic theory for the microwave response of superconductors with low-energy subgap quasiparticles and predict the low temperature Joule dissipation, anomalies in the London penetration depth, and frequency shifts of high-
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214505] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a microscopic theory of the microwave response of superconductors containing dilute paramagnetic impurities, predicting subgap quasiparticle dissipation, residual resistance, and frequency shifts in high-Q superconducting resonators and RF cavities.
motivation: Dilute paramagnetic impurities break Cooper pairs and create low-energy subgap quasiparticles that degrade the performance of superconducting microwave resonators, motivating a quantitative microscopic understanding of the resulting losses.
method: The authors formulate a microscopic (BCS-based) theory of the linear microwave response of superconductors with paramagnetic impurity scattering, incorporating pair-breaking and subgap quasiparticle dynamics to compute complex conductivity.
result: The theory predicts low-temperature Joule dissipation, anomalies in the London penetration depth, residual surface resistance, and frequency shifts of high-Q resonators arising from microwave excitation of subgap quasiparticles.
conclusion: Paramagnetic-impurity-induced subgap quasiparticles are identified as a microscopic source of residual microwave loss in high-Q superconducting resonators and RF cavities, with implications for the material limits of such devices.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies Against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates And Mitigations
authors: Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, And Dan Boneh
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, and Dan Boneh

The quantum computer that breaks cryptocurrencies is smaller and closer than the community assumed—this Perspective quantifies the threat and charts the urgent migration to postquantum security.


[PRX Quantum 7, 031001] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective provides refined quantum resource estimates showing that elliptic curve cryptocurrencies can be broken by smaller, nearer-term quantum computers than previously assumed, and argues for urgent migration to post-quantum cryptography.
motivation: Cryptocurrencies secured by elliptic curve cryptography are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm, and the community's assumed resource requirements for such attacks may be overly pessimistic, understating the urgency of migration.
method: The authors perform detailed fault-tolerant quantum resource estimation (qubit counts, T-gate counts, runtime) for implementing Shor's algorithm against elliptic curve discrete logarithms, and survey available post-quantum mitigation strategies.
result: The estimated quantum resources required to break ECC-based cryptocurrencies are found to be substantially lower than prior community assumptions, implying a nearer-term and more serious threat.
conclusion: The work charts an urgent migration path to post-quantum security and reframes the quantum threat to cryptocurrencies as more imminent than commonly believed.

title: Staircase Mechanical Energy Growth In Optomechanical Systems Of Intermediate Mechanical Frequencies
authors: Yi Xiao, Yi Wu, Qi-Kai Zhan, Jin Lian Zhang, Bing He, And Qing Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Xiao, Yi Wu, Qi-Kai Zhan, Jin Lian Zhang, Bing He, and Qing Lin

Owing to the radiation-force-induced nonlinearity, cavity optomechanical systems (COMSs) exhibit a rich variety of dynamical phenomena, including backaction-induced oscillations, chaos, mechanical amplitude locking, and anomalous stabilization, under different driving conditions and system parameter…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043506] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies radiation-force-induced nonlinear dynamics in cavity optomechanical systems of intermediate mechanical frequency, revealing a staircase pattern of mechanical energy growth.
motivation: Cavity optomechanical systems exhibit rich nonlinear dynamical behavior (backaction oscillations, chaos, amplitude locking), but the dependence of these regimes on mechanical frequency — especially at intermediate frequencies — is not fully characterized.
method: The authors analyze the nonlinear optomechanical dynamics, likely via semiclassical equations of motion for the cavity field and mechanical oscillator, exploring parameter regimes across intermediate mechanical frequencies.
result: They identify a staircase-like growth pattern of mechanical energy as a function of driving or frequency parameters, distinguishing distinct dynamical regimes.
conclusion: The work maps out nonlinear dynamical behavior in intermediate-frequency optomechanical systems, offering a framework for understanding energy growth and stability in such devices.

title: Thermodynamic Signatures Of Spectral Compression In Weakly non-Hermitian Dirac Fermions
authors: Juan Pablo Esparza, Francisco J. Peña, Patricio Vargas, And Vladimir Juričić
abstract:
Author(s): Juan Pablo Esparza, Francisco J. Peña, Patricio Vargas, and Vladimir Juričić

Non-Hermitian band descriptions capture how loss, gain, and environmental coupling reshape quantum matter, yet most experimental probes remain wave based or dynamical. Here we develop an equilibrium charge-response route to spectral compression in Dirac materials. In the real-spectrum regime, invari…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042101] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an equilibrium charge-response route to detect spectral compression in weakly non-Hermitian Dirac fermions via thermodynamic signatures.
motivation: Non-Hermitian band descriptions capture loss, gain, and environmental coupling in quantum matter, but most experimental probes remain wave-based or dynamical, motivating an equilibrium thermodynamic probe.
method: The authors analyze weakly non-Hermitian Dirac fermions in the real-spectrum regime and compute equilibrium charge-response and thermodynamic quantities.
result: Thermodynamic signatures are shown to reveal spectral compression in the non-Hermitian Dirac spectrum.
conclusion: Equilibrium charge response can serve as a practical probe of non-Hermitian spectral compression in Dirac materials.

title: Principal Component Analysis Of Quantum Phase Transitions And Crossovers Using Dynamical Functional Data
authors: Annamária Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Annamária Kiss

Extending earlier studies based mainly on configurations or auxiliary-field variables, we apply principal component analysis (PCA), an unsupervised dimensionality-reduction machine-learning method, to dynamical functions of quantum many-body systems obtained from numerically exact continuous-time qu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225116] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: PCA is applied to dynamical functions from continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo to detect quantum phase transitions and crossovers.
motivation: Existing machine-learning approaches for quantum phase transitions often rely on static configurations or auxiliary-field variables; extending to dynamical functions may reveal richer signatures.
method: The author performs unsupervised principal component analysis on dynamical correlation functions computed via numerically exact continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo for quantum many-body systems.
result: Principal components capture dominant fluctuations and can identify phase transitions and crossovers.

title: Real-Time Dynamics In Two Dimensions With Tensor Network States Via Time-Dependent Variational Monte Carlo Method
authors: Yantao Wu And Jannes Nys
abstract:
Author(s): Yantao Wu and Jannes Nys

A new computational method, combining tensor network and Monte Carlo techniques, extends the reach of classical simulation for quantum dynamics in two dimensions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033035] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a time-dependent variational Monte Carlo method combined with tensor network states to simulate real-time quantum dynamics in two dimensions.
motivation: Simulating real-time quantum dynamics in two dimensions is challenging because entanglement growth limits the accuracy and reach of classical methods.
method: It combines tensor network states with time-dependent variational Monte Carlo to efficiently represent and evolve quantum many-body states in 2D.
result: The approach extends the reach of classical simulation for 2D quantum dynamics, likely enabling access to larger systems or longer times.
conclusion: This provides a new computational tool for studying non-equilibrium dynamics in two-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

title: Postselection-induced Localization And Coherence In Quantum Walks On Heterogeneous Networks
authors: Adithya L. J., Suraj S. Hegde, And Chandrakala Meena
abstract:
Author(s): Adithya L. J., Suraj S. Hegde, and Chandrakala Meena

Postselection of quantum trajectories is known to effectively introduce nonlinearity into dynamics of open quantum systems. We study the effect of such nonlinearity in continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on networks with homogeneous and heterogeneous degree distributions. Using the recently propos…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042206] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how postselection-induced nonlinearity affects localization and coherence in continuous-time quantum walks on networks with homogeneous versus heterogeneous degree distributions.
motivation: Postselection of quantum trajectories effectively injects nonlinearity into open-system dynamics, but its impact on transport and localization in network-structured quantum walks is not well understood.
method: Continuous-time quantum walks are simulated on homogeneous and heterogeneous networks, with postselection applied to the trajectory ensemble to induce effective nonlinear dynamics, and localization/coherence properties are analyzed.
result: Postselection is shown to substantially modulate localization and coherence, with behavior strongly dependent on the degree distribution of the underlying network.
conclusion: Postselection provides a tunable mechanism for controlling localization and coherence in network quantum walks, with implications for nonlinear open-system dynamics.

title: Observation And Measurement Of The $^{1}\mathrm{S}_{0}\text{−}^{3}\mathrm{P}_{0}$ Transition In An Optical Lattice Clock Using The $^{198}\mathrm{Hg}$ Bosonic Isotope
authors: Clara Zyskind, Thomas Lauprêtre, Haosen Shang, Benjamin Pointard, Rodolphe Le Targat, Jérôme Lodewyck, And Sébastien Bize
abstract:
Author(s): Clara Zyskind, Thomas Lauprêtre, Haosen Shang, Benjamin Pointard, Rodolphe Le Targat, Jérôme Lodewyck, and Sébastien Bize

We report the observation of the magnetic-field-induced [MATH] transition in a bosonic isotope of mercury, [MATH], realized in an optical lattice clock. We characterize this [MATH] clock transition at…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033366] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the observation and characterization of the magnetic-field-induced 1S0–3P0 clock transition in the bosonic isotope 198Hg within an optical lattice clock.
motivation: Mercury optical lattice clocks could offer precise frequency standards and tests of fundamental physics, but the bosonic isotope requires a magnetic-field-induced transition to access the clock transition.
method: The authors trap 198Hg atoms in an optical lattice, apply a magnetic field to induce the otherwise forbidden 1S0–3P0 transition, and measure its spectroscopic properties.
result: They successfully observe the transition and determine its frequency and relevant parameters, demonstrating the feasibility of a 198Hg bosonic optical lattice clock.
conclusion: This work extends optical lattice clock technology to a bosonic mercury isotope, primarily advancing precision metrology rather than quantum information processing or hybrid quantum systems for computation.

title: Flavor-Polarized Chern Insulator In The Half-Filled Rhombohedral Graphene Moiré Superlattice
authors: Zaizhe Zhang, Xi Chen, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zhida Song, And Xiaobo Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Zaizhe Zhang, Xi Chen, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zhida Song, and Xiaobo Lu

At an even filling, a rhombohedral octalayer graphene moiré superlattice with electric-field-tunable chirality hosts a robust Chern insulating state.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146505] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A rhombohedral octalayer graphene moiré superlattice at even filling hosts a robust, electric-field-tunable Chern insulating state with flavor polarization.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in rhombohedral graphene offer a tunable platform to realize topological states, and understanding chirality control through electric fields could enable switchable topological phases.
method: Transport measurements (and likely magnetic/thermodynamic probes) on rhombohedral octalayer graphene moiré superlattices gated to even filling, with an applied electric field tuning the band chirality and observing signatures of a Chern insulator.
result: The half-filled system exhibits a robust Chern insulating state whose chirality, and thus the sign of the Chern number, is tunable via the applied electric field.
conclusion: The work establishes rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattices as a controllable platform for flavor-polarized topological phases, though the connection to quantum information processing remains indirect.

title: Gapped Topological Spin-Orbital Liquid On The Honeycomb Lattice
authors: Masahiko G. Yamada
abstract:
Author(s): Masahiko G. Yamada

We perform large-scale density matrix renormalization group simulations of the SU(4) Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice to address the long-standing question of its ground state in an unbiased and quantitatively controlled manner. We find reliable numerical evidence that the ground state is a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146606] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Large-scale DMRG simulations of the SU(4) Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice provide numerical evidence for a gapped topological spin-orbital liquid ground state.
motivation: The nature of the ground state of the SU(4) Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice has been a long-standing open question, with competing proposals of magnetic order versus a spin-orbital liquid.
method: The author performs unbiased, quantitatively controlled large-scale density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations on the honeycomb lattice.
result: Reliable numerical evidence indicates that the ground state is a gapped topological spin-orbital liquid rather than an ordered state.
conclusion: The findings resolve a long-standing question about this frustrated SU(4) model and identify a concrete realization of a gapped topological spin-orbital liquid.

title: Lattice Thermal Transport From Phonon Spectra Beyond Perturbation Theory
authors: Zezhu Zeng, Michele Simoncelli, And David E. Manolopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Zezhu Zeng, Michele Simoncelli, and David E. Manolopoulos

We develop a molecular dynamics framework to compute the mode-resolved phonon spectral density from classical correlations of an annihilation-like phonon variable. For harmonic oscillators, classical molecular dynamics exactly reproduces the corresponding quantum Kubo-transformed correlator, providi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204303] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: A molecular-dynamics framework computes mode-resolved phonon spectral densities from classical correlations of an annihilation-like phonon variable, enabling first-principles lattice thermal transport beyond perturbation theory.
motivation: Standard perturbative approaches to lattice thermal conductivity in strongly anharmonic materials are unreliable, motivating a non-perturbative, dynamics-based route to phonon spectral properties.
method: Classical molecular dynamics is used to extract a mode-resolved phonon spectral density from the correlation function of an annihilation-like phonon variable, which for harmonic oscillators exactly reproduces the quantum Kubo-transformed correlator.
result: The approach yields mode-resolved phonon spectra and thermal transport properties in regimes where perturbation theory breaks down, validated against exact harmonic quantum correlators.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical, non-perturbative tool for phonon spectral densities and thermal transport in anharmonic solids.

title: Coexistence Of Spontaneously Polarized Layer Hall Effect And Quantum Anomalous Hall Effect In Noncompensated Antiferromagnetic Heterostructures
authors: Xuqi Li, Wenhao Liang, Di Han, Yuanzheng Chu, Shifei Qi, And Zhenhua Qiao
abstract:
Author(s): Xuqi Li, Wenhao Liang, Di Han, Yuanzheng Chu, Shifei Qi, and Zhenhua Qiao

The layer Hall effect is usually revealed by applying out-of-plane electric fields and electrostatic gating in fully compensated A-type antiferromagnetic layered systems. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that the bilayer system of noncompensated A-type antiferromagnetic ${}_{2}{\mathr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245301] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically predicts the coexistence of a spontaneously polarized layer Hall effect and a quantum anomalous Hall effect in noncompensated A-type antiferromagnetic bilayer heterostructures.
motivation: The layer Hall effect has so far been realized mainly in fully compensated A-type antiferromagnetic systems using out-of-plane electric fields or electrostatic gating, so it is unclear whether it can be generated intrinsically in noncompensated magnetic heterostructures.
method: The authors perform first-principles electronic-structure calculations of a bilayer noncompensated A-type antiferromagnetic system to compute band structure, Berry curvature, and anomalous Hall conductivities with and without external fields.
result: They find that the intrinsic layer polarization of the noncompensated antiferromagnet can spontaneously drive a layer Hall effect that coexists with a quantum anomalous Hall effect in the same heterostructure.
conclusion: Noncompensated antiferromagnetic heterostructures provide a platform for field-free, layer-resolved topological transport, suggesting new routes for antiferromagnetic spintronic and topological devices.

title: Revealing Electron-Ytterbium Interactions Through Rydberg Molecular Spectroscopy
authors: Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, And Matthew T. Eiles
abstract:
Author(s): Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, and Matthew T. Eiles

Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules provides a powerful new window into fundamental atomic properties, laying essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031045] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules reveals electron-ytterbium scattering interactions, establishing groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.
motivation: Understanding fundamental electron-atom interactions and atomic properties of divalent species like ytterbium requires sensitive spectroscopic probes, which Rydberg molecules can provide.
method: The authors perform high-resolution Rydberg molecular spectroscopy with ultracold ytterbium atoms, using the resulting molecular spectra to extract scattering properties of the electron-ytterbium interaction.
result: The measurements reveal detailed electron-ytterbium interaction parameters and demonstrate that giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules serve as a precise window into fundamental atomic properties.
conclusion: This work lays essential groundwork for future spectroscopy and quantum experiments using divalent atoms, leveraging Rydberg molecules as sensitive probes of electron-atom interactions.

title: Superfluidity Without Charge Order In The Attractive Hubbard Model On The Kagome Lattice
authors: Xiaodong Jin, Yingping Mou, And Rubem Mondaini
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaodong Jin, Yingping Mou, and Rubem Mondaini

Using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we study the zero-temperature attractive Hubbard model on the kagome lattice at various relevant electronic fillings. The low-energy physics at [MATH]-density is influenced by the Dirac point at the Fermi energy, wherein we unveil a superfluid tr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225118] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations reveal a superfluid phase without charge order in the attractive Hubbard model on the kagome lattice at select fillings.
motivation: The attractive Hubbard model captures the competition between superconductivity/superfluidity and charge-density-wave order, and the kagome lattice's Dirac points may host exotic correlated phases.
method: Zero-temperature auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations are performed on the kagome-lattice attractive Hubbard model across several electronic fillings.
result: At the Van Hove-like filling influenced by the Dirac point at the Fermi energy, a superfluid phase emerges that is not accompanied by charge order.
conclusion: The kagome geometry can stabilize superfluidity decoupled from charge-density-wave ordering, suggesting a distinct correlated ground state worth further exploration.

title: Solving Conic Programs Over Sparse Graphs Using A Variational Quantum Approach: The Case Of The Ac Optimal Power Flow
authors: Thinh Viet Le, Mark M. Wilde, And Vassilis Kekatos
abstract:
Author(s): Thinh Viet Le, Mark M. Wilde, and Vassilis Kekatos

Conic programs arising in physics, quantum information, machine learning, and engineering are oftentimes defined over sparse graphs. Although such problems can be solved in polynomial time using classical interior-point solvers, the computational complexity scales unfavorably with the graph size. In…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042413] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A variational quantum algorithm is proposed to solve conic programs defined over sparse graphs, demonstrated on the AC optimal power flow problem.
motivation: Conic programs over sparse graphs scale unfavorably with graph size when solved by classical interior-point methods, motivating a quantum approach.
method: The authors formulate a variational quantum algorithm that exploits sparse graph structure to represent and solve conic optimization problems, applying it to AC optimal power flow.
result: The variational quantum approach is shown to handle sparse conic programs, including instances arising in power systems, though practical quantum advantage remains to be demonstrated.
conclusion: The work connects variational quantum algorithms to conic optimization over sparse graphs, suggesting a route to quantum-enhanced optimization but remaining largely applied in scope.

title: Néel-Antiferromagnet-Proximitized Superconductivity In The ${\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}/{\text{MnPS}}_{3}$ Heterostructures
authors: Xinyi Zheng, Ruihuan Duan, Xilin Feng, Desheng Wu, Xue Yang, Lihong Hu, Lei Xu, Sicheng Zhou, Siyuan Zhou, Ximing Zhang, Zishuo Peng, Bingbing Tong, Peiling Li, Junya Feng, Zhaozheng Lyu, Hua Ke, Jie Shen, Jianlin Luo, Fanming Qu, Zheng Liu, Kam Tuen Law, Guangtong Liu, And Li Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyi Zheng, Ruihuan Duan, Xilin Feng, Desheng Wu, Xue Yang, Lihong Hu, Lei Xu, Sicheng Zhou, Siyuan Zhou, Ximing Zhang, Zishuo Peng, Bingbing Tong, Peiling Li, Junya Feng, Zhaozheng Lyu, Hua Ke, Jie Shen, Jianlin Luo, Fanming Qu, Zheng Liu, Kam Tuen Law, Guangtong Liu, and Li Lu

Antiferromagnet-superconductor (AFM-SC) hybrids offer a rich but largely unexplored platform for realizing spin-triplet Cooper pairing and chiral topological superconductivity, yet experimental demonstrations remain scarce. Here, we report the modification of superconductivity in ${}_{2…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156301] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports proximity-modified superconductivity in NbSe2/MnPS3 heterostructures, where an antiferromagnet induces signatures consistent with spin-triplet and possibly chiral topological pairing.
motivation: Antiferromagnet-superconductor hybrids are promising platforms for spin-triplet Cooper pairing and chiral topological superconductivity, but experimental realizations have been scarce.
method: The authors fabricate NbSe2/MnPS3 heterostructures and perform transport measurements to probe how the antiferromagnetic proximity effect modifies the superconducting state.
result: They observe modification of superconductivity in the heterostructure, with signatures attributed to spin-triplet pairing and chiral topological superconducting behavior.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental demonstration that AFM-SC hybrids can host unconventional topological superconductivity, motivating further study of such platforms.

title: First-order Maxwell Operator Formalism For Macroscopic Quantum Electrodynamics With Open Dielectric Boundaries
authors: Ishita Agarwal, Ankit Kundu, Christian M. Lange, And Jonathan D. Hood
abstract:
Author(s): Ishita Agarwal, Ankit Kundu, Christian M. Lange, and Jonathan D. Hood

Macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (QED) describes light-matter interactions in dispersive, absorptive media. The Green's function propagates the field and noise operators arising from material absorption account for quantum fluctuations. Standard macroscopic QED represents the field through bulk n…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043711] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a first-order Maxwell operator formalism for macroscopic quantum electrodynamics with open dielectric boundaries.
motivation: Standard macroscopic QED formulations based on bulk normal modes can be inconvenient for open dielectric structures, motivating a more general operator approach.
method: The authors develop a first-order Maxwell operator formalism to describe field propagation and quantum fluctuations in dispersive, absorptive media with open boundaries.
result: The formalism provides a systematic framework for treating light-matter interactions and noise operators in dielectric environments with open boundaries.
conclusion: This approach may simplify calculations for macroscopic QED in complex dielectric systems, though its direct relevance to quantum information science is limited.

title: High-resolution Spectroscopy Of Ionic-core Transitions In Alkaline-earth-metal Rydberg Atoms
authors: Mitsuki Odahara And Shinsuke Haze
abstract:
Author(s): Mitsuki Odahara and Shinsuke Haze

We report high-resolution spectroscopy of ionic-core transitions in alkaline-earth-metal Rydberg atoms. We perform high-resolution measurements of isotope shifts and the hyperfine splitting of dipole transitions in the ionic core. A key element of this work is the reduction of the linewidth by more …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042803] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports high-resolution spectroscopy of ionic-core transitions in alkaline-earth-metal Rydberg atoms, measuring isotope shifts and hyperfine splittings with reduced linewidth.
motivation: Precise knowledge of ionic-core transitions in Rydberg atoms is important for understanding atomic structure and for applications in precision metrology and quantum technologies.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on alkaline-earth-metal Rydberg atoms, reducing the linewidth to measure isotope shifts and hyperfine splitting of dipole transitions in the ionic core.
result: They obtain high-resolution measurements of isotope shifts and hyperfine splittings, demonstrating reduced linewidths for these ionic-core transitions.
conclusion: The results provide benchmark spectroscopic data for alkaline-earth-metal Rydberg atoms, potentially useful for refining atomic theory and future precision measurements.

title: Emergence Of Magnetic Excitations In One-dimensional Quantum Mixtures Under Confinement
authors: P. Capuzzi, P. Vignolo, A. Minguzzi, And S. Musolino
abstract:
Author(s): P. Capuzzi, P. Vignolo, A. Minguzzi, and S. Musolino

We obtain an exact solution for the spectral function for one-dimensional Bose-Bose and Fermi-Fermi mixtures with strong repulsive interactions, valid in arbitrary confining potentials and at all frequency scales. For the case of harmonic confinement, we show that, on top of the ladder structure of …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033370] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: An exact solution for the spectral function of strongly repulsive one-dimensional Bose-Bose and Fermi-Fermi mixtures in arbitrary confining potentials reveals the emergence of magnetic (spin) excitations in harmonically trapped systems.
motivation: One-dimensional quantum mixtures with strong repulsive interactions host rich many-body physics, but their excitation spectra in realistic confining potentials are difficult to access theoretically and experimentally.
method: The authors derive an exact spectral function valid for arbitrary confinement and all frequency scales by exploiting the integrable structure of strongly repulsive 1D mixtures, then specialize to the harmonic trap case.
result: Beyond the usual ladder structure of the spectrum, new magnetic (spin-flip-like) excitation branches emerge in the confined mixture, with signatures that depend on the trapping geometry.
conclusion: The exact spectral function provides a benchmark for spectroscopic probes of 1D cold-atom mixtures and clarifies how confinement reshapes their excitation spectrum.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions In Nonreciprocal Living Matter
authors: Hyunseok Lee, Eliseanne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunseok Lee, EliseAnne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, and Nikta Fakhri

Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031061] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a topological flowscape framework to characterize nonreciprocal dynamics and state transitions in living matter far from equilibrium.
motivation: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, and understanding nonreciprocity and self-organization in such active matter requires new theoretical tools beyond standard equilibrium descriptions.
method: The authors develop a topological flowscape approach that maps nonreciprocal flows onto topological structures to identify and classify state transitions in experimental living systems.
result: The framework reveals distinct state transitions and nonreciprocal flow patterns in living matter, linking topological features of the flowscape to biological self-organization.
conclusion: Topological flowscape analysis provides a general lens for probing nonreciprocal physics in active and living matter, bridging topology, nonequilibrium physics, and biology.

title: Removing Nodal And Support-Mismatch Pathologies In Variational Monte Carlo Via Blurred Sampling
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, And Shiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, and Shiwei Zhang

A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031059] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo postprocessing technique called blurred sampling removes infinite-variance and systematic-bias pathologies in variational quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) is a leading numerical approach for strongly correlated quantum many-body systems, but nodal and support-mismatch issues introduce infinite variance and systematic bias that degrade accuracy and convergence.
method: The authors introduce 'blurred sampling,' a Monte Carlo postprocessing procedure that smooths the sampling distribution to eliminate nodal and support-mismatch pathologies within the VMC framework.
result: Blurred sampling is shown to remove infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations, improving the reliability of variational energy estimates.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical fix for long-standing numerical issues in VMC, though the contribution is a computational many-body method rather than a quantum-information or thermodynamics result.

title: Imaginary Time Evolution And Ground State Preparation Using Unitary Multi-Copy Protocols
authors: Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, And H. R. Sadeghpour
abstract:
Author(s): Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, and H. R. Sadeghpour

Real-time evolution and sᴡᴀᴘ operations are combined to efficiently suppress excited-state populations using multiple copies of the quantum system.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033033] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unitary multi-copy protocol combining real-time evolution and swap operations to suppress excited-state populations for ground state preparation.
motivation: Ground state preparation is essential for quantum simulation and many-body physics, but imaginary time evolution is non-unitary and challenging to implement on quantum devices.
method: The authors use multiple copies of the quantum system and combine unitary real-time evolution with swap operations to effectively realize imaginary time evolution.
result: The protocol efficiently suppresses excited-state populations, enabling ground state preparation without non-unitary operations.
conclusion: This work provides a viable unitary approach to ground state preparation, potentially useful for near-term quantum devices.

title: Energy- And Momentum-Resolved Single-Shot Yield Fluctuations In Bright-Squeezed-Vacuum-Driven Atomic Strong-Field Ionization
authors: Haodong Liu, Xiaoxiao Long, Peizeng Li, And Yunquan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Haodong Liu, Xiaoxiao Long, Peizeng Li, and Yunquan Liu

When intense quantum light knocks electrons out of atoms, the statistics of the light can be transferred to the electrons.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 153201] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper measures energy- and momentum-resolved single-shot yield fluctuations in atomic strong-field ionization driven by bright squeezed vacuum, showing that quantum-light statistics imprint on electron emission.
motivation: To understand how the quantum fluctuations of intense squeezed light are transferred to strong-field ionization and the resulting electron statistics.
method: Atomic strong-field ionization is driven by bright squeezed vacuum, and single-shot photoelectron yields are recorded with energy and momentum resolution.
result: Correlated fluctuations in ionization yield and electron distributions are observed, reflecting the photon-number statistics of the driving squeezed vacuum.
conclusion: Quantum-light statistics can be mapped onto strong-field ionization, offering a route to probe quantum optical correlations in atomic processes.

title: Fractional Incompressible Phases And Ordering Competition In Tilted Dipolar Bosons With Cavity-mediated Interactions
authors: Fang-Ru Jin And Ji-Guo Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Fang-Ru Jin and Ji-Guo Wang

We investigate the ground-state phase structure of tilted dipolar bosons in a two-dimensional square optical lattice in the presence of cavity-mediated global interactions. Our analysis is based primarily on the single-site Gutzwiller mean-field (SGMF) method, supplemented by representative [MATH] cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043303] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: A Gutzwiller mean-field study of the ground-state phase diagram of tilted dipolar bosons in a square optical lattice with cavity-mediated global interactions, revealing fractional incompressible phases and ordering competition.
motivation: Cavity-mediated interactions provide a tunable long-range global coupling that can compete with the dipolar and lattice physics, motivating the exploration of novel many-body phases such as fractional incompressible states.
method: Single-site Gutzwiller mean-field (SGMF) calculations, supplemented by representative exact or perturbative checks, are used to map the ground-state phase structure as a function of tilt and interaction parameters.
result: The phase diagram exhibits fractional incompressible phases and competition between ordered phases, arising from the interplay of dipolar interactions, lattice tilt, and cavity-mediated global coupling.
conclusion: The work highlights how cavity-mediated interactions can stabilize fractional incompressible phases in tilted dipolar lattice bosons, offering a route to engineer correlated phases of matter.

title: Hybrid Method For Quantum Dynamics Simulation
authors: Niladri Gomes, Jia Yin, Siyuan Niu, Chao Yang, And Wibe Albert de Jong
abstract:
Author(s): Niladri Gomes, Jia Yin, Siyuan Niu, Chao Yang, and Wibe Albert de Jong

We propose a hybrid approach to simulate quantum many-body dynamics by combining the Trotter-based quantum algorithm with classical dynamic mode decomposition. In quantum simulation, the interest often lies in estimating observables rather than explicitly obtaining the wave function. Instead of char…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042609] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical method combines Trotter-based quantum simulation with classical dynamic mode decomposition to estimate observables in quantum many-body dynamics.
motivation: Simulating quantum many-body dynamics often requires estimating observables rather than the full wave function, motivating more efficient hybrid approaches.
method: The authors integrate a Trotter-based quantum algorithm with classical dynamic mode decomposition to simulate dynamics and extract observables.
result: The hybrid method is proposed and likely demonstrated to reduce quantum resources or improve accuracy for observable estimation in many-body dynamics.
conclusion: Hybrid quantum-classical techniques can enable practical quantum dynamics simulations by leveraging classical post-processing alongside quantum evolution.

title: Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquid Theory For One-dimensional Attractive Fermi Gases
authors: Hai-Ying Cui, Yu-Hao Yeh, Aashish Kafle, Randall G. Hulet, Han Pu, Thierry Giamarchi, And Xi-Wen Guan
abstract:
Author(s): Hai-Ying Cui, Yu-Hao Yeh, Aashish Kafle, Randall G. Hulet, Han Pu, Thierry Giamarchi, and Xi-Wen Guan

The one-dimensional (1D) Yang-Gaudin model, an integrable [MATH]-function interacting Fermi gas, serves as a paradigm in quantum many-body physics, encompassing phenomena from spin-charge separation to the Luther-Emery liquid. However, a consistent description of the Luther-Emery liquid and the Fulde-F…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042203] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid description of the 1D attractive Yang-Gaudin Fermi gas, connecting integrable-model results to Luther-Emery liquid and Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov physics.
motivation: The 1D Yang-Gaudin model with attractive interactions is a paradigm of quantum many-body physics, but a unified and consistent description of the Luther-Emery liquid and the FFLO-like regime has been lacking.
method: The authors combine Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid bosonization with exact Bethe-ansatz/integrability results for the delta-function interacting Fermi gas, and compare with cold-atom experiments.
result: They obtain a consistent Luttinger-liquid framework that captures the crossover behavior, identifying the relevant Luttinger parameters and the emergence of the Luther-Emery and FFLO phases in the attractive 1D Fermi gas.
conclusion: The work clarifies the low-energy physics of attractive 1D Fermi gases and provides a benchmark for interpreting ultracold-atom experiments in this integrable regime.

title: Upward Deviation From The Wiedemann-Franz Law And Phonon-dominated Thermal Transport In The Topological Semimetal ${\mathrm{NbP}}_{2}$
authors: Jie Yang, Luyao Zhong, And Xiaolong Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Yang, Luyao Zhong, and Xiaolong Yang

Transition-metal dipnictides [MATH] ([MATH] or Ta and [MATH], Sb, or As) represent a key class of topological semimetals that exhibit rich quantum transport phenomena owing to their nontrivial band topology. However, their thermal transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. H…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204302] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper measures electrical and thermal transport in the topological semimetal NbP2 and finds an upward deviation from the Wiedemann-Franz law attributed to phonon-dominated thermal transport.
motivation: Transition-metal dipnictides are topological semimetals with rich quantum transport behavior, but their thermal transport mechanisms remain poorly understood.
method: Electrical and thermal conductivity measurements on NbP2 single crystals, analyzed via the Wiedemann-Franz law and its deviations to separate electronic and phonon contributions.
result: An upward deviation from the Wiedemann-Franz law is observed, indicating that phonons dominate the thermal transport in this material.
conclusion: The findings clarify the thermal transport mechanisms in transition-metal dipnictides and highlight the role of phonons in these topological semimetals.

title: Collective Dynamics Of Trail-interacting Particles
authors: Paul Pineau, Samuel Bell, Raphaël Voituriez, And Ram M. Adar
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Pineau, Samuel Bell, Raphaël Voituriez, and Ram M. Adar

Trail interactions occur when past particle trajectories bias future motion, rendering the system out of thermodynamic equilibrium. While such systems are abundant in nature, their understanding is limited to the single-particle level or phenomenological mean-field theories. Here, we introduce a min…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042102] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a minimal microscopic model for collective dynamics of particles that interact through the trails they leave behind, a classical non-equilibrium active-matter system.
motivation: Trail-mediated interactions (as in ants, slime molds, or chemotactic bacteria) drive systems far from thermodynamic equilibrium, but existing understanding is limited to single-particle treatments or phenomenological mean-field descriptions.
method: The authors introduce a minimal model of trail-interacting particles and analyze its collective behavior analytically and/or via simulations, moving beyond mean-field approaches.
result: The model reveals collective effects and phase behavior arising from the coupling between particle motion and the dynamically modified environment (trail field).
conclusion: The work provides a tractable framework for understanding collective phenomena governed by trail interactions, extending beyond single-particle and mean-field descriptions.

title: Protocols For A Many-Body Phase Microscope: From Coherences And $d$-Wave Superconductivity To Green’s Functions
authors: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

New protocols allow extracting of relevant many-body observables, such as
[PRX Quantum 7, 033068] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes protocols for a many-body phase microscope that uses quantum gas microscopes to extract observables like coherences, d-wave superconducting order parameters, and Green's functions.
motivation: To enable direct probing of complex many-body phases and superconductivity in cold-atom quantum simulators, going beyond conventional measurement techniques.
method: Develops measurement protocols for state-of-the-art quantum gas microscopes to reconstruct many-body observables from experimental data, including coherences and Green's functions.
result: The protocols allow extraction of relevant many-body observables such as the d-wave superconducting order parameter, demonstrating the microscope's enhanced capabilities.
conclusion: These protocols expand the use of quantum gas microscopes for studying strongly correlated systems, but they do not directly address the researcher's core interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Engineered Diabatic Transition Under Arbitrarily Slow Evolution Via Phase-Difference Manipulation
authors: Oubo You, Zhaoqi Jiang, Jinhui Shi, Qing Dai, Chunying Guan, And Shuang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Oubo You, Zhaoqi Jiang, Jinhui Shi, Qing Dai, Chunying Guan, and Shuang Zhang

The quantum adiabatic theorem, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, asserts that a gapped quantum system remains in its instantaneous eigenstate during sufficiently slow evolution, provided no resonances occur. Here, we show that adiabaticity can be violated even in arbitrarily slow processes. We int…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 150801] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that adiabaticity can be violated even in arbitrarily slow quantum evolution via engineered phase-difference manipulation, enabling diabatic transitions.
motivation: The quantum adiabatic theorem conventionally states that a gapped system remains in its instantaneous eigenstate under sufficiently slow evolution, but the authors question whether this can be circumvented.
method: They engineer diabatic transitions by manipulating phase differences in a slowly evolving quantum system, likely using a theoretical model and possibly experimental or numerical analysis.
result: They demonstrate that adiabaticity breaks down despite arbitrarily slow evolution, producing controlled diabatic transitions through phase-difference engineering.
conclusion: The work challenges the standard adiabatic theorem and suggests new routes for quantum control, with potential implications for adiabatic quantum computing and state manipulation.

title: Nuclear Polarization By Intense Laser Pulses
authors: Hanxu Zhang, Tao Li, And Xu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hanxu Zhang, Tao Li, and Xu Wang

Nuclear polarization plays an essential role in precision measurements, symmetry tests, and emerging quantum technologies, yet efficient polarization of heavy nuclei remains a major challenge. We propose an efficient, intense-laser-based approach that achieves high-efficiency polarization of heavy n…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 152501] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an intense-laser-based method to efficiently polarize heavy nuclei for precision measurements and quantum technologies.
motivation: Efficient nuclear polarization of heavy nuclei is challenging but important for precision measurements, symmetry tests, and emerging quantum technologies.
method: The authors use intense laser pulses to drive an efficient polarization process for heavy nuclei.
result: The approach achieves high-efficiency polarization of heavy nuclei.
conclusion: This laser-based technique may enable improved nuclear polarization for applications in precision metrology and quantum technologies.

title: Probing False Vacuum Decay On A Cold-Atom Gauge-Theory Quantum Simulator
authors: Zi-Hang Zhu, Ying Liu, Gianluca Lagnese, Federica Maria Surace, Wei-Yong Zhang, Ming-Gen He, Jad C. Halimeh, Marcello Dalmonte, Siddhardh C. Morampudi, Frank Wilczek, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Hang Zhu, Ying Liu, Gianluca Lagnese, Federica Maria Surace, Wei-Yong Zhang, Ming-Gen He, Jad C. Halimeh, Marcello Dalmonte, Siddhardh C. Morampudi, Frank Wilczek, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

Researchers observe atoms trapped in an optical lattice mimicking particles created in a strong electric field.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 141601] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Researchers use a cold-atom gauge-theory quantum simulator to observe false vacuum decay, mimicking particle creation in a strong electric field.
motivation: False vacuum decay is a fundamental process in quantum field theory and cosmology, but its real-time dynamics are difficult to study directly.
method: Atoms trapped in an optical lattice are used to simulate a gauge theory, specifically the dynamics of false vacuum decay under a strong electric field.
result: The experiment observes signatures of false vacuum decay, including the creation of particles, in a controllable quantum simulator.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the potential of cold-atom quantum simulators for probing non-perturbative quantum field theory phenomena, though it lies outside the core research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.

title: Deviations From Thermal Light Statistics In Ensembles Of Independent Two-level Emitters
authors: M. Bojer, A. Cidrim, R. Bachelard, And J. von Zanthier
abstract:
Author(s): M. Bojer, A. Cidrim, R. Bachelard, and J. von Zanthier

We investigate the light statistics of an ensemble of independent motionless two-level atoms in a product state. In particular, we explore under which conditions the atomic ensemble produces light similar to that of a classical thermal source obeying the Gaussian moment theorem (GMT). We derive lead…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043710] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies when light emitted by an ensemble of independent two-level atoms reproduces classical thermal light statistics satisfying the Gaussian moment theorem.
motivation: Thermal light sources are fundamental in quantum optics, but the conditions under which an ensemble of independent quantum emitters mimics thermal statistics are not fully understood.
method: The authors model an ensemble of motionless independent two-level atoms in a product state and analytically derive photon-number statistics and correlation functions, comparing them with the Gaussian moment theorem.
result: They identify conditions under which the emitted light deviates from thermal statistics and quantify the breakdown of the Gaussian moment theorem for finite ensembles.
conclusion: The work clarifies the limits of using independent two-level emitters as thermal light sources and provides criteria for observing non-thermal photon statistics.

title: Ionization Energies For Rydberg $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ ($1snp^{1,3}P$) States Using The Correlated B-spline Basis Function Method
authors: Jing Chi, Hao Fang, Yong-Hui Zhang, Li-Yan Tang, And Ting-Yun Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Chi, Hao Fang, Yong-Hui Zhang, Li-Yan Tang, and Ting-Yun Shi

We extend the correlated B-spline basis function (C-BSBF) method to high-precision calculations of the ionization energies of helium Rydberg [MATH] states ([MATH]). Using a unified basis set, we evaluate nonrelativistic energies, relativistic corrections of order [MATH] (including finite-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042804] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the correlated B-spline basis function method to compute high-precision ionization energies for Rydberg 1snp 1,3P states of helium.
