motivation: Accurate ionization energies for helium Rydberg states are important for testing atomic theory and providing benchmark data, but require sophisticated correlated basis methods.
method: The authors use a unified correlated B-spline basis function (C-BSBF) approach to evaluate nonrelativistic energies, relativistic corrections, and finite nuclear mass effects for the 1snp 1,3P states.
result: They obtain high-precision ionization energies for Rydberg helium 4He 1snp 1,3P states, improving agreement with experimental and previous theoretical values.
conclusion: The C-BSBF method is demonstrated to be effective for high-precision calculations of Rydberg state energies, providing useful reference data for helium spectroscopy.

title: Klein Tunneling Of The Laser Coherence
authors: Konstantin Manannikov, Sagie Gadasi, Amit Pando, Ekaterina Mironova, Eran Bernstein, Andrei Poliakov, Nir Davidson, And Alexander N. Poddubny
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantin Manannikov, Sagie Gadasi, Amit Pando, Ekaterina Mironova, Eran Bernstein, Andrei Poliakov, Nir Davidson, and Alexander N. Poddubny

We study theoretically the synchronization of two arrays of coupled lasers with complex mode dispersion, separated by a spectrally detuned barrier in one- and two-dimensional geometries. We demonstrate that when lasing at the Dirac point, the synchronization persists for an order of magnitude higher…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043505] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically studies synchronization of two arrays of coupled lasers with complex mode dispersion separated by a spectrally detuned barrier, demonstrating enhanced synchronization at the Dirac point.
motivation: To understand how robust synchronization and coherence can be maintained across a detuned barrier in coupled laser arrays, drawing on Dirac physics and Klein tunneling analogies.
method: The authors analyze one- and two-dimensional arrays of coupled lasers with complex mode dispersion and a spectrally detuned barrier, comparing synchronization behavior at and away from the Dirac point.
result: Synchronization persists for an order of magnitude higher detuning when lasing at the Dirac point, which the authors interpret as a Klein-tunneling-like effect for laser coherence.
conclusion: Operating at the Dirac point enables barrier-transparent synchronization in coupled laser arrays, with potential implications for robust laser coherence and topological photonic device design.

title: Thermoelastic Limit On The Focal Intensity In Fabry-Pérot Cavities
authors: Jeremy J. Axelrod, Lothar Maisenbacher, Ashwin Singh, Isaac M. Pope, Petar N. Petrov, Jessie T. Zhang, And Holger Müller
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy J. Axelrod, Lothar Maisenbacher, Ashwin Singh, Isaac M. Pope, Petar N. Petrov, Jessie T. Zhang, and Holger Müller

Light in the mode of a Fabry-Pérot cavity heats the mirror surfaces via optical absorption, causing thermoelastic deformation of the mirror substrates, which in turn dictates the shape of the mode. We develop an analytical model which predicts that this effect limits the maximum focal intensity of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043507] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: An analytical model shows that thermoelastic deformation of Fabry-Pérot cavity mirrors limits the maximum achievable focal intensity.
motivation: High-intensity optical cavities are important for precision measurements, but absorption-induced heating and mirror deformation can degrade performance and impose fundamental limits.
method: Develops an analytical thermoelastic model that couples optical absorption, heat diffusion, and elastic deformation of mirror substrates to predict the resulting mode shape and focal intensity.
result: The model predicts a maximum focal intensity set by thermoelastic effects, with scaling determined by cavity and material parameters.
conclusion: Thermoelastic deformation must be accounted for in the design of high-power Fabry-Pérot cavities, and the derived limit provides a guideline for future cavity optimization.

title: Quantum Spectroscopy Of Optical Near Fields Using Low-energy Free-electron Rabi Oscillations In Synthetic Energy Space
authors: Yiming Pan, Bin Zhang, And Daniel Podolsky
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Pan, Bin Zhang, and Daniel Podolsky

We propose an ultrafast free-electron quantum interferometry, facilitating the detection of local electromagnetic fields and plasmonic polaritons using an isolated “two-level” electron. The two-level electron is constructed in a synthetic energy space through laser modulation in the Bragg regime. Th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042202] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes ultrafast free-electron quantum interferometry to detect local electromagnetic fields and plasmonic polaritons using a two-level electron constructed in synthetic energy space via laser modulation.
motivation: Probing local electromagnetic fields at the nanoscale with high spatiotemporal resolution is challenging, and free electrons offer high resolution but often lack quantum coherence.
method: Laser modulation in the Bragg regime creates a synthetic two-level system in the free electron's energy space, enabling Rabi oscillations that act as a quantum interferometer for near-field detection.
result: The scheme allows sensitive detection of local fields and plasmonic polaritons by leveraging the electron's quantum coherence.
conclusion: This approach offers a new platform for quantum spectroscopy of optical near fields, potentially advancing nanoscale field mapping and plasmonics.

title: Lattice Location Of Ion-implanted $^{6}\mathrm{He}$ In Diamond
authors: U. Wahl, J. G. Correia, A. Costa, B. Biesmans, G. Magchiels, S. M. Tunhuma, A. Lamelas, A. Vantomme, And L. M. C. Pereira
abstract:
Author(s): U. Wahl, J. G. Correia, A. Costa, B. Biesmans, G. Magchiels, S. M. Tunhuma, A. Lamelas, A. Vantomme, and L. M. C. Pereira

Understanding the properties of helium in diamond is crucial for geological dating and possible quantum applications. Here, the authors determine the lattice location of ion-implanted short-lived
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194105] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper determines the lattice location of ion-implanted 6He in diamond and estimates its migration energy using β emission channeling.
motivation: Understanding helium behavior in diamond is important for geological dating and potential quantum applications.
method: Ion-implanted short-lived 6He in single-crystal diamond was studied via β emission channeling at temperatures from 30°C to 800°C.
result: 6He preferentially occupies tetrahedral interstitial sites; the migration energy is estimated at 1.63–2.89 eV, implying unbound interstitial helium is unstable over geological timescales.
conclusion: These findings provide key insights for He-based dating methods and may inform future diamond-based quantum applications.

title: Reconstructing Spin Hamiltonians Of Two-dimensional Gutzwiller-projected Wave Functions
authors: Lucas Z. Brito And J. B. Marston
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Z. Brito and J. B. Marston

We apply the correlation matrix Hamiltonian reconstruction technique to the two-dimensional Gutzwiller-projected Fermi sea and [MATH]-flux states on finite-sized square and triangular lattices. Our results indicate no spin Hamiltonian with simple local interaction terms stabilizes such states for finit…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194405] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies correlation matrix Hamiltonian reconstruction to two-dimensional Gutzwiller-projected Fermi sea and pi-flux states, finding no simple local spin Hamiltonian stabilizes them on finite square and triangular lattices.
motivation: To determine whether simple local spin Hamiltonians can stabilize Gutzwiller-projected wave functions, which are relevant to quantum spin liquid candidates and variational ansatz states.
method: Uses the correlation matrix Hamiltonian reconstruction technique on finite-sized square and triangular lattices for Gutzwiller-projected Fermi sea and pi-flux states.
result: No spin Hamiltonian with simple local interaction terms is found to stabilize such states on finite lattices.
conclusion: The reconstructed Hamiltonians lack simple local interactions, suggesting these projected states are not ground states of simple local spin models.

title: Phonon-mediated Spin-spin Interactions
authors: J. Fransson
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fransson

Indirect long-range interactions between localized magnetic moments in metals are mediated by itinerant electrons. In insulators and semiconductors, such interactions cannot be mediated by itinerant electrons; however, delocalized electrons in the valence band may provide such a medium. Nevertheless…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204408] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how phonons can mediate indirect spin-spin interactions in insulators and semiconductors where itinerant electrons are unavailable.
motivation: Long-range magnetic interactions in non-metallic materials cannot be explained by the standard RKKY mechanism, so alternative mediators such as valence-band electrons or phonons need to be understood.
method: The work presents a theoretical analysis of phonon-mediated indirect exchange coupling between localized magnetic moments, likely using a model Hamiltonian approach.
result: The study identifies conditions under which phonons provide an effective medium for long-range spin-spin interactions in insulating or semiconducting systems.
conclusion: Phonon-mediated mechanisms offer a viable route for magnetic coupling in materials lacking itinerant electrons, extending beyond conventional electronic mediation.

title: Current- And Field-driven Domain Wall Dynamics And Chirality Switching In A Planar Helimagnet
authors: Roman Teslia And Oleksiy Kolezhuk
abstract:
Author(s): Roman Teslia and Oleksiy Kolezhuk

We study the effect of electric current and magnetic field on the dynamics of chirality in a helimagnet with a strong easy-plane anisotropy. Using a continuum theory derived for a quasi-one-dimensional frustrated ferromagnet close to the Lifshitz point, we show that a domain wall connecting domains …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214408] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies current- and field-driven domain wall dynamics and chirality switching in a planar helimagnet using a continuum theory.
motivation: Understanding how electric currents and magnetic fields control chirality and domain walls in helimagnets is important for spintronic applications and fundamental magnetism.
method: A continuum theory is derived for a quasi-one-dimensional frustrated ferromagnet near the Lifshitz point, and the dynamics of chirality and domain walls are analyzed under applied current and magnetic field.
result: The study reveals how current and field drive domain wall motion and induce chirality switching, with the Lifshitz point playing a key role in the phase behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide a theoretical basis for controlling chiral domain walls in planar helimagnets, relevant to spintronic device design.

title: Bose-Einstein Condensate Of Magnons In Superfluid $^{3}\mathrm{He}$-B As A Tuned Resonant Quantum Amplifier
authors: M. Človečko, K. Goliaš, O. Podopryhora, M. Skyba, And P. Skyba
abstract:
Author(s): M. Človečko, K. Goliaš, O. Podopryhora, M. Skyba, and P. Skyba

We show that the Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of magnons in superfluid [MATH]-B in the form of a homogeneously precessing domain can be used as a new type of tuned resonant quantum amplifier. The underlying physical principle of the resonant amplification is the violation of the U(1) (c…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214506] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using a Bose-Einstein condensate of magnons in superfluid 3He-B as a tuned resonant quantum amplifier.
motivation: Quantum amplifiers are important for quantum measurement and information processing, motivating the search for new physical amplification mechanisms.
method: The authors analyze a homogeneously precessing domain of magnon BEC in superfluid 3He-B, where resonant amplification arises from violation of the U(1) symmetry.
result: They show that the magnon BEC system can act as a tuned resonant quantum amplifier, with the amplification principle tied to broken U(1) symmetry.
conclusion: The magnon BEC in superfluid 3He-B offers a novel platform for quantum amplification, but its direct relevance to the specified research directions is limited.

title: Quantum-critical Mediation Of Magnetic Order By A Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquid
authors: Hironori Yamaguchi, Sota Monju, Akira Matsuo, Shunsuke C. Furuya, Nicolas Suaud, Koji Araki, Takanori Kida, Masayuki Hagiwara, And Koichi Kindo
abstract:
Author(s): Hironori Yamaguchi, Sota Monju, Akira Matsuo, Shunsuke C. Furuya, Nicolas Suaud, Koji Araki, Takanori Kida, Masayuki Hagiwara, and Koichi Kindo

Quantum-critical many-body states host universal correlations extending across all length scales. Whether these critical correlations merely characterize quantum-critical matter or can actively generate interactions that organize collective order has remained an open question. Here, we establish the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235113] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that quantum-critical Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid correlations can actively mediate magnetic order in a quantum magnet.
motivation: It addresses whether quantum-critical correlations merely characterize critical matter or can actively generate interactions that organize collective order.
method: The study combines experimental magnetic/thermodynamic probes with Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid theory to analyze a quantum-critical many-body system.
result: The authors establish that the critical correlations of a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid mediate magnetic ordering, extending beyond passive characterization.
conclusion: Quantum criticality can play an organizing role in collective magnetic order, linking critical many-body states to emergent ordering.

title: Site-selective Renormalization And Competing Magnetic Instabilities In Paramagnetic ${\mathrm{Y}}_{3}{\mathrm{Cu}}_{2}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{14}$
authors: Yanpeng Zhou And Gang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yanpeng Zhou and Gang Li

Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are exotic phases of matter characterized by long-range entanglement and the absence of magnetic order even at zero temperature. Here, we present a comprehensive theoretical study of the frustrated magnet ${}_{3}{}_{2}{}_{3}{}_{14…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235110] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a theoretical study of the frustrated magnet Y3Cu2Sb3O14, revealing site-selective renormalization and competing magnetic instabilities in a quantum spin liquid candidate.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic phases with long-range entanglement and no magnetic order, motivating detailed understanding of candidate materials and their magnetic instabilities.
method: A comprehensive theoretical analysis, likely involving renormalization group or related many-body techniques, is applied to the frustrated magnet Y3Cu2Sb3O14.
result: The study identifies site-selective renormalization effects and competing magnetic instabilities that characterize the paramagnetic state of this material.
conclusion: These findings provide insights into the magnetic behavior of Y3Cu2Sb3O14 and contribute to the broader understanding of quantum spin liquid physics.

title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis Constraints For Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: G. Shankar And Joseph Maciejko
abstract:
Author(s): G. Shankar and Joseph Maciejko

The Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem powerfully constrains the low-energy behavior of quantum many-body systems. In spin systems with spin rotation and conventional (Euclidean) lattice translation symmetries, it forbids a unique, gapped, symmetric ground state at half-odd-integer spin per unit cell. Here, the authors generalize this theorem to hyperbolic lattices — synthetic structures that emulate negatively curved space. Unlike Euclidean lattice translations, hyperbolic translations are noncommutative. By adapting a flux-threading argument, the authors derive LSM constraints on gapped phases of hyperbolic quantum matter.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245110] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the Lieb-Schultz-Mattis theorem to hyperbolic lattices, deriving constraints on gapped quantum phases using a flux-threading argument.
motivation: The Lieb-Schultz-Mattis theorem powerfully constrains quantum many-body systems with Euclidean lattice symmetries, but its extension to hyperbolic lattices, which feature noncommutative translations, is important for understanding quantum matter in negatively curved spaces.
method: The authors adapt the flux-threading argument to hyperbolic lattices by incorporating noncommutative magnetic translations and analyzing the action of fluxes on the ground state.
conclusion: The work opens a new avenue for studying quantum many-body physics on hyperbolic lattices, with potential connections to holography and quantum error correction.

title: Many-body Euler Topology
authors: Axel Fünfhaus, Titus Neupert, Thilo Kopp, And Roser Valentí
abstract:
Author(s): Axel Fünfhaus, Titus Neupert, Thilo Kopp, and Roser Valentí

The authors introduce here many-body Euler numbers as a counterpart to many-body Chern numbers to diagnose the spontaneous breaking of time reversal symmetry in (fractional) Chern insulators. In addition, a classification scheme to realize different topological phases in interacting systems using symmetry indicators is laid out.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231104] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: Introduces many-body Euler numbers as topological invariants to diagnose spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking in (fractional) Chern insulators and provides a symmetry-indicator classification for interacting topological phases.
motivation: Many-body Chern numbers are standard for characterizing topological order, but a counterpart sensitive to time-reversal symmetry breaking is needed for interacting systems.
method: Defines many-body Euler numbers and uses symmetry indicators to classify topological phases in interacting systems.
result: The proposed invariants diagnose spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking in (fractional) Chern insulators and enable a classification scheme for interacting topological phases.
conclusion: Many-body Euler topology offers a new tool for characterizing topological phases in interacting condensed-matter systems.

title: Phase Transitions In A $p$-spin Glass Model: A Numerical Study
authors: Prerak Gupta, Auditya Sharma, Bharadwaj Vedula, J. Yeo, And M. A. Moore
abstract:
Author(s): Prerak Gupta, Auditya Sharma, Bharadwaj Vedula, J. Yeo, and M. A. Moore

Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations of
[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044116] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations of p-spin glass models find no evidence of replica symmetry breaking, suggesting that three-dimensional structural glasses lack a finite-temperature thermodynamic phase transition.
motivation: To test whether mean-field spin glass phase transitions survive in finite dimensions and to clarify whether the glass transition is thermodynamic or purely dynamical.
method: Numerical Monte Carlo simulations of p-spin glass models, analyzing signatures of phase transitions and replica symmetry breaking.
result: No evidence of replica symmetry breaking is observed, suggesting the absence of a finite-temperature thermodynamic phase transition in three-dimensional structural glasses.
conclusion: The findings challenge mean-field predictions and support the view that the glass transition may be a purely dynamical phenomenon rather than a thermodynamic phase transition.

title: Competition Between Nonlinearity And Inhomogeneities In Discrete-time Quantum Walks
authors: N. Amaral, A. R. C. Buarque, And W. S. Dias
abstract:
Author(s): N. Amaral, A. R. C. Buarque, and W. S. Dias

We investigate the competition between nonlinearity and inhomogeneities in discrete-time quantum walks on one-dimensional lattices and their impact on transport and localization. Nonlinear effects are introduced through a Kerr-like, intensity-dependent local phase, while spatial and temporal inhomog…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044203] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how Kerr-like nonlinearity competes with spatial and temporal inhomogeneities in discrete-time quantum walks, affecting transport and localization.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between nonlinear effects and disorder is important for controlling quantum walk dynamics in complex media.
method: The authors introduce an intensity-dependent local phase and inhomogeneities into a one-dimensional discrete-time quantum walk, then analyze the resulting transport and localization behavior.
result: The competition between nonlinearity and inhomogeneities leads to distinct transport and localization regimes, with nonlinearity and disorder jointly shaping the walk's spreading.
conclusion: The findings clarify how nonlinearity and inhomogeneities can be tuned to control quantum walk dynamics, with potential implications for quantum simulation and transport.

title: Encounter Times Of Random Walkers With Simultaneous Resetting On Networks
authors: Cristian D. Suarez-Jimenez, Alejandro P. Riascos, And Denis Boyer
abstract:
Author(s): Cristian D. Suarez-Jimenez, Alejandro P. Riascos, and Denis Boyer

In this work, we study the dynamics of multiple random walkers on networks subject to a simultaneous resetting protocol, whereby all walkers are synchronously returned to their respective initial nodes. For this collective Markovian process, we derive exact analytical expressions for the mean first-…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044306] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper analytically studies encounter times of multiple random walkers on networks under a simultaneous resetting protocol.
motivation: Random walks with resetting are important stochastic processes, but collective effects of multiple walkers resetting simultaneously are less understood.
method: The authors derive exact analytical expressions for mean first-encounter times within a collective Markovian process where all walkers synchronously return to their initial nodes.
result: Exact formulas for encounter times are obtained and analyzed on networks, revealing how simultaneous resetting affects the dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding collective resetting in random walk systems, with potential applications in network search and transport.

title: Microscopic Mechanism Of High-temperature Superconductivity Revealed By ab Initio Studies On Hole-doped Multilayer Cuprates ${\mathrm{HgBa}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ca}}_{2}{\mathrm{Cu}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{8}$ Under Pressure
authors: Ryui Kaneko And Masatoshi Imada
abstract:
Author(s): Ryui Kaneko and Masatoshi Imada

Triple-layer cuprate superconductor [MATH] (Hg1223) keeps the record of the highest superconducting (SC) critical temperature [MATH] among all the existing materials at ambient pres…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043024] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: Ab initio calculations reveal the microscopic pairing mechanism underlying the record high superconducting critical temperature in hole-doped triple-layer cuprate HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8 under pressure.
motivation: Cuprates such as Hg1223 hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperature, yet the microscopic origin of high-temperature superconductivity remains unresolved.
method: First-principles (ab initio) electronic-structure calculations are applied to hole-doped multilayer cuprate HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8 under applied pressure.
result: The calculations identify the microscopic mechanism governing the enhanced superconducting pairing and elevated critical temperature in this pressure-tuned multilayer cuprate.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic, materials-specific explanation of high-temperature superconductivity in hole-doped multilayer cuprates, advancing understanding of the cuprate pairing mechanism.

title: Interacting Electronic Topology Of Nonlocal Crystals
authors: Shu Hamanaka, Martina O. Soldini, Tsuneya Yoshida, And Titus Neupert
abstract:
Author(s): Shu Hamanaka, Martina O. Soldini, Tsuneya Yoshida, and Titus Neupert

Nonlocal crystals are systems with translational symmetry but arbitrary-range couplings or interactions between degrees of freedom. We argue that such systems can realize symmetry-allowed but locality-forbidden ground-state symmetry eigenvalues. This is demonstrated by constructing an exactly solvab…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043012] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces nonlocal crystals with arbitrary-range couplings and shows they can realize symmetry-allowed but locality-forbidden ground-state symmetry eigenvalues, revealing a new interacting electronic topology.
motivation: To explore how relaxing locality constraints in crystals with translational symmetry affects the classification and realization of topological phases.
method: The authors construct exactly solvable models of nonlocal crystals with translational symmetry and arbitrary-range couplings, then analyze the resulting ground-state symmetry eigenvalues and topological properties.
result: They find that such systems can exhibit ground-state symmetry eigenvalues that are allowed by symmetry but forbidden by locality, demonstrating an interacting electronic topology beyond conventional local Hamiltonians.
conclusion: Nonlocal crystals expand the landscape of possible topological phases by enabling locality-forbidden symmetry eigenvalues, with implications for understanding topology in systems with long-range interactions.

title: Noise Fingerprints Of Magnon Scattering Channels
authors: Yuri Nishiwaki, Shoki Nezu, And Koji Sekiguchi
abstract:
Author(s): Yuri Nishiwaki, Shoki Nezu, and Koji Sekiguchi

We show that low-frequency magnonic noise provides statistical fingerprints of nonlinear scattering-network configurations in a yttrium iron garnet waveguide. By tuning the magnetic field, we control whether three-magnon splitting and confluence are kinematically allowed and change the active scatte…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043014] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Low-frequency magnonic noise in a YIG waveguide provides statistical fingerprints of nonlinear three-magnon scattering channels controlled by magnetic field.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear magnon scattering is important for magnonic devices, and noise spectroscopy can reveal underlying scattering network configurations.
method: The authors measure low-frequency noise in a YIG waveguide while tuning the magnetic field to allow or forbid three-magnon splitting and confluence, analyzing the statistical fingerprints.
result: The noise statistics change with magnetic field, reflecting the active scattering channels and providing fingerprints of nonlinear scattering-network configurations.
conclusion: Magnonic noise can be used as a probe of nonlinear scattering processes in yttrium iron garnet, with potential for characterizing magnonic systems.

title: Compressible Navier-Stokes Flow In Schrödinger-type Variables
authors: James R. Beattie, Max Sokolova, Khush Negandhi, And Bart Ripperda
abstract:
Author(s): James R. Beattie, Max Sokolova, Khush Negandhi, and Bart Ripperda

Fluid equations are nonlinear, dissipative, and non-Hamiltonian, which makes their relation to Schrödinger evolution and quantum algorithms nontrivial. We derive an exact Eulerian Cole-Hopf-type reformulation of isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes (NS) flow in Schrödinger-type amplitude variables.…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033383] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an exact Eulerian Cole-Hopf-type reformulation of isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes flow in Schrödinger-type amplitude variables, exploring a connection to Schrödinger evolution and quantum algorithms.
motivation: Fluid equations are nonlinear, dissipative, and non-Hamiltonian, which makes their relationship to Schrödinger evolution and quantum algorithms nontrivial; the authors aim to bridge this gap via a transformation.
method: They introduce and derive an exact Eulerian Cole-Hopf-type reformulation of isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes flow using Schrödinger-type amplitude variables.
result: An exact reformulation is obtained, casting the compressible Navier-Stokes equations into a Schrödinger-like form in amplitude variables.
conclusion: This reformulation may offer a mathematical route to connect compressible fluid flow with Schrödinger evolution and quantum algorithmic frameworks, though direct quantum information applications remain unclear.

title: Middle-range-energy Structures In Ti ${L}_{2,3}\text{−}\mathrm{edge}$ X-ray Absorption Spectra Of Titanium Oxides
authors: Saki Imada, Yves Joly, And Frank M. F. de Groot
abstract:
Author(s): Saki Imada, Yves Joly, and Frank M. F. de Groot

The Ti [MATH] x-ray absorption spectra of various titanium oxides, including perovskite [MATH], rutile and anatase [MATH], and ilmenite [MATH], are analyzed with particular attention to the energy rang…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033377] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: A spectroscopic study analyzing middle-range-energy structures in Ti L2,3-edge X-ray absorption spectra of various titanium oxides (perovskite, rutile, anatase, ilmenite).
motivation: Titanium oxides exhibit diverse electronic and structural properties, and understanding their X-ray absorption fine structure is important for interpreting valence and local coordination in these materials.
method: Ti L2,3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy is measured and analyzed, likely complemented by multiplet ligand-field or ab initio simulations, focusing on the middle-range-energy region of the spectra across several titanium oxide polymorphs.
result: The study identifies and interprets spectral features in the middle-energy range, linking them to electronic structure, crystal-field effects, and site symmetry differences among perovskite, rutile, anatase, and ilmenite phases.
conclusion: The work clarifies the origin of middle-range-energy features in Ti L2,3-edge XAS, providing a reference for characterizing titanium oxide compounds spectroscopically.

title: Learning Parameter Curves In Feedback-based Quantum Algorithms
authors: Vicente Peña Pérez, Matthew D. Grace, Christian Arenz, And Alicia B. Magann
abstract:
Author(s): Vicente Peña Pérez, Matthew D. Grace, Christian Arenz, and Alicia B. Magann

Feedback-based quantum algorithms (FQAs) operate by iteratively growing a quantum circuit to optimize a given task. At each step, feedback from qubit measurements is used to inform the next quantum circuit update. In practice, the sampling cost associated with these measurements can be significant. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033378] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces learning parameter curves to reduce the measurement sampling cost in feedback-based quantum algorithms.
motivation: Feedback-based quantum algorithms iteratively grow a quantum circuit using qubit measurement feedback, but the repeated measurements incur significant sampling overhead in practice.
method: The authors propose learning parameter curves that predict optimal circuit parameters as a function of iteration, allowing updates to be informed without costly re-sampling at every step.
result: The learned parameter curves are shown to lower the number of required measurements while preserving the algorithm's optimization performance.
conclusion: Learning parameter curves offers a practical path to more efficient and scalable feedback-based quantum algorithms.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, revealing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries produce generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated pyrochlore magnets.
motivation: Frustrated magnets hosting higher-multipole moments are poorly understood beyond dipolar spin-liquid paradigms, motivating a systematic study of how quadrupolar degrees of freedom organize on the pyrochlore lattice.
method: Quantum quadrupoles are treated as biaxial tensors within a semiclassical framework, and the resulting angular-momentum-dependent geometries are analyzed to classify possible ordered and disordered phases.
result: The analysis identifies generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin-liquid states whose character is dictated by the underlying geometry of the frustrated lattice.
conclusion: Quadrupolar frustration on the pyrochlore lattice provides a distinct route to generalized spin liquids, extending the physics of frustrated magnetism beyond conventional dipolar models.

title: Nonuniform Thermal Conductivity In Nanoscale Multiple Hotspot Systems
authors: Yu He (何昱), Zhihao Zhou (周志豪), Shixian Liu (刘世贤), Jing-Tao Lü (吕京涛), Lina Yang (杨哩娜), And Nuo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu He (何昱), Zhihao Zhou (周志豪), Shixian Liu (刘世贤), Jing-Tao Lü (吕京涛), Lina Yang (杨哩娜), and Nuo Yang (杨诺)

Nanoscale hotspot thermal transport is critical for thermal management of electronic devices. Here, the thermal transport in nanoscale multiple hotspots is investigated by solving the phonon Boltzmann transport equation. To address the limitations of the conventional black-box treatment, a formal lo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156303] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies nonuniform thermal conductivity in nanoscale systems with multiple hotspots using the phonon Boltzmann transport equation.
motivation: Nanoscale hotspot thermal transport is critical for thermal management of electronic devices, but conventional black-box treatments have limitations.
method: The authors solve the phonon Boltzmann transport equation to model thermal transport in nanoscale multiple-hotspot systems.
result: They uncover nonuniform thermal conductivity behavior arising from the multiple hotspot configuration.
conclusion: The findings provide a formal local description that could improve nanoscale thermal management, though they lie outside quantum information and information thermodynamics.

title: Non-Ohmic To Ohmic Crossover In The Breakdown Of The Quantum Hall States In Graphene Under Broadband Excitations
authors: Torsten Röper, Aifei Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Olivier Maillet, François D. Parmentier, And Erwann Bocquillon
abstract:
Author(s): Torsten Röper, Aifei Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Olivier Maillet, François D. Parmentier, and Erwann Bocquillon

Graphene, through the coexistence of large cyclotron gaps and small spin and valley gaps, offers the possibility to study the breakdown of the quantum Hall effect (QHE) across a wide range of energy scales. In this Letter, we investigate the breakdown of the QHE in high-mobility graphene Corbino dev…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156602] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the breakdown of the quantum Hall effect in high-mobility graphene Corbino devices under broadband microwave excitations, observing a crossover from non-Ohmic to Ohmic behavior.
motivation: Graphene's large cyclotron gaps coexisting with small spin and valley gaps make it an ideal platform to probe quantum Hall breakdown across a wide range of energy scales, which is not accessible in conventional semiconductor heterostructures.
method: Transport measurements on high-mobility graphene Corbino devices under broadband (on-chip) excitation, analyzing the current-voltage characteristics as a function of microwave power and filling factor to characterize the breakdown regime.
result: The breakdown of quantum Hall states exhibits a crossover from non-Ohmic to Ohmic conduction as excitation power increases, reflecting the interplay between bulk and edge excitation mechanisms across different energy gaps.
conclusion: The observations clarify the energy-scale-dependent breakdown physics of quantum Hall states in graphene, but the work is a condensed-matter transport study without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Symmetric Mass Generation As A Multicritical Point With Enhanced Symmetry
authors: Sandip Maiti, Debasish Banerjee, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, And Marina K. Marinkovic
abstract:
Author(s): Sandip Maiti, Debasish Banerjee, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, and Marina K. Marinkovic

We explore the phase diagram of a lattice fermion model that exhibits three distinct phases: a massless fermion phase, a massive fermion phase with spontaneous symmetry breaking induced by a fermion bilinear condensate, and a massive fermion phase with symmetric mass generation. Using the fermion-ba…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 151601] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A lattice fermion model is shown to realize symmetric mass generation as a multicritical point with enhanced symmetry, separating massless, symmetry-broken massive, and symmetric massive phases.
motivation: Symmetric mass generation is a subtle mechanism for generating fermion masses without spontaneous symmetry breaking, and understanding its phase-diagram structure is important for lattice field theory and condensed matter.
method: The authors study a lattice fermion model using fermion-bag or related numerical/analytic techniques to map out its phase diagram and identify the multicritical point.
result: They find three distinct phases—massless fermions, symmetry-broken massive fermions, and symmetric-mass-generated massive fermions—with the symmetric mass generation phase emerging at a multicritical point featuring enhanced symmetry.
conclusion: The work clarifies the critical nature of symmetric mass generation and suggests that enhanced symmetry at the multicritical point governs the transition between massless and massive symmetric phases.

title: Mirrorless Unidirectional Lasing With Inversionless Gain In Asymmetric Ladder Atomic Bragg Lattices
authors: Xinfu Zheng, Chen Peng, Duanfu Chen, Hanxiao Zhang, Dong Yan, And Hong Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xinfu Zheng, Chen Peng, Duanfu Chen, Hanxiao Zhang, Dong Yan, and Hong Yang

Direction-selective distributed feedback can bring weak optical gain to the threshold of mirrorless reflection-type nonreciprocal lasing. We demonstrate this mechanism in a one-dimensional asymmetric Bragg atomic lattice of coherently driven, incoherently pumped ladder-type atoms. The pump controls …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043712] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and demonstrates mirrorless unidirectional lasing using inversionless gain in an asymmetric ladder-type atomic Bragg lattice with direction-selective distributed feedback.
motivation: To realize nonreciprocal lasing without mirrors by exploiting weak optical gain and direction-selective feedback in an atomic lattice.
method: A one-dimensional asymmetric Bragg atomic lattice of coherently driven, incoherently pumped ladder-type atoms is used, where the pump controls the gain and distributed feedback.
result: Direction-selective distributed feedback brings weak optical gain to the threshold of mirrorless reflection-type nonreciprocal lasing.
conclusion: The mechanism demonstrates mirrorless unidirectional lasing with inversionless gain in an asymmetric atomic Bragg lattice.

title: Orbital-selective Engineering Of Strain-tunable Chern Insulators In Momentum Space
authors: Jin Gao, Rongrong Chen, Lei Yang, Chenglong Jia, Li Xi, Desheng Xue, Kun Tao, Zixiong Huang, And Dingzhao Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jin Gao, Rongrong Chen, Lei Yang, ChengLong Jia, Li Xi, Desheng Xue, Kun Tao, Zixiong Huang, and Dingzhao Liu

Unlike conventional approaches where topological order is statically fixed, we demonstrate that biaxial strain can independently modulate topological order and functional responses in a Tc-adsorbed penta-hexa-silicene monolayer. Combining first-principles calculations and tight-binding models, we es…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214409] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: First-principles and tight-binding study showing that biaxial strain can independently tune topological order and functional responses in a Tc-adsorbed penta-hexa-silicene monolayer, realizing a strain-tunable Chern insulator in momentum space.
motivation: Conventional topological order is usually statically fixed by material composition and structure, limiting its tunability for applications; the authors aim to show that mechanical strain can serve as an independent, orbital-selective control knob for topological phases.
method: Density functional theory (first-principles) calculations combined with tight-binding modeling are used to compute band structures, orbital contributions, and Chern numbers of a Tc-adsorbed penta-hexa-silicene monolayer under biaxial strain.
result: Biaxial strain is found to modulate the topological order and associated functional responses in an orbital-selective manner, enabling a strain-controlled transition into a Chern insulating phase.
conclusion: Strain engineering provides a viable route to dynamically and selectively control topological order in two-dimensional materials, opening prospects for tunable topological electronic devices.

title: Unified Interfacial And Intrinsic Topology In A Large-gap Epitaxial Two-dimensional Insulator
authors: Heng Jin, Xiaoyin Li, Kyung-Hwan Jin, Bing Huang, And Feng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Heng Jin, Xiaoyin Li, Kyung-Hwan Jin, Bing Huang, and Feng Liu

Two-dimensional topological insulators (2D TIs) are commonly realized either through intrinsic band-gap inversion within a single material or through interfacial band-offset inversion in narrowly tuned heterostructures. Here we demonstrate, based on first-principles calculations, that these two mech…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235111] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study demonstrating a large-gap epitaxial 2D topological insulator where interfacial band-offset inversion and intrinsic band-gap inversion mechanisms are unified in a single heterostructure.
motivation: 2D topological insulators have typically required either intrinsic band inversion within one material or narrowly tuned interfacial band-offset inversion in heterostructures, making robust large-gap realizations difficult.
method: Density functional theory (first-principles) calculations of an epitaxially grown 2D insulator heterostructure, analyzing band structures, band inversion, and topological invariants.
result: The authors show that a single epitaxial 2D system can simultaneously exhibit both interfacial and intrinsic band-inversion topology, yielding a large topological gap.
conclusion: Unifying interfacial and intrinsic topological mechanisms offers a practical route to robust, large-gap 2D topological insulators for potential spintronic or dissipationless transport applications.

title: Neural Networks As Low-cost Surrogates For Impurity Solvers In Quantum Embedding Methods
authors: Rohan Nain, Philip M. Dee, Kipton Barros, Steven Johnston, And Thomas A. Maier
abstract:
Author(s): Rohan Nain, Philip M. Dee, Kipton Barros, Steven Johnston, and Thomas A. Maier

A promising application of machine learning is the creation of low-cost surrogate models to mitigate computational bottlenecks in quantum many-body simulations. Here, we explore whether a neural network (NN) can be trained in the low-data regime, with one to two orders of magnitude fewer training ex…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225114] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores whether neural networks can serve as low-cost surrogate models for impurity solvers in quantum embedding methods.
motivation: Quantum embedding methods such as dynamical mean-field theory rely on repeated impurity solver calls, which are a major computational bottleneck in quantum many-body simulations.
method: The authors train neural networks in a low-data regime, using one to two orders of magnitude fewer training examples than typical, to approximate impurity solver outputs.
result: The neural network surrogates are shown to reproduce impurity solver results with reduced computational cost, suggesting they can accelerate quantum embedding workflows.
conclusion: Machine learning surrogates may help mitigate bottlenecks in quantum many-body simulation, but the work lies outside the core quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Lee-Yang Property Of The Blume-Capel Model
authors: Yuri Kozitsky And Yurij Holovatch
abstract:
Author(s): Yuri Kozitsky and Yurij Holovatch

The Lee-Yang theory is based on the theorem concerning a property of the ferromagnetic Ising model partition function proved by Lee and Yang in 1952. It provides powerful tools for understanding the very nature of phase transitions and critical phenomena in various spin and similar models. Sometimes…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044107] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the Lee-Yang property of the partition function for the classical Blume-Capel spin model to analyze its phase transitions.
motivation: Lee-Yang theory uses partition function zeros to characterize phase transitions and critical phenomena, and the Blume-Capel model generalizes the Ising model with vacancies and anisotropy.
method: The authors perform rigorous statistical-mechanical and mathematical analysis of the partition function zeros, likely establishing conditions for the Lee-Yang property in the Blume-Capel model.
result: They prove or characterize the Lee-Yang property for certain parameter regimes, showing that the partition function zeros lie on appropriate curves, which constrains the phase structure.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of phase transitions in a classical spin model but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Signatures Of The Circular Unruh Effect In Electric And Magnetic Dipole Transitions Of Multilevel Atoms
authors: Gregor Janson, Fabio Di Pumpo, Lorenz Thoma, And Maxim A. Efremov
abstract:
Author(s): Gregor Janson, Fabio Di Pumpo, Lorenz Thoma, and Maxim A. Efremov

The circular Unruh effect is the excitation of a detector moving along a planar circular trajectory within an electromagnetic vacuum. We demonstrate that the magnetic dipole transitions in an atom, acting as the detector, dominate the electric dipole transitions. Our analysis of both free-space and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043029] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies signatures of the circular Unruh effect in electric and magnetic dipole transitions of multilevel atoms, finding that magnetic dipole transitions dominate over electric dipole transitions.
motivation: The circular Unruh effect—excitation of a detector moving on a circular trajectory in the electromagnetic vacuum—is a fundamental prediction of quantum field theory, and its observable signatures in atomic systems are of interest.
method: The authors analyze multilevel atoms as detectors undergoing uniform circular motion in free space, comparing the contributions of electric and magnetic dipole transitions to the excitation rate.
result: They demonstrate that magnetic dipole transitions dominate the circular Unruh effect compared to electric dipole transitions for realistic atomic parameters.
conclusion: These results suggest that magnetic dipole transitions provide a more promising route for experimentally detecting the circular Unruh effect in atomic systems.

title: Observing The Spatial And Temporal Evolution Of Exciton Wave Functions In Organic Semiconductors
authors: Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, and Peter Puschnig

Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography tracks photoelectron profiles to reconstruct the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031054] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography is used to reconstruct the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.
motivation: Understanding how exciton wave functions evolve spatially and temporally is key to exciton transport physics in organic semiconductors, but direct experimental access to their real-space shape and phase has been lacking.
method: The authors combine femtosecond time-resolved photoemission with orbital tomography, tracking photoelectron momentum profiles to reconstruct the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons.
result: The experiment visualizes the spatial and temporal evolution of the exciton wave function, revealing its internal quantum phase structure in an organic semiconductor.
conclusion: Time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography offers a general route to imaging exciton wave-function dynamics, with implications for optoelectronic materials but no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid qubit platforms.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A resource analysis of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics on fault-tolerant quantum computers, bounding the achievable quantum advantage.
motivation: Nonlinear fluid simulations are classically demanding, motivating quantum algorithms, but their practical speedups and resource bottlenecks require rigorous assessment.
method: Detailed resource estimation for a fault-tolerant quantum algorithm simulating nonlinear fluid dynamics, including gate counts, qubit overhead, and runtime scaling.
result: The analysis identifies fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups, establishing bounds on the quantum advantage for nonlinear fluid simulation.
conclusion: The end-to-end algorithm yields only bounded quantum advantage, with practical performance limited by fault-tolerant resource requirements.

title: Kink-Boundary-Induced Polarity Revealed By Nonreciprocal Charge Transport In ${\mathrm{FeTe}}_{0.7}{\mathrm{Se}}_{0.3}$ Superconductor
authors: Shengyao Li, Ya Deng, Han Yan, Dianyi Hu, Zherui Yang, Xueyan Wang, Ming Yue, Qiong Wu, Zheng Liu, And X. Renshaw Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shengyao Li, Ya Deng, Han Yan, Dianyi Hu, Zherui Yang, Xueyan Wang, Ming Yue, Qiong Wu, Zheng Liu, and X. Renshaw Wang

Nonreciprocal charge transport, characterized by direction-dependent electrical response, provides a powerful probe of electronic structure and a platform for rectification. However, its realization is typically governed by intrinsic crystal symmetry, restricting the range of suitable materials. Her…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156302] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports nonreciprocal charge transport in the FeTe0.7Se0.3 superconductor arising from kink-boundary-induced polarity, enabling direction-dependent electrical rectification.
motivation: Nonreciprocal charge transport is normally constrained by intrinsic crystal symmetry, limiting the range of materials in which it can be realized; the authors seek a mechanism that relaxes this symmetry restriction.
method: The authors perform electrical transport measurements on FeTe0.7Se0.3 thin films, correlating direction-dependent resistance with the presence and geometry of kink boundaries.
result: A polarity-dependent nonreciprocal transport response is observed and attributed to kink boundaries rather than bulk crystal symmetry.
conclusion: Kink boundaries provide a tunable route to engineer nonreciprocal charge transport in superconductors, broadening the material platforms for rectification devices.

title: Microscopic Signatures Of Chern Number Sign Reversal In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$
authors: Ke Lv, Ya-Ning Ren, And Lin He
abstract:
Author(s): Ke Lv, Ya-Ning Ren, and Lin He

The observation of quantized Chern numbers in twisted transition metal dichalcogenide homobilayers, including 3.7° twisted [MATH] and 1.23° twisted [MATH], represents a landmark breakthrough in moiré physics. A striking and unresolved paradox to emerge from these studies…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156201] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports microscopic signatures of a sign reversal in the Chern number of twisted bilayer WSe2 moiré bands, using scanning-probe measurements to resolve the underlying mechanism behind an apparent paradox in moiré Chern physics.
motivation: Quantized Chern numbers in twisted transition metal dichalcogenide homobilayers represent a landmark result in moiré physics, yet an unresolved paradox concerning the sign of the Chern number in these systems remains.
method: The authors perform microscopic local-probe (scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy) measurements on twisted bilayer WSe2 to spatially resolve electronic structure signatures associated with the Chern number sign reversal.
result: They identify microscopic signatures that reconcile the observed quantized anomalous Hall response with the underlying band topology, clarifying how the Chern number sign reverses between different twisted configurations.
conclusion: The findings provide a local, microscopic picture of Chern number sign reversal in twisted TMD homobilayers, deepening the understanding of topological moiré bands.

title: Effective Skyrmion Number For Mixed Polarization States Of Light
authors: Rosario Martínez-Herrero And Ángel S. Sanz
abstract:
Author(s): Rosario Martínez-Herrero and Ángel S. Sanz

Polarization skyrmions are usually characterized through a unit Stokes vector field, which defines a map from the transverse plane to the Poincaré (Bloch) sphere and allows one to assign a skyrmion number under appropriate boundary conditions. This description assumes complete polarization. In many …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043503] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper defines an effective skyrmion number for mixed (partially polarized) states of light, extending the usual complete-polarization Stokes-vector description.
motivation: Polarization skyrmions are typically characterized assuming complete polarization, which fails for mixed or partially polarized light that commonly occurs in practice.
method: The authors generalize the Stokes-vector map from the transverse plane to the Poincaré sphere by accounting for mixed polarization states and introduce an effective skyrmion number.
result: An effective skyrmion number is formulated that remains well-defined for mixed polarization states and reduces to the standard skyrmion number in the fully polarized limit.
conclusion: The work provides a topological characterization of polarization textures beyond complete polarization, relevant to structured light and singular optics.

title: Mechanisms For Extreme Events In Position-dependent Mass Systems
authors: M. Wasif Ahamed, V. Chithiika Ruby, M. Sathish Aravindh, A. Venkatesan, And M. Lakshmanan
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wasif Ahamed, V. Chithiika Ruby, M. Sathish Aravindh, A. Venkatesan, and M. Lakshmanan

Oscillators defined on curved spaces provide a natural framework for exploring geometry-induced nonlinear dynamics. The two-dimensional Mathews-Lakshmanan oscillator and Higgs oscillator are prominent examples of geometrically induced nonlinear oscillators. The two-dimensional Higgs oscillator in fl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044204] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies extreme events and nonlinear dynamics in position-dependent mass systems, focusing on Mathews-Lakshmanan and Higgs oscillators on curved spaces.
motivation: Oscillators defined on curved spaces provide a natural framework for exploring geometry-induced nonlinear dynamics and extreme-event formation.
method: The authors analyze the two-dimensional Mathews-Lakshmanan oscillator and the Higgs oscillator, likely using dynamical systems techniques and numerical simulations.
result: Mechanisms underlying extreme events in these position-dependent mass systems are identified, revealing geometry-induced nonlinear phenomena.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of extreme events in classical nonlinear oscillator models on curved spaces, but it does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Excitation Spectrum And Mean Energy Of Thermal Fluctuations Of A Simple Fluid In The Maxwell Generalized Hydrodynamics Model
authors: E. V. Usov
abstract:
Author(s): E. V. Usov

Within the framework of linear Maxwell generalized hydrodynamics, explicit expressions for the Green's functions of longitudinal and transverse modes are obtained. Using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, the spectral densities of individual contributions to the total energy of the fluid are deter…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044108] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives Green's functions and spectral densities for thermal fluctuations in a simple fluid using the Maxwell generalized hydrodynamics model.
motivation: To characterize the excitation spectrum and mean energy of thermal fluctuations in fluids beyond standard hydrodynamics.
method: Linear Maxwell generalized hydrodynamics is used to obtain Green's functions, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem yields spectral densities of energy contributions.
result: Explicit expressions for longitudinal and transverse Green's functions and the spectral densities of individual energy contributions are obtained.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed spectral analysis of thermal fluctuations in a simple fluid within linear Maxwell generalized hydrodynamics.

title: Vanishing Phase Stiffness And Fluctuation-Dominated Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$
authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, And B. J. Ramshaw
abstract:
Author(s): Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, and B. J. Ramshaw

Ultrasound measurements in uranium ditelluride (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041006] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound measurements on the heavy-fermion superconductor UTe2 reveal superconducting fluctuations extending up to twice Tc, indicating vanishing phase stiffness and fluctuation-dominated superconductivity with high kinetic inductance.
motivation: UTe2 is an unconventional superconductor of intense interest, and understanding the nature and extent of its superconducting fluctuations could illuminate the pairing mechanism and the unusually low superfluid stiffness.
method: The authors performed ultrasound (acoustic) measurements as a function of temperature on single-crystal UTe2, extracting the superfluid phase stiffness and elastic response to probe precursor superconducting fluctuations.
result: They observe fluctuation signatures up to roughly 2Tc, consistent with a vanishingly small phase stiffness in a very clean material, implying a large kinetic inductance dominated by fluctuations.
conclusion: The findings establish UTe2 as a fluctuation-dominated superconductor, with implications for its pairing symmetry and for applications exploiting its high kinetic inductance.

title: Exact Nematic And Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven By Competing Orders On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, And Daniel Lozano-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, and Daniel Lozano-Gómez

Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031070] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A frustrated pyrochlore spin model is shown to stabilize exact nematic and mixed magnetic phases through thermal fluctuations and competing orders.
motivation: Frustrated magnets on the pyrochlore lattice can host unconventional states when conventional order is suppressed by competing interactions and fluctuations.
method: The authors analyze a parameter-dependent pyrochlore spin model, using symmetry arguments and exact treatments to identify stable magnetic phases.
result: The model exhibits a magnetic nematic phase and mixed magnetic phases in regimes where thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order.
conclusion: The work provides an exact characterization of nematic and mixed magnetic orders on the pyrochlore lattice, highlighting the role of competing orders and fluctuations.

title: Effective Ionic Valence And Local Magnetic Moment In Kagome Superconductors
authors: Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, And Wei Ku
abstract:
Author(s): Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, and Wei Ku

Revealing concealed ionic local moments in kagome superconductors reflects strong local correlations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031064] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates effective ionic valence and concealed local magnetic moments in kagome superconductors, revealing signatures of strong local electronic correlations.
motivation: Kagome superconductors host intertwined electronic orders whose underlying local electronic structure and magnetic moment formation remain poorly understood, motivating a detailed probe of ionic valence and local moments.
method: The authors combine experimental probes (e.g., magnetization and local magnetic measurements such as muon spin rotation) with electronic-structure analysis to extract effective ionic valences and local magnetic moments in kagome superconductor compounds.
result: They find evidence for concealed local magnetic moments and non-trivial effective ionic valence, indicating that strong local correlations play a central role in the electronic physics of these kagome materials.
conclusion: The work argues that local moment formation and ionic valence effects are essential ingredients for understanding the correlated electronic and superconducting behavior of kagome superconductors.

title: Particle View Of Many-Body Electronic Structure With Neural Network Wave Function
authors: Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, And Ji Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, and Ji Chen

A combination of theoretical approaches bridges the gap between complex quantum wave functions and the classical picture of electron positions for molecules and solids.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031048] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a particle-view approach to many-body electronic structure using neural network wave functions for molecules and solids.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge complex quantum wave functions with the classical picture of electron positions, improving interpretability and accuracy in electronic structure calculations.
method: They combine theoretical approaches with neural network wave functions to represent many-body electronic states and extract particle-position information.
result: The method is demonstrated on molecules and solids, showing that neural network wave functions can provide a useful particle view of electronic structure.
conclusion: The work advances computational electronic structure and quantum chemistry, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Information Bound On Navigation Speed In Smart Active Matter
authors: Kristian Stølevik Olsen, Mitsusuke Tarama, And Hartmut Löwen
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Stølevik Olsen, Mitsusuke Tarama, and Hartmut Löwen

Intelligent behavior in lifelike systems often arises from the ability to gather, process, and act on information. While active matter provides a framework for studying lifelike dynamics, it typically omits internal information processing and decision making. Here we introduce an adaptive active par…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 157101] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an adaptive active particle model and derives an information-theoretic bound on navigation speed in smart active matter.
motivation: Intelligent behavior in lifelike systems arises from information gathering and processing, but standard active matter models omit internal information processing and decision making.
method: The authors develop a model of an adaptive active particle that processes information to navigate, and derive a bound relating its navigation speed to information processing capacity.
result: An information bound on navigation speed is obtained, showing how the speed of a smart active particle is constrained by its information processing rate.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of information in active matter dynamics, though it remains classical and outside quantum information or thermodynamics frameworks.

title: Huge Symmetric Elastoresistance In The Kondo Lattice ${\mathrm{YbRh}}_{2}{\mathrm{Si}}_{2}$
authors: Soumendra Nath Panja, Jacques G. Pontanel, Julian Kaiser, Anton Jesche, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Soumendra Nath Panja, Jacques G. Pontanel, Julian Kaiser, Anton Jesche, and Philipp Gegenwart

Heavy-fermion metals are prototype correlated electron systems for the study of Kondo entanglement and quantum criticality. We use the symmetry decomposed elastoresistance to uncover the fingerprints of strain-dependent Kondo scattering as a function of temperature and magnetic field in the prototyp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156502] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: Symmetry-decomposed elastoresistance measurements on the heavy-fermion Kondo lattice YbRh2Si2 reveal a large symmetric strain response tied to strain-dependent Kondo scattering.
motivation: Heavy-fermion metals are prototype correlated-electron systems for probing Kondo entanglement and quantum criticality, and understanding how strain couples to the Kondo lattice can illuminate these phenomena.
method: The authors perform symmetry-decomposed elastoresistance measurements on YbRh2Si2 as a function of temperature and magnetic field to isolate the strain-dependent Kondo scattering contribution.
result: A huge symmetric elastoresistance response is observed, with fingerprints of strain-dependent Kondo scattering varying systematically with temperature and magnetic field.
conclusion: Elastoresistance provides a sensitive probe of Kondo entanglement and quantum criticality in heavy-fermion metals, but the work is a condensed-matter transport study without a quantum-information or information-thermodynamic framing.

title: Micromotion Area As Proxy For Anomalous Floquet Topological Systems
authors: Luca Asteria, Klaus Sengstock, André Eckardt, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Asteria, Klaus Sengstock, André Eckardt, and Christof Weitenberg

Driven Floquet systems can realize topological phases with no static counterparts. This so-called anomalous Floquet topology breaks the bulk-boundary correspondence based on the Chern number. The number of edge modes in each band gap is instead determined by another integer index, a winding number, …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 153401] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using the micromotion area as a proxy for detecting anomalous Floquet topological phases characterized by a winding number.
motivation: Anomalous Floquet topological insulators break the conventional bulk-boundary correspondence based on the Chern number, making their topological characterization and experimental detection challenging.
method: The authors analyze the micromotion of periodically driven quantum systems and relate its area in phase space to the topological winding number that determines the number of edge modes.
result: They show that the micromotion area can serve as an experimentally accessible signature of anomalous Floquet topology, distinguishing it from trivial or conventional topological phases.
conclusion: This work provides a simple and practical tool for identifying anomalous Floquet topological phases in driven quantum systems, with potential applications in cold-atom and photonic experiments.

title: Demonstration Of Robust Chiral Edge Transport In Field-Induced Chern Insulator ${\mathrm{MnBi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{4}$ Devices With Engineered Geometric Defects
authors: Pinyuan Wang, Jun Ge, Jiawei Luo, Xiaoqi Liu, Jiayi Yang, Fucong Fei, Fengqi Song, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Pinyuan Wang, Jun Ge, Jiawei Luo, Xiaoqi Liu, Jiayi Yang, Fucong Fei, Fengqi Song, and Jian Wang

Chiral edge states in Chern insulators are theoretically predicted to propagate unidirectionally along the sample boundary with inherent robustness against local perturbations, which manifests as the immunity to impurity-induced backscattering, a key factor for the development of robust, high-perfor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156601] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of robust chiral edge transport in field-induced Chern insulator MnBi2Te4 devices with engineered geometric defects.
motivation: Chern insulators are predicted to host topologically protected chiral edge states that are robust against local perturbations, but testing this robustness in real devices with controlled defects is challenging.
method: Fabricated field-induced Chern insulator MnBi2Te4 devices containing engineered geometric defects and performed transport measurements to probe chiral edge conduction.
result: Observed robust chiral edge transport that remains immune to impurity-induced backscattering and local geometric defects.
conclusion: The findings confirm topological protection in MnBi2Te4 Chern insulator devices and support potential applications in robust low-dissipation electronics.

title: Magnetic Exchange-Coupled Superconducting Devices With Broken Symmetry For Cryogenic Memory
authors: Josep Ingla-Aynés, Lina Johnsen Kamra, Franklin Dai, Yasen Hou, Shouzhuo Yang, Peng Chen, Oleg A. Mukhanov, And Jagadeesh S. Moodera
