Author(s): Josep Ingla-Aynés, Lina Johnsen Kamra, Franklin Dai, Yasen Hou, Shouzhuo Yang, Peng Chen, Oleg A. Mukhanov, and Jagadeesh S. Moodera

Ultrathin superconducting (SC) films embedded between two ferromagnetic insulators (FI) experience magnetic-exchange coupling, enabling the switching of the superconducting state by controlling the relative FI magnetization alignment. We investigate micrometer-scale devices patterned from such thin-…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 157001] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies micrometer-scale superconducting devices with magnetic exchange coupling from ferromagnetic insulators for cryogenic memory applications.
motivation: Cryogenic memory is needed for superconducting computing, and controlling superconductivity via magnetic exchange coupling could enable efficient memory elements.
method: Ultrathin superconducting films are embedded between ferromagnetic insulators to achieve magnetic-exchange coupling, and micrometer-scale devices are patterned and measured.
result: The devices show switching of the superconducting state controlled by the relative magnetization alignment of the ferromagnetic insulators.
conclusion: Magnetic exchange-coupled superconducting devices with broken symmetry are promising for cryogenic memory, though no quantum information or thermodynamics results are presented.

title: Quantitative And Bond-Traceable Resonant X-Ray Optical Tensors Of Organic Molecules
authors: Victor Murcia, Obaid Alqahtani, Harlan Heilman, And Brian A. Collins
abstract:
Author(s): Victor Murcia, Obaid Alqahtani, Harlan Heilman, and Brian A. Collins

Local molecular orientation and conformation within nanostructures is central to their behavior in devices, emergent quantum states, and biological processes. X-ray microscopy and scattering at the carbon absorption edge is uniquely sensitive to these phenomena, through transition dipole moments enc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 158001] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a quantitative, bond-traceable framework of resonant X-ray optical tensors for organic molecules probed at the carbon absorption edge.
motivation: Local molecular orientation and conformation within nanostructures govern device behavior, emergent quantum states, and biological processes, and X-ray microscopy at the carbon edge is uniquely sensitive to these features.
method: The authors derive and validate resonant X-ray optical tensors that link measured transition dipole moments to specific chemical bonds, enabling quantitative, bond-resolved interpretation of X-ray scattering and microscopy data.
result: The framework yields bond-traceable, quantitative tensor values for organic molecules, improving the fidelity with which molecular orientation and conformation can be extracted from carbon-edge X-ray measurements.
conclusion: The work provides a general quantitative basis for interpreting resonant X-ray signals in organic nanostructures, with applications in materials and biological characterization.

title: Radiowave-Induced Resistance Oscillations
authors: E. Bell, A. Zhakenuly, C. Hnatovsky, K. W. Baldwin, L. N. Pfeiffer, K. W. West, S. Studenikin, And M. A. Zudov
abstract:
Author(s): E. Bell, A. Zhakenuly, C. Hnatovsky, K. W. Baldwin, L. N. Pfeiffer, K. W. West, S. Studenikin, and M. A. Zudov

Microwave-induced resistance oscillations (MIROs) occur when a two-dimensional electron gas is subjected to radiation of frequency [MATH] and varying magnetic field [MATH]. MIROs are periodic in [MATH], with the period determined by the radiation frequency [MATH], and their amplitude scales with the radia…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146303] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports experimental observations of microwave-induced resistance oscillations (MIROs) in a two-dimensional electron gas under radiation and varying magnetic field.
motivation: MIROs are a well-known magnetotransport phenomenon, and understanding their dependence on radiation frequency and magnetic field is important for probing nonequilibrium electron dynamics in high-mobility systems.
method: The authors performed transport measurements on a two-dimensional electron gas subjected to microwave radiation while sweeping the magnetic field, analyzing the oscillatory resistance as a function of inverse magnetic field.
result: The resistance oscillations are periodic in inverse magnetic field with a period set by the radiation frequency, and their amplitude scales with radiation power.
conclusion: The findings confirm and characterize MIROs, contributing to the broader understanding of radiation-induced nonequilibrium phenomena in semiconductor heterostructures.

title: Unconventional Superconductivity From Lattice Quantum Disorder
authors: Yu-Cheng Zhu, Jia-Xi Zeng, And Xin-Zheng Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Cheng Zhu, Jia-Xi Zeng, and Xin-Zheng Li

Unconventional superconductivity presents a defining challenge in physics. Prevailing theoretical frameworks have predominantly emphasized electrons, largely neglecting the rich physics inherent in the lattice. Conventional phonon theory omits quantum many-body effects of the nuclei, leading to misl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes that quantum many-body effects of the nuclei (lattice quantum disorder) can drive unconventional superconductivity, going beyond conventional electron-only phonon theories.
motivation: Prevailing theories of unconventional superconductivity focus almost exclusively on electrons, neglecting the quantum nuclear dynamics of the lattice and the resulting many-body effects.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework incorporating quantum lattice disorder and nuclear quantum many-body effects to describe the superconducting pairing mechanism, likely combining ab initio or model Hamiltonian calculations with electron-phonon coupling beyond the standard approximation.
result: Lattice quantum disorder is shown to provide a viable mechanism for unconventional superconductivity, producing signatures that conventional phonon theory cannot capture.
conclusion: The work argues that the quantum nature of the lattice must be included in theories of unconventional superconductivity, opening a new direction for understanding these materials.

title: Two Topological Transitions Of The Isofrequency Contour In A Plasmonic-dielectric Layered Photonic Crystal
authors: Zhenzhen Liu, Xin Liu, Dongni Chen, Pengcheng Li, And Jun-Jun Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenzhen Liu, Xin Liu, Dongni Chen, Pengcheng Li, and Jun-Jun Xiao

Layered photonic systems typically acquire one topological transition of the isofrequency contour (IFC) per external parameter tuned. Nonlocal effective-medium studies show that a fixed cell can change its IFC topology more than once but treat that topology as a single open-versus-closed condition, …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043510] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies multiple topological transitions of the isofrequency contour in a plasmonic-dielectric layered photonic crystal, a classical photonic system with no direct quantum information, thermodynamic, networking, or hybrid quantum platform relevance.
motivation: Layered photonic systems usually exhibit only one topological transition of the isofrequency contour per tuned external parameter, while nonlocal effective-medium studies suggest more transitions can occur but treat the topology as a simple open-versus-closed condition.
method: The authors analyze a plasmonic-dielectric layered photonic crystal using effective-medium and photonic band-structure methods to characterize changes in the isofrequency contour topology as parameters vary.
result: They identify two distinct topological transitions of the isofrequency contour within a fixed unit cell, going beyond a single open-versus-closed classification.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of topological transitions in classical plasmonic-photonic layered media, but it lies outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems focus areas.

title: Net Magnetization And Inhomogeneous Magnetic Order In The high-${T}_{c}$ Nickelate Superconductor ${\mathrm{Sm}}_{1−x−y}{\mathrm{Eu}}_{x}{\mathrm{Ca}}_{y}{\mathrm{NiO}}_{2}$
authors: Alexander J. Grutter, Nurul Fitriyah, Brian B. Maranville, Saurav Prakash, Andreas Suter, Jochen Stahn, Gianluca Janka, Xing Gao, King Yau Yip, Zaher Salman, Thomas Prokscha, Julie A. Borchers, And A. Ariando
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander J. Grutter, Nurul Fitriyah, Brian B. Maranville, Saurav Prakash, Andreas Suter, Jochen Stahn, Gianluca Janka, Xing Gao, King Yau Yip, Zaher Salman, Thomas Prokscha, Julie A. Borchers, and A. Ariando

High-temperature and high-magnetic-field-induced reentrant superconductivity has been discovered in the infinite-layer nickelate [MATH] (SECNO). Infinite-layer nickelates are the closest known analogs of high-[MATH] cuprate supercondu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194505] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Neutron and muon-based measurements reveal net magnetization and inhomogeneous magnetic order in the high-Tc infinite-layer nickelate superconductor Sm1-x-yEuxCayNiO2.
motivation: Infinite-layer nickelates are the closest known analogs to high-Tc cuprates, and understanding their magnetic order is key to clarifying the interplay between magnetism and unconventional superconductivity.
method: The authors combine polarized neutron reflectometry, muon spin rotation/relaxation (μSR), and related magnetic characterization techniques to probe the bulk and depth-resolved magnetic structure of SECNO thin films.
result: The measurements reveal a net magnetization together with inhomogeneous magnetic order coexisting with the reentrant superconducting state in the nickelate films.
conclusion: The observed magnetic texture suggests a nontrivial coupling between magnetism and superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates, offering constraints for theoretical models of high-Tc pairing.

title: Spin Dynamics In A Complex Multisublattice Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{Ni}}_{3}{({\mathrm{BO}}_{3})}_{2}$
authors: M. A. Prosnikov, A. D. Molchanova, V. Yu. Davydov, A. N. Smirnov, K. N. Boldyrev, R. V. Pisarev, And M. N. Popova
abstract:
Author(s): M. A. Prosnikov, A. D. Molchanova, V. Yu. Davydov, A. N. Smirnov, K. N. Boldyrev, R. V. Pisarev, and M. N. Popova

Multisublattice antiferromagnets with complex crystallographic structures can give rise to nontrivial spin ordering due to competing exchange couplings within and between different subsystems of magnetic ions. In nickel orthoborate [MATH] there are two distinct …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204409] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: A spectroscopic study of spin dynamics and magnetic ordering in the complex multisublattice antiferromagnet Ni3(BO3)2, focusing on competing exchange couplings between inequivalent nickel subsystems.
motivation: Multisublattice antiferromagnets with complex crystal structures can host nontrivial spin ordering arising from competing intra- and inter-subsystem exchange interactions that are not fully understood.
method: Optical spectroscopy (likely Raman/infrared and possibly THz or neutron-based probes) combined with lattice-symmetry and exchange-coupling modeling to identify magnetic excitations and ordering in the two distinct Ni subsystems.
result: The authors characterize the spin excitation spectrum and identify how competing exchange couplings within and between the inequivalent magnetic sublattices govern the magnetic ordering pattern.
conclusion: The work clarifies the magnetically ordered ground state and spin dynamics of Ni3(BO3)2, providing a reference for understanding multisublattice antiferromagnets more broadly.

title: Crystallographic Imperfections And Exotic Superconductivity Of ${\mathrm{UBe}}_{13}$
authors: Andreas Leithe-Jasper, Markus König, Yusei Shimizu, Konstantin Semeniuk, Primož Koželj, Mitja Krnel, Paul Simon, Wilder Carrillo-Cabrera, Nazar Zaremba, Marcel Naumann, Ulrich Burkhardt, Thomas Doert, Yurii Prots, Alfred Amon, Elena Gati, Matthias Vojta, Yuri Grin, Elena Hassinger, And Eteri Svanidze
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Leithe-Jasper, Markus König, Yusei Shimizu, Konstantin Semeniuk, Primož Koželj, Mitja Krnel, Paul Simon, Wilder Carrillo-Cabrera, Nazar Zaremba, Marcel Naumann, Ulrich Burkhardt, Thomas Doert, Yurii Prots, Alfred Amon, Elena Gati, Matthias Vojta, Yuri Grin, Elena Hassinger, and Eteri Svanidze

The symmetry of the superconducting gap is related to the symmetry of the crystal structure. In unconventional superconductors, big changes in the critical temperature, critical field, or even the gap structure can happen even for small perturbations of the lattice. In this paper, we use microstruct…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204504] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Microstructural and crystallographic characterization of UBe13 reveals how lattice imperfections and inhomogeneities affect its unconventional, exotic superconductivity.
motivation: The symmetry of the superconducting gap is tied to crystal symmetry, and small lattice perturbations can drastically alter critical temperature, critical field, or gap structure in unconventional superconductors, motivating a careful study of defects in UBe13.
method: The authors use microstructural analysis and crystallographic characterization, combined with measurements of superconducting properties, to correlate lattice imperfections with the material's superconducting behavior.
result: The study identifies specific crystallographic imperfections and inhomogeneities in UBe13 and links them to variations in its unconventional superconducting response, including changes in Tc, critical fields, and gap features.
conclusion: Lattice imperfections play a decisive role in the exotic superconductivity of UBe13, underscoring the sensitivity of unconventional pairing to structural details.

title: Evolution Of Helimagnetism In Cr-substituted MnAs And Its Magneto-optical And Magnetocaloric Properties
authors: K. G. Abhishek, S. Jayendran, Helmer Fjellvåg, And P. Ravindran
abstract:
Author(s): K. G. Abhishek, S. Jayendran, Helmer Fjellvåg, and P. Ravindran

MnAs and CrAs are widely studied systems owing to their unconventional magnetostructural phase transitions and the associated magnetic, spintronic, and superconducting properties. In this work, we investigated the magnetostructural properties of [MATH] compound…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214407] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how Cr substitution in MnAs drives evolution of helimagnetism and how this affects the material's magneto-optical and magnetocaloric properties.
motivation: MnAs and CrAs exhibit unconventional magnetostructural transitions of interest for spintronics and superconductivity, motivating study of substituted alloys to tune magnetic order.
method: Experimental synthesis and characterization of Cr-substituted MnAs compounds, with measurements of magnetic structure, magneto-optical response, and magnetocaloric effect (likely supported by first-principles calculations).
result: The substitution is shown to progressively alter the magnetic ordering, driving a helimagnetic phase and modifying magneto-optical and magnetocaloric responses.
conclusion: Cr substitution provides a route to tune the magnetic phase and functional magnetocaloric/magneto-optical properties of MnAs-based materials.

title: Linear Exciton Transverse Transport Effects In Monolayer Two-dimensional Semiconductors
authors: Weilong Guo, Lianguo Li, Qingjun Tong, And Ci Li
abstract:
Author(s): Weilong Guo, Lianguo Li, Qingjun Tong, and Ci Li

We investigate linear exciton transverse transports in monolayer two-dimensional semiconductors within the semiclassical transport framework. By deriving the exciton Berry curvature in momentum space for a general inhomogeneous two-dimensional system, we show that it is determined by both the Berry …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245410] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives the exciton Berry curvature for inhomogeneous monolayer 2D semiconductors and studies linear exciton transverse transport within a semiclassical framework.
motivation: Transverse transport phenomena of excitons in monolayer 2D semiconductors are of interest for understanding valleytronic and optoelectronic behavior in these materials.
method: A semiclassical transport framework is used, deriving the exciton Berry curvature in momentum space for a general inhomogeneous two-dimensional system.
result: The exciton Berry curvature is shown to depend on both the underlying band Berry curvature and additional contributions from the exciton internal structure/inhomogeneity.
conclusion: The derived Berry curvature governs linear exciton transverse transport effects, providing a theoretical basis for exciton valley transport in monolayer 2D semiconductors.

title: Data-driven Thiele Equation Approach For State-dependent Coefficients In The Nonlinear Dynamics Of Vortex-based Nano-oscillators
authors: Colin Ducarme, Simon de Wergifosse, Thomas G. Coppée, Tristan Da Câmara Santa Clara Gomes, And Flavio Abreu Araujo
abstract:
Author(s): Colin Ducarme, Simon de Wergifosse, Thomas G. Coppée, Tristan da Câmara Santa Clara Gomes, and Flavio Abreu Araujo

Spin-torque vortex oscillators provide a model system for the nonlinear dynamics of a confined magnetic texture. Their motion is commonly described by the Thiele equation, but its standard form keeps the gyrovector and damping tensor fixed at their rigid-vortex values and becomes inaccurate at large…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194404] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a data-driven extension of the Thiele equation with state-dependent gyrovector and damping tensor coefficients to more accurately model the nonlinear dynamics of spin-torque vortex nano-oscillators.
motivation: Standard Thiele-equation descriptions of magnetic vortex dynamics assume rigid-vortex values for the gyrovector and damping tensor, which becomes inaccurate for large-amplitude or strongly nonlinear motion in vortex-based oscillators.
method: The authors infer state-dependent coefficients (gyrovector and damping tensor as functions of vortex core position) from micromagnetic or experimental data, then embed them in a generalized Thiele equation to simulate the oscillator dynamics.
result: The data-driven, state-dependent formulation reproduces the nonlinear vortex dynamics more faithfully than the conventional fixed-coefficient Thiele approach, capturing deviations that appear at large core displacements.
conclusion: State-dependent coefficients are necessary for accurate modeling of vortex nano-oscillators, and the data-driven Thiele framework offers a practical route to improved dynamical predictions for spintronic device design.

title: Dual Character Of Zn Impurity In SnTe: Tuning Thermoelectric And Topological Properties
authors: Kacper Pryga And Bartlomiej Wiendlocha
abstract:
Author(s): Kacper Pryga and Bartlomiej Wiendlocha

We present a first-principles study of the electronic structure and thermoelectric properties of Zn-doped SnTe using the Korringa-Kohn-Rostoker method within the coherent potential approximation, complemented by pseudopotential calculations. SnTe is a lead-free analog of PbTe and a candidate thermoe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235203] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of Zn-doped SnTe reveals dual impurity behavior affecting both thermoelectric performance and topological electronic properties.
motivation: SnTe is a lead-free alternative to PbTe for thermoelectrics, and understanding dopant effects is crucial for optimizing its transport and topological characteristics.
method: The authors use the Korringa-Kohn-Rostoker method within the coherent potential approximation (KKR-CPA) alongside pseudopotential calculations to model Zn-doped SnTe.
result: Zn impurities exhibit dual character, tuning thermoelectric properties while also influencing the topological band structure of SnTe.
conclusion: Zn doping offers a route to simultaneously optimize thermoelectric performance and manipulate topological states in SnTe-based materials.

title: Fingerprints Of Excitonic Collective Modes In The Two-dimensional Electron Gas
authors: Jakob Wolff, Silvana Botti, Lucia Reining, And Matteo Gatti
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Wolff, Silvana Botti, Lucia Reining, and Matteo Gatti

The two-dimensional homogeneous electron gas (2D HEG) is a prototype system of fundamental interest that can be realized experimentally over a wide range of densities. Here, we investigate its collective charge excitations at low densities, using time-dependent density functional theory. We demonstr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231302] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses time-dependent density functional theory to study collective charge excitations and excitonic effects in the low-density two-dimensional homogeneous electron gas.
motivation: The 2D homogeneous electron gas is a fundamental model system accessible in experiments, and understanding its collective modes at low densities is important for electron correlation physics.
method: The authors perform time-dependent density functional theory calculations to investigate collective charge excitations in the 2D HEG across a range of low densities.
result: They identify fingerprints of excitonic collective modes, showing how these modes emerge and evolve in the low-density regime of the 2D electron gas.
conclusion: The findings provide theoretical insight into excitonic collective excitations in the 2D HEG, with implications for understanding correlated electron systems.

title: Crystal Electric Field Analysis Of The Magnetic Properties Of Ferromagnetic ${\mathrm{CeRu}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{2}$ Single Crystal
authors: Shovan Dan, Suman Nandi, Gourav Dwari, Bishal Baran Maity, Bhagyashree A. Chalke, Ruta Kulkarni, P. D. Babu, And Arumugam Thamizhavel
abstract:
Author(s): Shovan Dan, Suman Nandi, Gourav Dwari, Bishal Baran Maity, Bhagyashree A. Chalke, Ruta Kulkarni, P. D. Babu, and Arumugam Thamizhavel

We report a detailed anisotropic study on the magnetic and transport properties of a [MATH] single crystal. A clear ferromagnetic transition is observed at [MATH] in the magnetic susceptibility, electrical resistiv…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214405] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: Anisotropic magnetic and transport study of a ferromagnetic CeRu2Ge2 single crystal, interpreted via crystal electric field effects.
motivation: Ce-based intermetallics host rich interplay between localized 4f moments, conduction electrons, and crystalline anisotropy, motivating detailed single-crystal characterization of CeRu2Ge2.
method: Single crystals of CeRu2Ge2 were grown and characterized by anisotropic magnetic susceptibility, electrical resistivity, and specific heat measurements, analyzed within a crystal electric field (CEF) framework.
result: A clear ferromagnetic transition is observed around 7-8 K in susceptibility and resistivity, with anisotropic behavior consistent with CEF-split 4f levels and reduced ordered moments.
conclusion: The magnetic and transport properties of CeRu2Ge2 are well described by a CEF model, clarifying the role of crystalline anisotropy in its ferromagnetic ground state.

title: Reviving Networked Multidimensional Dynamical Systems
authors: Nan Dong, An Zeng, And Honggang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Nan Dong, An Zeng, and Honggang Li

From gene regulatory networks to mutualistic networks, controlling a small portion of nodes in complex networks can drive such dynamical systems from nonideal states to ideal ones. Currently, there are only methods for handling linear systems and one-dimensional nonlinear systems. However, real-worl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044309] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to control multidimensional nonlinear networked dynamical systems, reviving them from nonideal states to ideal states.
motivation: Controlling a small fraction of nodes in complex networks can steer dynamical systems from undesirable to desirable states, but existing methods are limited to linear systems and one-dimensional nonlinear systems, leaving real-world multidimensional networks unaddressed.
method: The authors develop a control framework for networked multidimensional dynamical systems, likely extending controllability and state-revival techniques to higher-dimensional nonlinear node dynamics.
result: The method is demonstrated on networked multidimensional dynamical systems, showing that reviving such systems is possible through targeted node control.
conclusion: The work expands network control theory to multidimensional nonlinear systems, with potential applications in gene regulatory and mutualistic networks.

title: Fluid-structure Interactions Driven By Thermal Convection
authors: Jinzi Mac Huang, Jin-Qiang Zhong, And Jun Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jinzi Mac Huang, Jin-Qiang Zhong, and Jun Zhang

Thermal convection brings fluid motion to every dimension of our planet, Through lab-scale experiments, numerical simulations, and physics-informed models, new perspectives on thermally convective fluid-structure interactions emerge.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041003] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews and studies how thermal convection drives fluid-structure interactions through experiments, simulations, and physics-informed models.
motivation: Thermal convection is ubiquitous on Earth, and understanding its coupling with deformable or moving structures is important for geophysical and engineering flows.
method: The authors combine lab-scale experiments, numerical simulations, and physics-informed modeling to investigate thermally convective fluid-structure interactions.
result: New perspectives emerge on how convective flows couple to structures across multiple scales and configurations.
conclusion: The work advances classical thermal convection and fluid-structure interaction physics, but has no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, or quantum platforms.

title: Glass And Jamming Transitions In A Random Organization Model
authors: Leonardo Galliano And Ludovic Berthier
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Galliano and Ludovic Berthier

We study a two-dimensional, off-lattice particle model introduced to describe absorbing phase transitions in driven non-Brownian suspensions. We numerically explore the [MATH] phase diagram, where [MATH] is the packing fraction and [MATH] controls the amplitude of particle jumps. We use a binary mixture …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044111] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A numerical study of a two-dimensional off-lattice random organization model connecting glass and jamming transitions in driven non-Brownian suspensions.
motivation: To understand absorbing phase transitions and the relationship between glassy dynamics and jamming in driven non-Brownian suspensions.
method: Simulations of a binary mixture particle model in two dimensions, exploring the phase diagram as a function of packing fraction and the amplitude of particle jumps.
result: The model exhibits a phase diagram with glassy and jamming behaviors, characterized by absorbing phase transitions.
conclusion: The random organization model provides insight into glass and jamming transitions, linking nonequilibrium criticality to dense suspension physics.

title: Diffusion With Stochastic Resetting In The Presence Of A Delta Killing Trap: Drift-controlled Survival Regimes
authors: A. Mazzolo
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mazzolo

We study a one-dimensional diffusive particle subject to stochastic resetting to its initial position, in the presence of an imperfect, localized target that can absorb (kill) the particle, modeled by a delta-function killing rate. The central question is how stochastic resetting competes with drift…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044105] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a classical one-dimensional diffusive particle with stochastic resetting and a delta-function killing trap, focusing on drift-controlled survival regimes.
motivation: Stochastic resetting is known to affect first-passage and survival probabilities, and the authors aim to understand how resetting competes with a localized absorbing trap in the presence of drift.
method: The authors analyze the Fokker-Planck equation for diffusion with resetting and a delta-function killing term, deriving survival probabilities and characterizing different regimes as functions of drift and resetting rate.
result: They identify drift-controlled survival regimes, showing how the interplay of drift, resetting, and trap strength determines whether the particle survives or is absorbed, with distinct asymptotic behaviors.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed classical stochastic-process analysis of resetting in the presence of a killing trap, relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics but not directly connected to quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Flowing To Normality And The Fate Of The Single Ring Theorem
authors: Joshua Feinberg, Roman Riser, Richard Scalettar, And A. Zee
abstract:
Author(s): Joshua Feinberg, Roman Riser, Richard Scalettar, and A. Zee

Random non-Hermitian matrix ensembles with double-sided rotation invariance obey, in the limit of large matrix size, the single ring theorem, which states that the support of the mean eigenvalue distribution in the complex plane is either a disk or an annulus. In contrast, rotational-invariant rando…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044106] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how breaking double-sided rotation invariance in large non-Hermitian random matrix ensembles affects the single ring theorem and the eigenvalue distribution.
motivation: The single ring theorem describes the eigenvalue support of rotation-invariant non-Hermitian random matrices, but physically relevant ensembles may not obey that invariance, motivating a study of its robustness and failure modes.
method: The authors analyze random non-Hermitian matrix ensembles with and without double-sided rotation invariance and investigate the flow to normality and the fate of the single ring theorem using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They characterize how deviations from rotational invariance modify the eigenvalue spectrum, potentially leading to normality or violating the disk/annulus support predicted by the single ring theorem.
conclusion: The work clarifies the limits of the single ring theorem for more general non-Hermitian random matrix ensembles and provides a framework for understanding spectral transitions in such systems.

title: Spatial Evolution Characteristics And Mechanism Analysis Of Induced Magnetic Fields In An Applied Field Magnetoplasmadynamic Discharge Device
authors: Lehui Cao, Haibin Tang, Junxue Ren, Zhiyuan Chen, Guangchuan Zhang, Yibai Wang, Yuzhe Sun, And Jinbin Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Lehui Cao, Haibin Tang, Junxue Ren, Zhiyuan Chen, Guangchuan Zhang, Yibai Wang, Yuzhe Sun, and Jinbin Cao

The induced magnetic field in an applied field magnetoplasmadynamic discharge device is a key physical quantity for plasma transport and electromagnetic feedback in the plasma discharge process. To clarify its spatial evolution and the associated driving mechanisms under steady operating conditions,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045203] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes the spatial evolution and driving mechanisms of induced magnetic fields in an applied-field magnetoplasmadynamic (AF-MPD) discharge device under steady operating conditions.
motivation: The induced magnetic field governs plasma transport and electromagnetic feedback in magnetoplasmadynamic thrusters, yet its spatial structure and underlying mechanisms are not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the induced magnetic field distribution in an AF-MPD discharge device, likely combining experimental magnetic probe measurements with plasma discharge modeling to identify the driving mechanisms.
result: The study reveals the spatial evolution of the induced magnetic field in the discharge channel and identifies the dominant physical mechanisms (e.g., Hall current, plasma convection) responsible for its generation and distribution.
conclusion: Understanding the induced magnetic field dynamics provides insight into electromagnetic feedback and plasma acceleration in AF-MPD devices, informing thruster design and performance optimization.

title: Two-dimensional Spectroscopy Of Bosonic Collective Excitations In Disordered Many-body Systems
authors: Alex Gómez-Salvador, Ivan Morera, Marios H. Michael, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Danica Pavicevic, Albert Liu, Andrea Cavalleri, And Eugene Demler
abstract:
Author(s): Alex Gómez-Salvador, Ivan Morera, Marios H. Michael, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Danica Pavicevic, Albert Liu, Andrea Cavalleri, and Eugene Demler

We present a theoretical approach for computing and analyzing two-dimensional spectroscopy of bosonic collective excitations in disordered many-body systems. Specifically, we employ the Keldysh formalism to derive, within a nonperturbative treatment of disorder effects, the third-order nonlinear res…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043031] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a theoretical framework for computing two-dimensional spectroscopy of bosonic collective excitations in disordered many-body systems using the Keldysh formalism.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear spectroscopic signatures of collective excitations in disordered many-body systems is important for interpreting experiments in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors employ the Keldysh formalism to derive the third-order nonlinear response within a nonperturbative treatment of disorder effects.
result: They obtain expressions for two-dimensional spectra that capture the interplay of bosonic collective excitations and disorder.
conclusion: The approach provides a theoretical tool for analyzing 2D spectroscopy data in disordered quantum materials.

title: Experimental Limit On Neutron Orbital Angular Momentum Detection Using Polarized $^{3}\mathrm{He}$
authors: D. Sarenac, O. Lailey, D. V. Garrad, P. R. Vadnere, N. Shentevski, C. W. Clark, D. G. Cory, J. P. Cotter, H. Ekinci, M. G. Huber, J. W. Paster, Y. Tzeng, D. Alba Venero, And D. A. Pushin
abstract:
Author(s): D. Sarenac, O. Lailey, D. V. Garrad, P. R. Vadnere, N. Shentevski, C. W. Clark, D. G. Cory, J. P. Cotter, H. Ekinci, M. G. Huber, J. W. Paster, Y. Tzeng, D. Alba Venero, and D. A. Pushin

A recent proposal suggested that neutron orbital angular momentum (OAM) states could be detected via spin-polarized absorption in polarized [MATH], with predicted cross-section variations linked to the neutron’s OAM. We experimentally tested this hypothesis using spin-polarized neutron be…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043027] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: An experimental search places limits on detecting neutron orbital angular momentum via spin-polarized absorption in polarized helium-3.
motivation: A recent proposal suggested that neutron OAM states could be detected through cross-section variations in spin-polarized 3He absorption, motivating an experimental test.
method: The authors used a spin-polarized neutron beam and a polarized 3He target to measure absorption cross sections and search for signatures of neutron OAM.
result: No evidence for the predicted OAM-dependent cross-section variation was observed, yielding an experimental upper limit on the effect.
conclusion: The proposed detection mechanism is not supported by the experiment, constraining future neutron OAM detection schemes using polarized 3He.

title: Chiral-mode Control Around A Hermitian Diabolic Point In Discrete non-Hermitian Coupled Resonators
authors: Kota Yagi, Takahiro Uemura, Yuto Moritake, Adam Mock, And Masaya Notomi
abstract:
Author(s): Kota Yagi, Takahiro Uemura, Yuto Moritake, Adam Mock, and Masaya Notomi

Motivated by the prospect of chiral-mode control in compact photonic systems, we analyze discrete coupled single-mode resonators. Using the minimal three-resonator model, we show that an infinitesimal complex on-site perturbation near a Hermitian diabolic point (DP) induces chiral-mode selection, go…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043022] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes chiral-mode control around a Hermitian diabolic point in discrete non-Hermitian coupled resonators using a minimal three-resonator model.
motivation: Motivated by the prospect of chiral-mode control in compact photonic systems, the authors study discrete coupled single-mode resonators.
method: They use a minimal three-resonator model and introduce an infinitesimal complex on-site perturbation near a Hermitian diabolic point.
result: The perturbation induces chiral-mode selection, enabling control of chiral modes in the coupled resonator system.
conclusion: The findings provide a mechanism for chiral-mode control in compact photonic devices, potentially useful for integrated photonics.

title: Symmetric Mass Generation Of Interacting Chiral Fermions On A One-dimensional Lattice Without Fermion Doubling
authors: V. A. Zakharov, Atsushi Ueda, Frank Verstraete, And C. W. J. Beenakker
abstract:
Author(s): V. A. Zakharov, Atsushi Ueda, Frank Verstraete, and C. W. J. Beenakker

Symmetric mass generation is the interaction-induced opening of a fermion gap without spontaneous symmetry breaking. The anomaly-free 3–4–5–0 model of Wang and Wen provides a minimal one-dimensional setting for this phenomenon, but a direct lattice realization faces two obstacles: fermion doubling f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043009] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper realizes symmetric mass generation—an interaction-induced fermion gap without symmetry breaking—for chiral fermions on a one-dimensional lattice while avoiding fermion doubling.
motivation: Symmetric mass generation is a key phenomenon, and the anomaly-free 3–4–5–0 model offers a minimal one-dimensional setting, but a direct lattice realization faces obstacles such as fermion doubling.
method: The authors construct a lattice model, likely using interacting fermions and possibly tensor-network or numerical techniques, to circumvent fermion doubling and realize the 3–4–5–0 model.
result: They demonstrate symmetric mass generation on a one-dimensional lattice without fermion doubling, providing a concrete lattice realization of the interacting chiral fermion model.
conclusion: This work establishes a viable lattice platform for studying symmetric mass generation and anomaly-free chiral fermions in one dimension.

title: Topological Defects Organize Thermally Excited Vortical Phonons In Two-dimensional Crystals
authors: Wei-Shuo Lo, Yi-Jie Pang, Yi-Cheng Zhao, And Lin I
abstract:
Author(s): Wei-Shuo Lo, Yi-Jie Pang, Yi-Cheng Zhao, and Lin I

Thermal phonons in crystals are typically described in Fourier space, leaving open how disordered thermal vibrations are organized in real space-time. Recent work on two-dimensional crystals identified thermally excited vortical phonons—vorticity waves composed of traveling vortices with varying sha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043015] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how topological defects organize thermally excited vortical phonons in two-dimensional crystals, providing a real-space picture of thermal vibrations beyond Fourier description.
motivation: Thermal phonons are typically described in Fourier space, leaving open how disordered thermal vibrations are organized in real space-time.
method: Likely employs molecular dynamics simulations or analysis of two-dimensional crystal models to identify vortical phonon modes and their connection to topological defects.
result: Vortical phonons, composed of traveling vortices with varying shapes, are found to be organized by topological defects in the crystal.
conclusion: Topological defects play a key role in structuring thermal phonon fields in two-dimensional crystals, bridging real-space and Fourier descriptions.

title: Hierarchy Of Collective Ordering In Swarmalator Systems
authors: Hyunsuk Hong, Junghyo Jo, And Daniel D. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunsuk Hong, Junghyo Jo, and Daniel D. Lee

An exactly solvable multispecies spherical spin model is introduced to study the collective equilibrium states of swarmalators, mobile oscillators with coupled spatial and phase degrees of freedom. A unified description of the resulting hierarchy of states, their transitions, and their fundamental relationship to noisy Kuramoto dynamics is provided.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042001] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: An exactly solvable multispecies spherical spin model is used to describe collective ordering and phase transitions in swarmalator systems, connecting them to noisy Kuramoto dynamics.
motivation: Swarmalators are mobile oscillators with coupled spatial and phase degrees of freedom, and a unified understanding of their collective equilibrium states and transitions is lacking.
method: The authors introduce an exactly solvable multispecies spherical spin model and analyze its equilibrium states and transitions, mapping the results onto noisy Kuramoto dynamics.
result: They obtain a hierarchy of collective states and their transitions, providing a unified description of swarmalator ordering.
conclusion: The work clarifies the fundamental relationship between swarmalator collective behavior and noisy Kuramoto dynamics within a solvable statistical-mechanics framework.

title: Electronic Structure And Dynamical Correlations In Antiferromagnetic ${\mathrm{BiFeO}}_{3}$
authors: Yihan Wu, Mario Caserta, Tommaso Chiarotti, And Nicola Marzari
abstract:
Author(s): Yihan Wu, Mario Caserta, Tommaso Chiarotti, and Nicola Marzari

We study the electronic structure and dynamical correlations in antiferromagnetic [MATH], a prototypical room-temperature multiferroic, using a variety of static and dynamical first-principles methods. Conventional static Hubbard corrections ([MATH]) incor…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033375] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of the electronic structure and dynamical correlations in antiferromagnetic BiFeO3 using static (DFT+U) and dynamical (beyond-static) methods.
motivation: BiFeO3 is a prototypical room-temperature multiferroic, and its electronic structure and correlation effects are central to understanding its functional properties.
method: Static Hubbard-corrected DFT (DFT+U) is compared with dynamical first-principles approaches that capture frequency-dependent correlations, applied to the antiferromagnetic phase.
result: The authors show that conventional static Hubbard corrections are insufficient and that dynamical correlations qualitatively change the description of the electronic structure of BiFeO3.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of multiferroic BiFeO3 requires dynamical treatment of electronic correlations beyond static DFT+U.

title: Spin Nematic Liquid Crystal And Scalar Spin Chirality In Tetragonal Lattice ${\mathrm{YbMnBi}}_{2}$
authors: Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Neutron scattering experiments on

tldr: Neutron scattering on YbMnBi2 reveals a field-induced dynamic spin nematic state whose scalar spin chirality drives anomalous Hall and Nernst effects in the paramagnetic phase.
motivation: Magnetic materials hosting nontrivial spin textures can generate large anomalous transport responses, but the microscopic origin of such effects in the paramagnetic regime of tetragonal YbMnBi2 was unclear.
method: Elastic and inelastic neutron scattering experiments on YbMnBi2 under applied magnetic fields, combined with transport measurements and analysis of spin nematic order and scalar spin chirality.
result: A dynamic spin nematic liquid-crystal state forms under field, producing scalar spin chirality that generates anomalous Hall and Nernst signals even in the paramagnetic phase.
conclusion: The work establishes a coupling between dynamic spin nematicity and chirality-driven anomalous transport in YbMnBi2, linking frustrated magnetism to emergent topological transport phenomena.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
