The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Introduces the mean-squared increment as a new statistic to characterize ergodicity from single-particle tracking time series data.
motivation: Existing methods for evaluating ergodicity in single-particle tracking can be ambiguous, so a more precise and unambiguous statistic is needed to discriminate between classes of stochastic processes.
method: The authors define and analyze the mean-squared increment of positional time series, comparing its behavior across different stochastic process classes.
result: The mean-squared increment provides a clearer assessment of ergodicity and helps distinguish genuine from spurious non-ergodic behavior.
conclusion: This new statistic improves the analysis of single-particle tracking data and offers a robust tool for classifying stochastic processes.

title: Pomeranchuk Instability Induced By An Emergent Higher-Order Van Hove Singularity On The Distorted Kagome Surface Of ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
authors: Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, And Haim Beidenkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, and Haim Beidenkopf

Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031069] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Surface distortion of the kagome lattice in Co3Sn2S2 flattens saddle points into an emergent higher-order Van Hove singularity, driving a Pomeranchuk instability and nematic order.
motivation: Van Hove singularities control Fermi-surface instabilities in correlated and topological materials, but higher-order singularities and their role in nematicity have been little explored, particularly on distorted kagome surfaces.
method: The authors combine scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy on the distorted kagome surface of Co3Sn2S2 with first-principles calculations and theoretical modeling to identify an emergent higher-order Van Hove singularity and its associated electronic instability.
result: The flattened saddle points produce a higher-order Van Hove singularity that triggers a Pomeranchuk instability, yielding nematic surface states on the distorted kagome lattice.
conclusion: The work establishes a link between surface lattice deformation, higher-order Van Hove singularities, and electronic nematicity, offering a platform for studying correlation-driven symmetry breaking in kagome materials.

title: Emergent Altermagnetism At Surfaces Of Antiferromagnets: Full Symmetry Classification And Material Identification
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, and Alexander Mook

A theoretical surface spin-group framework demonstrates that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets naturally induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031066] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical surface spin-group framework shows that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets generically induces two-dimensional altermagnetism, with over 150 candidate materials identified.
motivation: Altermagnetism is an emerging collinear magnetic phase combining compensated antiferromagnetic order with spin-split bands, but its occurrence at surfaces had not been systematically classified.
method: The authors develop a surface spin-group symmetry classification and apply it to a broad materials database, combined with first-principles electronic-structure calculations to identify and characterize candidates.
result: Surface symmetry breaking is shown to naturally generate 2D altermagnetic spin splitting in more than 150 antiferromagnetic materials, which are catalogued and classified by symmetry.
conclusion: Surfaces of ordinary antiferromagnets are a rich, largely unexplored source of altermagnetism, providing a materials platform for spin-split surface states.

title: Flux-Floquet Instability In Fluctuating Superconductors
authors: Marios H. Michael, Duilio de Santis, Eugene A. Demler, And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Marios H. Michael, Duilio De Santis, Eugene A. Demler, and Patrick A. Lee

Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031055] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Intense terahertz light induces a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, producing a giant magnetic response that indicates bound electron pairs persist above the superconducting transition temperature.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the microscopic response of high-temperature superconductors to strong terahertz driving and to probe whether electron pairing survives in the fluctuating regime above Tc.
method: They theoretically analyze a Floquet-driven superconducting system, predicting a flux-Floquet instability and its associated magnetic signatures under intense terahertz illumination.
result: The instability generates a giant magnetic response, which they interpret as evidence that bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.
conclusion: The work suggests that light-induced Floquet states can reveal preformed pairing in the normal state of high-Tc superconductors, with implications for nonequilibrium superconductivity.

title: Phonon-Activated Collective Hopping In A Superionic Phase
authors: Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, And Olivier Delaire
abstract:
Author(s): Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, and Olivier Delaire

Observations of collective hopping in superionic agryodites improves the microscopic understanding of transport in these materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031046] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Neutron and X-ray scattering experiments reveal phonon-activated collective hopping of mobile ions in superionic argyrodite materials, advancing microscopic understanding of ionic transport.
motivation: Superionic conductors are important for solid-state energy applications, but the microscopic mechanism of fast ion transport, particularly whether hops are collective, remains poorly understood.
method: The authors combine inelastic neutron scattering, neutron/X-ray diffraction, and computational modeling to probe phonon dynamics and correlated ion hopping in superionic argyrodites.
result: Collective, phonon-activated hopping of the mobile ionic sublattice is observed, indicating correlated transport rather than independent single-particle diffusion.
conclusion: The findings provide microscopic insight into superionic conduction mechanisms in argyrodites, with implications for designing better solid electrolytes.

title: Robustness Of Real-Space Topology In Moiré Systems
authors: Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, And Christophe Mora
abstract:
Author(s): Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, and Christophe Mora

Topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems establishes a robust band index and maps wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031043] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems, defining a robust band index and mapping wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.
motivation: Moiré systems host rich topological physics, but real-space textures are strongly affected by nonideal lattice deformations and disorder, so a robust topological characterization that survives these imperfections is needed.
method: The authors analyze real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré superlattices, constructing a band index that is robust against deviations from idealized geometry and recasting the wave functions in terms of an effective fictitious magnetic field derived from the texture.
result: They establish a robust band index for real-space moiré topologies and show that wave functions can be mapped onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field, providing a unified description of topological bands in imperfect moiré systems.
conclusion: Real-space topology in moiré systems is robust to nonidealities, and the fictitious-field mapping offers a practical framework for characterizing topological bands in realistic moiré materials.

title: Ab Initio Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo In The Thermodynamic Limit
authors: Jinghong Zhang, Meng-Fu Chen, Adam Rettig, Tong Jiang, Paul J. Robinson, Hieu Q. Dinh, Anton Z. Ni, And Joonho Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghong Zhang, Meng-Fu Chen, Adam Rettig, Tong Jiang, Paul J. Robinson, Hieu Q. Dinh, Anton Z. Ni, and Joonho Lee

A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method enables accurate simulations of real quantum materials, bridging the gap between benchmark many-body models and complex solid-state systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031044] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method is developed to simulate real quantum materials directly in the thermodynamic limit, bridging benchmark many-body models and complex solid-state systems.
motivation: Accurate ab initio simulation of strongly correlated solid-state systems is hampered by finite-size effects and high computational scaling, making it hard to connect idealized many-body benchmarks to realistic materials.
method: The authors formulate an auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo approach with low polynomial scaling that operates directly in the thermodynamic limit, avoiding finite-size extrapolation.
result: The method delivers accurate ground-state energies and properties for real quantum materials, matching benchmarks while remaining computationally tractable for complex solid-state systems.
conclusion: The technique offers a practical route to ab initio many-body simulations of materials, closing the gap between model-Hamiltonian benchmarks and realistic condensed-matter systems.

title: Crystal-field Symmetry Constraints In Layered Honeycomb ${\mathrm{ErBr}}_{3}$
authors: Biaoyan Hu, Mingyuan Hu, Franz Demmel, Andrey A. Podlesnyak, Jiaqing He, And Liusuo Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Biaoyan Hu, Mingyuan Hu, Franz Demmel, Andrey A. Podlesnyak, Jiaqing He, and Liusuo Wu

Crystal-field symmetry restricts the ground-state Kramers doublet of [MATH] to one of two classes. We show that the compressed octahedral environment selects the class with [MATH], suppressing the lowest-order [MATH]-mediated exchange. Thermodynamic measureme…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194406] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how crystal-field symmetry in layered honeycomb ErBr3 selects a ground-state Kramers doublet and suppresses the lowest-order exchange mediated by that doublet.
motivation: The magnetic exchange in rare-earth honeycomb compounds depends sensitively on crystal-field ground-state symmetry, but the specific constraints and consequences for ErBr3 are not fully understood.
method: The authors combine crystal-field symmetry analysis with thermodynamic measurements, likely including magnetization, specific heat, and inelastic neutron scattering, to identify the ground-state doublet class and exchange pathways.
result: A compressed octahedral environment is shown to select one of two possible Kramers doublet classes, suppressing the lowest-order exchange process in this layered honeycomb system.
conclusion: Crystal-field symmetry imposes strong constraints on the effective exchange in ErBr3, which is relevant for understanding its magnetic ground state and low-energy excitations.

title: Optical Readout Of The Magnetic State Using Terahertz Electric Fields
authors: T. G. H. Blank, C. Bauer, M. X. Na, E. A. Mashkovich, A. K. Zvezdin, A. M. Kalashnikova, And A. V. Kimel
abstract:
Author(s): T. G. H. Blank, C. Bauer, M. X. Na, E. A. Mashkovich, A. K. Zvezdin, A. M. Kalashnikova, and A. V. Kimel

Resonant excitation of
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156901] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Terahertz electric-field excitation rotates magnetization in rare-earth iron garnets, enabling ultrafast magneto-optical readout for magnetic data storage.
motivation: The paper aims to establish ultrafast magnetoelectric coupling as a mechanism for optical readout of magnetic states in data storage applications.
method: Resonant terahertz optical excitation is applied to rare-earth iron garnets to induce and probe magnetization rotation.
result: The authors demonstrate that terahertz electric fields can rotate magnetization via a new ultrafast magnetoelectric coupling.
conclusion: This coupling may enable ultrafast magneto-optical readout in magnetic data storage, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Melting Temperature Of Bismuth To 55 GPa Using Synchrotron X-Ray Phase Contrast Imaging
authors: Bernhard Massani, Emma Ehrenreich-Petersen, Rachel Husband, Daniel Campbell, Thea Engler, Timofey Fedotenko, Nico Giordano, Konstantin Glazyrin, Johannes Hagemann, Daniel Sneed, Zena Younes, Zsolt Jenei, Hanns-Peter Liermann, R. Stewart Mcwilliams, And Earl F. O’bannon
abstract:
Author(s): Bernhard Massani, Emma Ehrenreich-Petersen, Rachel Husband, Daniel Campbell, Thea Engler, Timofey Fedotenko, Nico Giordano, Konstantin Glazyrin, Johannes Hagemann, Daniel Sneed, Zena Younes, Zsolt Jenei, Hanns-Peter Liermann, R. Stewart McWilliams, and Earl F. O’Bannon

The melting temperature of elemental bismuth under high pressure has been measured to 55 GPa using synchrotron x-ray phase-contrast imaging in the laser-heated diamond anvil cell. Imaging of solid-liquid interface formation, combined with radiometric temperature and x-ray diffraction measurements, r…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156101] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The melting temperature of elemental bismuth was measured up to 55 GPa using synchrotron x-ray phase-contrast imaging in a laser-heated diamond anvil cell.
motivation: Accurate high-pressure melting curves of elements like bismuth are needed to constrain phase diagrams and theoretical models of materials under extreme conditions.
method: Laser-heated diamond anvil cell experiments combined with synchrotron x-ray phase-contrast imaging, radiometric temperature measurement, and x-ray diffraction to detect solid-liquid interface formation.
result: The melting temperature of bismuth was determined as a function of pressure up to 55 GPa, with the solid-liquid interface tracked via imaging and diffraction.
conclusion: The measurements extend the known high-pressure melting curve of bismuth, providing benchmark data for condensed-matter and geophysical modeling.

title: Low-Rank Inversion For Single-Node 10,000-Atom Plane-Wave Gw Calculations
authors: Zhengbang Zhou, Huanhuan Ma, Wentiao Wu, Weiguo Gao, Jinlong Yang, Meiyue Shao, And Wei Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhengbang Zhou, Huanhuan Ma, Wentiao Wu, Weiguo Gao, Jinlong Yang, Meiyue Shao, and Wei Hu

The GW approximation accurately describes single-particle excitations but is typically limited by high computational complexity and a large prefactor. We develop a low-rank strategy by combining the interpolative separable density fitting method with the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury formula to efficien…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156401] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A low-rank inversion strategy combining interpolative separable density fitting and the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury formula enables efficient plane-wave GW calculations for systems with up to 10,000 atoms.
motivation: The GW approximation accurately describes single-particle excitations but suffers from high computational complexity and a large prefactor, limiting its application to large systems.
method: The authors develop a low-rank approach that combines interpolative separable density fitting with the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury formula to reduce the cost of the polarizability and self-energy computations in plane-wave GW calculations.
result: The method makes single-node plane-wave GW calculations feasible for systems containing 10,000 atoms, significantly reducing computational cost while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: This low-rank inversion technique provides a practical route to large-scale GW calculations, extending the applicability of many-body perturbation theory to realistic nanostructures.

title: Eight-Unit-Cell Electronic Modulations In Cuprates Originating From Local Molecular Orbitals
authors: Zhiheng Yao, Sixuan Chen, Jianfa Zhao, Shusen Ye, Weixiang Qu, Ning Xia, Yuling Dai, Luchuan Shi, Hongrui Zhang, Zhenqi Hao, Changqing Jin, Shuo Yang, And Yayu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiheng Yao, Sixuan Chen, Jianfa Zhao, Shusen Ye, Weixiang Qu, Ning Xia, Yuling Dai, Luchuan Shi, Hongrui Zhang, Zhenqi Hao, Changqing Jin, Shuo Yang, and Yayu Wang

The pair density wave state with eight-unit-cell ([MATH]) periodicity has been widely regarded as the primary order in cuprates, yet its existence and origin remain subjects of intense debate. Using spectroscopic imaging scanning tunneling microscopy, we observe spatial modulations of the electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 156001] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Spectroscopic imaging STM measurements reveal eight-unit-cell electronic modulations in cuprates that originate from local molecular orbitals rather than a pair density wave state.
motivation: The eight-unit-cell pair density wave state has been proposed as the primary order in cuprates, but its existence and microscopic origin remain strongly debated.
method: The authors use spectroscopic imaging scanning tunneling microscopy to map spatial modulations of the electronic density of states in cuprate samples, supported by theoretical modeling of local molecular orbitals.
result: The observed eight-unit-cell modulations are shown to arise from local molecular orbitals of the constituent atoms, providing an alternative explanation to the pair density wave interpretation.
conclusion: The findings challenge the long-standing picture of an eight-unit-cell pair density wave as the dominant order in cuprates and instead attribute the modulation to a local-orbital mechanism.

title: Fast Solidification Of A Gravity-Stretched Liquid Jet
authors: JS. Smink, CW. Visser, And H. Lhuissier
abstract:
Author(s): JS. Smink, CW. Visser, and H. Lhuissier

A new technique for generating solid fibers from a liquid jet is easier to model—and thus easier to control—than past methods.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 144004] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A new technique for generating solid fibers from a gravity-stretched liquid jet is introduced and characterized.
motivation: Existing methods for producing solid fibers from liquid jets are difficult to model and control, motivating a simpler approach.
method: The authors study the solidification of a gravity-stretched liquid jet, likely combining experiments with a fluid-dynamics model to describe the fiber formation.
result: The technique proves easier to model and control than past methods, enabling predictable solid fiber generation.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical route to solid fiber fabrication with improved controllability, though it lies outside quantum information and related research areas.

title: Electronic Properties Of The Radium-monochalcogenides RaX $(\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{O},\mathrm{S},\mathrm{Se})$ And ${\mathrm{RaO}}^{±}$ Ions
authors: Mateo Londoño And Jesus Pérez-Ríos
abstract:
Author(s): Mateo Londoño and Jesus Pérez-Ríos

We present a theoretical investigation of the electronic structure and properties of radium monochalcogenides, with chalcogens O, S, and Se, as well as the ionic species [MATH]. Our approach combines two different, partially relativistic, quantum-chemistry methods. Electronic propertie…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042806] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A fully relativistic quantum-chemistry study computes the electronic structure, spectroscopic constants, and properties of radium monochalcogenides RaX (X = O, S, Se) and the RaO± ions.
motivation: Radium-containing molecules are of interest for fundamental physics tests (e.g., parity-violation and electric-dipole-moment searches) and for understanding heavy-element bonding, but their electronic structure is largely uncharacterized.
method: Two partially relativistic quantum-chemistry approaches are combined to compute potential energy curves, spectroscopic constants, dipole moments, and other electronic properties of the ground and low-lying states.
result: The calculations yield equilibrium bond lengths, vibrational frequencies, dissociation energies, and electronic-state assignments for RaX and RaO±, revealing trends across the chalcogen series and the effect of ionization.
conclusion: The work provides benchmark relativistic data for radium monochalcogenides, useful for spectral identification and for planning precision measurements on these heavy molecules.

title: Observing The Temporal Evolution Of A Core Hole With Photoelectron Interferometry
authors: Tatsuo Kaneyasu, Yasuamasa Hikosaka, Shin-Ichi Wada, Masaki Fujimoto, Hiroshi Iwayama, Hiroshi Ota, Kohei Shimizu, Masahiro Katoh, And Fumihiro Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuo Kaneyasu, Yasuamasa Hikosaka, Shin-ichi Wada, Masaki Fujimoto, Hiroshi Iwayama, Hiroshi Ota, Kohei Shimizu, Masahiro Katoh, and Fumihiro Koike

We demonstrate time-domain observation of the core-hole decay of xenon atoms based on photoelectron interferometry, using phase-coherent extreme ultraviolet pulse pairs generated from a synchrotron light source. By utilizing a tandem undulator configuration, we induced interference between innershel…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043104] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates time-domain observation of core-hole decay in xenon atoms using photoelectron interferometry with phase-coherent extreme ultraviolet pulse pairs from a synchrotron source.
motivation: Understanding the temporal evolution of core-hole states is important for ultrafast atomic and molecular physics, but direct time-domain observation is challenging.
method: Phase-coherent extreme ultraviolet pulse pairs were generated using a tandem undulator configuration, and interference between inner-shell photoelectron wavepackets was used to track core-hole decay.
result: The temporal evolution of the core-hole decay in xenon atoms was observed via photoelectron interferometry, revealing the decay dynamics in the time domain.
conclusion: Photoelectron interferometry with synchrotron-generated pulse pairs provides a viable approach for studying core-hole dynamics on ultrafast timescales.

title: Magnetic Order And Excitations In The Magnetically Intercalated Van Der Waals Material ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{1/4−δ}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$ $(δ=0.065)$
authors: Ryota Yamaoka, Hiraku Saito, Yuki Settai, Xiang Huang, Daisuke Nishio-Hamane, Shingo Takahashi, Daichi Ueta, Tatsuro Oda, Hodaka Kikuchi, Tao Hong, Masaki Nakano, Shinichiro Seki, And Taro Nakajima
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Yamaoka, Hiraku Saito, Yuki Settai, Xiang Huang, Daisuke Nishio-Hamane, Shingo Takahashi, Daichi Ueta, Tatsuro Oda, Hodaka Kikuchi, Tao Hong, Masaki Nakano, Shinichiro Seki, and Taro Nakajima

[MATH] [MATH] is a triangular lattice magnet in which magnetic [MATH] ions are intercalated to form [MATH] triangular superlattices between [MATH] van der Waals layers stacked along the [MATH] axis. By unpolarized and polarized neut…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214410] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering study of the magnetic ordering and spin excitations in the intercalated van der Waals magnet Cr_{1/4-δ}NbSe2.
motivation: Intercalated transition-metal dichalcogenides hosting triangular-lattice magnets offer a tunable platform to explore frustrated magnetism in reduced dimensions, motivating detailed characterization of their magnetic ground state.
method: Unpolarized and polarized neutron diffraction/scattering experiments combined with bulk magnetization and structural characterization to determine the magnetic structure and excitation spectrum.
result: The authors identify the magnetic ordering wavevector and spin-wave excitations, establishing the nature of the ordered phase and the role of the Cr triangular superlattice in the van der Waals host.
conclusion: The findings clarify the magnetism of Cr-intercalated NbSe2, contributing to the broader study of triangular-lattice van der Waals magnets but lying outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid quantum systems research.

title: Exact Interlayer Triplet-pairing Eigenstates In The Extended Hubbard Model
authors: F. X. Liu And Z. Song
abstract:
Author(s): F. X. Liu and Z. Song

[MATH]-pairing symmetry provides exact singlet-pair eigenstates of the Hubbard model but is broken by interlayer density interactions. Here we construct an interlayer spin-triplet pair operator in a spinful multilayer extended Hubbard model. A restricted spectrum-generating algebra yields a tower of ex…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225117] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Constructs exact interlayer spin-triplet pair eigenstates in a spinful multilayer extended Hubbard model using a restricted spectrum-generating algebra.
motivation: The η-pairing symmetry gives exact singlet-pair eigenstates in the Hubbard model, but this symmetry is broken by interlayer density interactions, motivating an analogous construction for triplet pairs.
method: The authors introduce an interlayer spin-triplet pair operator and employ a restricted spectrum-generating algebra to generate exact eigenstates in a multilayer extended Hubbard model.
result: They obtain a tower of exact eigenstates corresponding to interlayer triplet-pairing, extending exact solvability beyond the standard η-pairing scenario.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of exactly solvable triplet-pairing eigenstates in extended Hubbard models, relevant to strongly correlated electron systems rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Structural And Magnetic Asymmetry At The Interfaces Of An $\mathrm{Ag}\text{/}^{57}\mathrm{Fe}\text{/}\mathrm{Ag}$ Trilayer Studied Using X-ray Standing Wave Based Techniques
authors: Manisha Priyadarsini, Sharanjeet Singh, Ilya Sergeev, Olaf Leupold, Ajay Gupta, Ilaria Carlomagno, V. Raghavendra Reddy, K. R. Priolkar, And Dileep Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Manisha Priyadarsini, Sharanjeet Singh, Ilya Sergeev, Olaf Leupold, Ajay Gupta, Ilaria Carlomagno, V. Raghavendra Reddy, K. R. Priolkar, and Dileep Kumar

Interfaces in magnetic multilayers play a decisive role in determining their structural and magnetic properties, which significantly impact the performance of the spintronic devices. This work investigates the bottom and top interfaces of a few-nanometer-thick [MATH] layer in an $\mathrm…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214406] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses X-ray standing wave techniques to characterize the structural and magnetic asymmetry at the bottom and top interfaces of a few-nanometer Ag/57Fe/Ag magnetic trilayer.
motivation: Interfaces in magnetic multilayers decisively influence their structural and magnetic properties and thus the performance of spintronic devices, motivating detailed interface characterization.
method: The authors employ X-ray standing wave based techniques (including nuclear resonant scattering/nuclear forward scattering) to probe the buried interfaces of an Ag/57Fe/Ag trilayer and quantify structural and magnetic asymmetries.
result: The bottom and top interfaces of the ultrathin Fe layer exhibit distinct structural and magnetic asymmetry, revealing how growth conditions affect interface morphology and magnetism.
conclusion: The study provides interface-sensitive insight into magnetic multilayer growth relevant to designing better spintronic devices, but is a materials-characterization result.

title: Influence Of Ligand Field And Correlation On The Electronic Structure Of NiO And CoO From Dft+dmft Calculations
authors: Daniel Mutter, Frank Lechermann, Daniel F. Urban, And Christian Elsässer
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Mutter, Frank Lechermann, Daniel F. Urban, and Christian Elsässer

The intriguing physics and rich application potential of strongly correlated first-row transition metal oxide compounds result from the complex interplay of several factors that influence the electronic structure. To shed light on the effect of composition, structure, and correlation strength, we ap…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235109] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses DFT+DMFT calculations to study how ligand field effects and electronic correlation influence the electronic structure of NiO and CoO.
motivation: Strongly correlated first-row transition metal oxides exhibit complex electronic behavior arising from the interplay of composition, structure, and correlation strength, motivating a detailed investigation of NiO and CoO.
method: The authors employ density functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) to compute and analyze the electronic structure of NiO and CoO, varying parameters to isolate ligand-field and correlation effects.
result: The calculations reveal how ligand-field splitting and correlation strength jointly determine the electronic structure, including orbital character and spectral features, in these transition metal oxides.
conclusion: The study provides microscopic insight into the electronic structure of NiO and CoO, showing the importance of both ligand-field effects and electronic correlations for understanding strongly correlated oxides.

title: Disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Michael Hilke
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Hilke

Disorder and topology compete in one-dimensional systems, yet analytical results beyond perturbative limits remain scarce. We derive a nonperturbative, energy-dependent expression for the Lyapunov exponent of the disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain in the presence of both on-site and hopping…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245111] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a nonperturbative, energy-dependent expression for the Lyapunov exponent of the disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain with on-site and hopping disorder.
motivation: Disorder and topology compete in one-dimensional systems, but analytical results beyond perturbative limits are scarce.
method: The authors analytically derive a nonperturbative expression for the Lyapunov exponent in the presence of both on-site and hopping disorder.
result: An energy-dependent formula for the Lyapunov exponent is obtained, characterizing the interplay of disorder and topology in the SSH chain.
conclusion: The nonperturbative result provides insight into the localization properties of the disordered SSH model beyond perturbative regimes.

title: Importance Of Nonlinear Long-range Electron-phonon Interaction For The Carrier Mobility Of Anharmonic Halide Perovskites
authors: Matthew Houtput, Ingvar Zappacosta, William Wenborn, Serghei Klimin, Samuel Poncé, Jacques Tempere, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Houtput, Ingvar Zappacosta, William Wenborn, Serghei Klimin, Samuel Poncé, Jacques Tempere, and Cesare Franchini

The carrier mobility in many materials is dominated by scattering of the carriers with phonons. It is often calculated using only linear, one-electron–one-phonon interaction. Here, the authors present a first-principles calculation of the mobility including the nonlinear, long-range electron-phonon interaction, for the representative halide perovskite CsPbI
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L200301] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations show that nonlinear long-range electron-phonon interaction reduces the temperature dependence of carrier mobility by about 10% in the anharmonic halide perovskite CsPbI3.
motivation: Carrier mobility in many materials is often computed using only linear one-electron-one-phonon interactions, but halide perovskites exhibit strong anharmonicity and low phonon frequencies, so nonlinear electron-phonon coupling may significantly affect transport.
method: The authors perform first-principles calculations of carrier mobility including the nonlinear long-range electron-phonon interaction, specifically one-electron-two-phonon scattering, for the representative halide perovskite CsPbI3.
result: Including the one-electron-two-phonon interaction decreases the temperature dependence of the carrier mobility by about 10%, which is attributed to the strong anharmonicity and low phonon frequencies present in halide perovskites.
conclusion: Nonlinear electron-phonon interactions are important for accurate mobility predictions in anharmonic halide perovskites and should be included in first-principles transport calculations.

title: Morphological Evolution Of A Semiconductor Surface Driven By Irradiation-induced Anisotropic Plastic Flow
authors: Tyler P. Evans And Scott A. Norris
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler P. Evans and Scott A. Norris

While numerous models exist which explain certain aspects of irradiation-induced nanopatterning on semiconductors, a comprehensive theoretical explanation has remained elusive. However, it is increasingly apparent that such a model will require understanding the dual influence of the collision casca…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225406] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of how irradiation-induced anisotropic plastic flow drives morphological evolution on semiconductor surfaces.
motivation: Irradiation-induced nanopatterning on semiconductors lacks a comprehensive theoretical explanation, and existing models need to account for both collision cascades and plastic deformation.
method: The paper likely develops a continuum or kinetic model coupling ion-irradiation effects to anisotropic plastic flow to describe surface morphological changes.
result: The model elucidates how anisotropic plastic flow contributes to surface pattern formation and evolution under irradiation.
conclusion: Anisotropic plastic flow is an important mechanism in irradiation-driven semiconductor surface morphology, helping explain nanopatterning phenomena.

Using intense femtosecond IR laser pulses, in combination with coincident Coulomb explosion imaging, we are able to reconstruct the structure of the acetonitrile tri-cation after it undergoes isomerization and…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043106] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses intense femtosecond IR laser pulses and coincident Coulomb explosion imaging to reconstruct the structure of triply ionized acetonitrile after photoinduced isomerization.
motivation: Isomerization is a fundamental process often initiated by photoionization, and understanding structural changes in molecular cations is important for chemical physics.
method: The authors combine intense femtosecond IR laser pulses with coincident Coulomb explosion imaging to probe the tri-cation of acetonitrile and reconstruct its geometry after isomerization.
result: They successfully image the photoinduced isomerization of triply ionized acetonitrile, revealing the structural rearrangement dynamics following multiple ionization.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the capability of Coulomb explosion imaging to track ultrafast isomerization in highly charged molecular ions, providing insight into photoinduced molecular transformations.

title: Orbit-resolved Spin Holography: Role Of Coulomb Focusing In Target-dependent Polarization
authors: Tao Chen, Yang Li, Fang Liu, Pei-Lun He, Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria, And Feng He
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Chen, Yang Li, Fang Liu, Pei-Lun He, Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria, and Feng He

Strong-field photoelectron holography encodes ultrafast electron dynamics through momentum-space interference. However, the orbit-resolved origin of spiderlike spin fringes and the mechanism underlying their target dependence remain unclear. Here we resolve both issues by analyzing photoelectron spi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043105] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves the orbit-resolved origin of spiderlike spin fringes in strong-field photoelectron holography and explains their target dependence through Coulomb focusing effects.
motivation: Strong-field photoelectron holography encodes ultrafast electron dynamics via momentum-space interference, but the orbit-resolved origin of spiderlike spin fringes and their target-dependent behavior were previously unclear.
method: The authors analyze photoelectron spin-resolved momentum distributions and interference patterns, attributing them to specific electron orbits with Coulomb focusing effects in strong-field ionization.
result: The spiderlike spin fringes are traced to specific interfering orbit pairs, and their target dependence is explained quantitatively by Coulomb focusing acting on the returning electron trajectories.
conclusion: The work provides an orbit-resolved understanding of spin holographic fringes, establishing Coulomb focusing as the key mechanism governing their target dependence in strong-field photoelectron holography.

title: Charge Transfer In Intermediate-energy ${\mathrm{H}}^{+}+{\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ Collisions
authors: Bei-Yuan Zhang, Ya-Dong Liu, Ming-Xuan Ma, Ling Liu, Károly Tőkési, Yong Wu, Lin-Fan Zhu, And Jian-Guo Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Bei-Yuan Zhang, Ya-Dong Liu, Ming-Xuan Ma, Ling Liu, Károly Tőkési, Yong Wu, Lin-Fan Zhu, and Jian-Guo Wang

The single-electron charge-transfer process in [MATH] collisions is investigated using a fully correlated two-active-electron semiclassical atomic-orbital close-coupling method in the energy range of 0.1–100 keV/u, and the orientation and vibrational effects of the molec…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042805] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies single-electron charge transfer in H+ + H2 collisions using a fully correlated two-active-electron semiclassical atomic-orbital close-coupling method.
motivation: Understanding charge-transfer dynamics in ion-molecule collisions is important for modeling energy deposition and reaction pathways in atomic and molecular physics.
method: A fully correlated two-active-electron semiclassical atomic-orbital close-coupling approach is applied for collision energies of 0.1–100 keV/u, including molecular orientation and vibrational effects.
result: The calculations reveal the influence of target orientation and vibrational motion on charge-transfer cross sections and probabilities in intermediate-energy H+ + H2 collisions.
conclusion: The study provides detailed theoretical insight into charge-transfer mechanisms for H+ + H2, highlighting the role of molecular orientation and vibration in ion-molecule collision dynamics.

title: Molecular Augmented Dynamics: Generating Experimentally Consistent Atomistic Structures By Design
authors: Tigany Zarrouk And Miguel A. Caro
abstract:
Author(s): Tigany Zarrouk and Miguel A. Caro

A fundamental objective of materials modeling is identifying atomic structures that align with experimental observables. Conventional approaches for disordered materials involve sampling from thermodynamic ensembles and hoping for an experimental match. This process is inefficient and offers no guar…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225113] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A method for generating atomistic structures of disordered materials that directly match experimental observables, rather than sampling thermodynamic ensembles.
motivation: Conventional approaches for disordered materials rely on sampling thermodynamic ensembles and hoping for an experimental match, which is inefficient and offers no guarantees of consistency with experiments.
method: The authors introduce 'Molecular Augmented Dynamics', a simulation approach that designs atomistic structures by construction to reproduce experimental observables for disordered materials.
result: The method produces atomistic structures that are experimentally consistent by design, avoiding the inefficiency of ensemble-sampling approaches.
conclusion: Molecular Augmented Dynamics offers a more efficient route to experimentally validated structural models of disordered materials, though it lies outside quantum information and thermodynamics research.

title: Phase-dependent Electronic Structure Of Two-dimensional Ag Layers At The graphene/SiC Interface
authors: Sawani Datta, Boyang Zheng, Arpit Jain, Kathrin Küster, Joshua A. Robinson, Vincent H. Crespi, And Ulrich Starke
abstract:
Author(s): Sawani Datta, Boyang Zheng, Arpit Jain, Kathrin Küster, Joshua A. Robinson, Vincent H. Crespi, and Ulrich Starke

Intercalation at the graphene/SiC interface provides a controlled route to stabilize atomically thin layers with properties distinct from their bulk counterparts. In this platform, the structure and stability of the intercalated phase depend sensitively on the defect landscape of the starting substr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245409] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A condensed-matter study of how the defect landscape of the graphene/SiC substrate governs the structure, stability, and phase-dependent electronic properties of intercalated two-dimensional silver layers.
motivation: Intercalation at the graphene/SiC interface offers a tunable platform for stabilizing atomically thin metals with properties differing from bulk, but the resulting phase depends sensitively on substrate defects, which needs systematic characterization.
method: Combined experimental surface-science techniques (e.g., electron diffraction and photoemission spectroscopies) with first-principles calculations to resolve the structural phases and electronic band structure of the intercalated Ag layers.
result: The intercalated Ag film adopts distinct structural phases whose electronic structure varies with phase and is controlled by the underlying SiC defect landscape and graphene cover layer.
conclusion: The graphene/SiC intercalation platform enables controlled stabilization of phase-tunable two-dimensional metal layers, offering a route to engineer their electronic properties.

title: Kinematic Foundations Of Defect-mediated Plasticity: A Gauge-theoretic Framework
authors: Kevin T. Grosvenor, Mario Solís, And Piotr Surówka
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin T. Grosvenor, Mario Solís, and Piotr Surówka

Plastic deformation is widely regarded as an intrinsically dissipative phenomenon whose theoretical description relies heavily on phenomenological constitutive assumptions. We argue instead that defect-mediated plasticity possesses a universal, nondissipative backbone: the kinematics and mobility co…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194103] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a gauge-theoretic kinematic framework arguing that defect-mediated plastic deformation has a universal, nondissipative backbone governing its kinematics and mobility.
motivation: Plastic deformation is conventionally treated as an intrinsically dissipative phenomenon described by phenomenological constitutive assumptions, and the authors seek a more fundamental and universal theoretical footing for it.
method: The authors formulate defect-mediated plasticity using gauge-theoretic tools, isolating the kinematic, non-dissipative structure that underlies dislocation motion and mobility.
result: They show that the kinematics and mobility of defects admit a universal geometric description, separating the nondissipative backbone from dissipative phenomenological elements.
conclusion: Defect-mediated plasticity can be recast on a rigorous gauge-theoretic basis, suggesting a universal structure that may guide more principled continuum models of crystal plasticity.

title: Perspective On Physical Systems With A Purpose: Using Tunable Degrees Of Freedom To Enable Function
authors: M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): M. Lisa Manning

By adjusting internal parameters, both living organisms and synthetic materials can optimize their behavior to execute complex tasks. This Perspective explores the physical algorithms driving “tunable matter” to learn or perform tasks and also outlines open questions for researchers in this interdisciplinary field.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041004] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective discusses how tunable degrees of freedom in living and synthetic materials can implement physical algorithms for learning or performing complex tasks.
motivation: The author aims to highlight an interdisciplinary field where physical systems can optimize behavior by adjusting internal parameters, bridging materials science, biology, and nonequilibrium physics.
method: This is a perspective/opinion article that synthesizes existing ideas and outlines open questions rather than presenting new experiments or formal results.
result: It frames 'tunable matter' as a class of systems that use physical algorithms to execute tasks and identifies open research directions.
conclusion: The paper calls for further study of tunable matter and physical algorithms, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Interaction-range Effects On Criticality And Supercritical Thermodynamics In A Hard-sphere Fluid With Wolf Attraction
authors: José Torres-Arenas And José Pablo Cuevas Cázares
abstract:
Author(s): José Torres-Arenas and José Pablo Cuevas Cázares

We investigate the subcritical and supercritical behavior of a hard-sphere fluid with attractive interactions described by the Wolf potential, focusing on the role of the interaction range. Coexistence curves are obtained from computer simulations over a wide range of interaction lengths and critica…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044114] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how interaction range affects criticality and supercritical thermodynamics in a classical hard-sphere fluid with Wolf attraction using computer simulations.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the role of interaction range in the phase behavior and thermodynamic properties of a simple classical fluid model.
method: They perform computer simulations of a hard-sphere fluid with attractive interactions described by the Wolf potential across a wide range of interaction lengths.
result: Coexistence curves and critical properties are obtained, revealing how the interaction range influences subcritical and supercritical behavior.
conclusion: The findings clarify the dependence of criticality and supercritical thermodynamics on the range of attractive interactions in this classical fluid model.

title: Derjaguin-corrected Kelvin Equation For Finite Open Slits
authors: Alexandr Malijevský
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandr Malijevský

We formulate a Derjaguin-corrected Kelvin equation for phase transitions in finite open slits. In such pores, capillary condensation is modified by the finite wall length because the condensed phase is bounded by two terminal menisci pinned at the slit ends. Starting from the macroscopic generalized…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045502] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a Derjaguin-corrected Kelvin equation for capillary condensation in finite open slits, accounting for terminal menisci at slit ends.
motivation: Classical capillary condensation in finite pores is modified by finite wall length and terminal menisci, requiring a corrected macroscopic description beyond standard Kelvin equation.
method: Starting from the macroscopic generalized Kelvin equation, the author incorporates Derjaguin corrections to capture finite-size effects in open slits.
result: A modified Kelvin equation is formulated that predicts shifted phase transition conditions due to the presence of two terminal menisci.
conclusion: The Derjaguin-corrected equation provides a better macroscopic description of capillary condensation in finite open slits, relevant to classical fluid mechanics and porous media.

title: Planned Behavior, Perceptual Biases, And The Dynamics Of Collective Action
authors: Rishi Dadlani, John S. Mcalister, Alice C. Schwarze, Mari Kawakatsu, Sarah Iams, Tahra L. Eissa, And Nina H. Fefferman
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Dadlani, John S. McAlister, Alice C. Schwarze, Mari Kawakatsu, Sarah Iams, Tahra L. Eissa, and Nina H. Fefferman

Classical models of collective behavior often assume that emergent dynamics result from external and observable interactions among individuals. However, how collective dynamics in human populations depend on the internal psychological processes of individuals remains underexplored. Here, we develop …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044308] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a model showing how internal psychological processes such as planned behavior and perceptual biases shape the emergent dynamics of collective action in human populations.
motivation: Classical models of collective behavior typically assume emergent dynamics arise solely from external, observable interactions among individuals, leaving the role of internal psychological processes underexplored.
method: The authors construct a dynamical model that couples individual-level psychological mechanisms (planned behavior, perceptual biases) with population-level collective action dynamics, likely using agent-based or dynamical-systems approaches.
result: The model demonstrates that internal psychological processes can substantially alter collective dynamics and are necessary for capturing observed patterns of collective action.
conclusion: Incorporating psychological factors into models of collective behavior yields a more complete and accurate account of how human groups mobilize and act.

title: Three-dimensional Microprinting Anisotropic And Deformable Active Matter
authors: Mengshi Wei And Daniela J. Kraft
abstract:
Author(s): Mengshi Wei and Daniela J. Kraft

3D microprinting provides unprecedented control over the shape, propulsion direction, and mechanical properties of active colloids and microstructures. This Perspective explores how anisotropy and deformability can enrich their (non)equilibrium dynamics and collective behavior, and open pathways towards programmable active materials and autonomous microrobots.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041001] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective discusses how 3D microprinting enables anisotropic and deformable active matter with programmable dynamics and collective behavior.
motivation: Active colloids and microstructures benefit from precise control over shape, propulsion, and mechanics, but the roles of anisotropy and deformability remain underexplored.
method: The authors review and perspective on 3D microprinting techniques to fabricate active particles and microstructures with controlled anisotropy and deformability.
result: The perspective highlights how these features enrich nonequilibrium dynamics and collective behavior, opening routes to programmable active materials and autonomous microrobots.
conclusion: 3D microprinting offers a versatile platform for designing active matter with complex, responsive behaviors, though the work is a perspective rather than a new experimental or theoretical result.

title: Phyllotactic Order From Radial Growth Of Spatial Symmetry-breaking Instabilities In Supercritical Conditions
authors: Marcello A. Budroni, Giulio Facchini, Fabian Brau, And Anne de Wit
abstract:
Author(s): Marcello A. Budroni, Giulio Facchini, Fabian Brau, and Anne De Wit

Phyllotactic patterns, i.e., the arrangements of organs around a stem in some plants, represent not only fascinating geometries but also a source of inspiration for advanced biomimetic technological applications. Recently, spatial symmetry-breaking instabilities have been shown to feature, in some c…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044202] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that phyllotactic patterns (leaf arrangements around plant stems) can emerge from radial growth of spatial symmetry-breaking instabilities under supercritical conditions in a reaction-diffusion-like framework.
motivation: Phyllotaxis is a striking botanical geometry with biomimetic technological value, and recent work linked spatial symmetry-breaking instabilities to such patterns, motivating a deeper mechanistic understanding of how radial growth drives these arrangements.
method: The authors analyze spatial symmetry-breaking instabilities in a supercritical regime, likely using continuum/reaction-diffusion modeling to track how radially growing fronts select phyllotactic configurations.
result: Radial growth of symmetry-breaking instabilities is shown to generate phyllotactic order, reproducing the characteristic organ arrangements observed in plants.
conclusion: The findings establish a physical mechanism linking symmetry-breaking pattern formation to phyllotaxis, offering insights relevant to biomimetic applications but unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Restoring Information In Aged Gene Regulatory Networks By Single Knock-ins
authors: Ryan Lefebre, Tyler Schutt, Fabrisia Ambrosio, And Andrew Mugler
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan LeFebre, Tyler Schutt, Fabrisia Ambrosio, and Andrew Mugler

Recent analyses have demonstrated that aging is associated with a loss of information within gene regulatory networks. In this article, a simple theoretical framework is developed for information transmission in gene regulatory networks and this framework is applied to gene expression data from muscle cells in young and old mice. The authors predict how much of the lost information is restored by “knocking in” (exogenously expressing) each gene and find that single knock-ins can restore network information by up to 10%.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044401] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for information transmission in gene regulatory networks predicts that single gene knock-ins can restore up to 10% of age-related information loss in muscle cells.
motivation: Aging has been linked to loss of information in gene regulatory networks, and the authors aim to quantify how much of that loss can be reversed by exogenously expressing individual genes.
method: The authors develop a simple theoretical framework for information transmission in gene regulatory networks and apply it to gene expression data from young and old mouse muscle cells.
result: They predict that knocking in each gene individually can restore network information by up to about 10%, depending on the gene.
conclusion: Single knock-ins may offer a partial strategy to counteract age-related information loss in gene regulatory networks.

title: Statistical Analysis Of Speckle Fields
authors: Ian D. Min-Roberts, Wojciech Rozmus, And Pierre A. Michel
abstract:
Author(s): Ian D. Min-Roberts, Wojciech Rozmus, and Pierre A. Michel

Speckles, or laser hot spots, are the intensity maxima of optically smoothed laser beams that seed instabilities, making a quantitative statistical description of speckles of interest. Earlier statistical theories estimated the number of speckles above an intensity level set for optically smoothed b…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045202] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper provides a statistical analysis of speckle fields, i.e., intensity maxima in optically smoothed laser beams, to quantify their role in seeding instabilities.
motivation: Speckles or laser hot spots are known to seed instabilities, so a quantitative statistical description is needed to understand and predict their occurrence and properties.
method: Earlier statistical theories for the number of speckles above a given intensity level are reviewed and likely extended or refined for optically smoothed laser beams.
result: The paper presents improved statistical estimates or distributions for speckle fields, potentially correcting previous theories and providing a more accurate description of hot-spot statistics.
conclusion: A refined statistical framework for speckle fields is established, useful for modeling laser-plasma interactions and instability seeding, but not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Remotely Tuned Metamaterials With Emergent Elastic Properties
authors: Laurin Sartori, Peer Fischer, And Athanasios G. Athanassiadis
abstract:
Author(s): Laurin Sartori, Peer Fischer, and Athanasios G. Athanassiadis

We introduce a framework for remotely tunable dynamical metamaterials based on interacting nodes embedded in an elastic matrix, effectively forming meta-atoms governed by a programmable nonlinear landscape. Using secondary acoustic radiation forces between microbubble arrays, we predict and experime…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043028] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces remotely tunable elastic metamaterials composed of interacting microbubble nodes in an elastic matrix, using acoustic radiation forces to program nonlinear dynamical properties.
motivation: There is a need for metamaterials whose elastic properties can be dynamically and remotely tuned, enabling adaptive acoustic and mechanical responses.
method: The authors design arrays of microbubbles embedded in an elastic medium, where secondary acoustic radiation forces between bubbles create a programmable nonlinear energy landscape that governs the effective meta-atom behavior.
result: They predict and experimentally demonstrate emergent elastic properties that can be controlled remotely via acoustic driving, showing tunable dynamical responses.
conclusion: This framework enables remotely programmable metamaterials with emergent elastic functionalities, opening routes for adaptive acoustic and mechanical devices.

title: Single-orbital Tight-binding Model For Chiral One-dimensional Hybrid Organic-inorganic Lead Halide Perovskites
authors: Yuya Ominato, Tetsuya Furukawa, Ayumi Ishii, And Tetsuaki Itou
abstract:
Author(s): Yuya Ominato, Tetsuya Furukawa, Ayumi Ishii, and Tetsuaki Itou

We present a single-orbital tight-binding model for the low-energy electronic states of the chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskite [MATH]. The model is constructed from a single effective orbital on each of the four symmetry-rela…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043017] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The authors construct a single-orbital tight-binding model to describe the low-energy electronic states of chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites.
motivation: Chiral 1D hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites exhibit interesting electronic and possibly spin-related properties, but a minimal low-energy model capturing their band structure was lacking.
method: They build a tight-binding model from a single effective orbital on each of four symmetry-related sites, parameterizing hopping terms to reproduce the low-energy electronic dispersion.
result: The model captures the essential low-energy band structure of the chiral perovskite chain, providing a minimal description of its electronic states.
conclusion: The single-orbital tight-binding model offers a tractable framework for understanding electronic properties of chiral 1D hybrid perovskites, potentially useful for further studies of their transport and spin physics.

title: Missing Links Prediction: Comparing Machine Learning With Physics-rooted Approaches
authors: Francesca Santucci, Giulio Cimini, And Tiziano Squartini
abstract:
Author(s): Francesca Santucci, Giulio Cimini, and Tiziano Squartini

An active research line within the broader field of network science is the one concerning link prediction. Close in scope to network reconstruction, link prediction targets specific connections with the aim of uncovering the missing ones, as well as predicting those most likely to emerge in the futu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043020] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares machine-learning and physics-rooted methods for predicting missing links in complex networks, a classical network-science problem with no quantum content.
motivation: Link prediction is a central problem in network science, closely related to network reconstruction, aiming to identify missing or future connections in networks.
method: The authors benchmark machine-learning approaches against physics-inspired statistical methods for link prediction on network datasets.
result: The study characterizes the relative performance and tradeoffs of ML versus physics-rooted link-prediction algorithms.
conclusion: The work clarifies when ML or physics-based approaches are preferable, but remains entirely within classical network science.

title: Suppressing Emittance Growth Via Ion Cloud Traps In Low-energy Beam Transport
authors: Hui Liao, Weidong Chen, Benzheng Chen, Hui Li, Yongchuan Xiao, Yongjia Lü, Xiuxia Cao, Shengjin Liu, Huachang Liu, Sheng Wang, And Liang Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Liao, Weidong Chen, Benzheng Chen, Hui Li, Yongchuan Xiao, Yongjia Lü, Xiuxia Cao, Shengjin Liu, Huachang Liu, Sheng Wang, and Liang Lu

Space-charge compensation is routinely used to mitigate emittance growth in linear accelerator beam transport lines. Severe space-charge effects and incomplete compensation within low-energy beam transport sections universally induce beam divergence and emittance degradation, constituting a key bott…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043023] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies ion cloud traps as a method to suppress emittance growth caused by space-charge effects in low-energy beam transport lines.
motivation: Space-charge compensation is commonly used to reduce emittance growth, but incomplete compensation and severe space-charge effects still cause beam divergence and degradation in low-energy beam transport sections.
method: The authors likely use beam dynamics simulations and/or experimental analysis to evaluate ion cloud traps within low-energy beam transport, focusing on space-charge compensation and emittance evolution.
result: The proposed ion cloud trap approach is reported to mitigate emittance growth and reduce beam divergence in low-energy beam transport.
conclusion: Ion cloud traps may provide an effective means to control space-charge-induced emittance degradation in accelerator beam transport, though the work is outside quantum information science.

title: Cross-order Induced Behaviors In Contagion Dynamics On Higher-order Networks
authors: Kaloyan Danovski, Sandro Meloni, And Michele Starnini
abstract:
Author(s): Kaloyan Danovski, Sandro Meloni, and Michele Starnini

Recent studies have shown that novel collective behaviors emerge in complex systems due to higher-order interactions. However, the way in which the structural correlations of these interactions shape such behaviors remains a significant gap in current research. To address this, we use signatures of …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043010] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how structural correlations in higher-order interactions (e.g., hypergraphs/simplicial complexes) shape collective contagion behavior in spreading dynamics.
motivation: Higher-order interactions have been shown to generate novel collective behaviors in complex systems, but how structural correlations among such interactions modulate these behaviors is not well understood.
method: The authors use structural signatures of higher-order interactions to characterize correlations and analyze contagion/spreading models on higher-order networks.
result: Cross-order induced behaviors are identified, showing that correlations across interaction orders qualitatively alter contagion thresholds and outcomes.
conclusion: Accounting for cross-order structural correlations is essential for accurately predicting spreading behavior on higher-order networks.

title: Quasicrystal Topological Hydrodynamics
authors: Jun-Liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-Jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, And Jin-Hui Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, and Jin-hui Chen

Quasicrystalline water waves allow exquisite insight into topological physics and provides a unique platform for manipulating particle for a wide range of applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031078] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quasicrystalline water waves as a platform for topological hydrodynamics and particle manipulation.
motivation: Quasicrystalline systems offer rich topological physics, and water waves provide a tunable classical platform to explore such phenomena.
method: The authors likely use theoretical and experimental water-wave setups to realize quasicrystalline lattices and analyze topological hydrodynamic modes.
result: They demonstrate topological features in quasicrystalline water waves and show their potential for controlling particle motion.
conclusion: This classical hydrodynamic system provides a new avenue for topological physics, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Erratum: Programmable Quantum Anomalous Hall Insulator In Twisted Crystalline Flatbands [Phys. Rev. X 16, 011015 (2026)]
authors: Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, And Xiaobo Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, and Xiaobo Lu
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 039901] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum notice for a Physical Review X paper on a programmable quantum anomalous Hall insulator realized in twisted crystalline flatbands.
motivation: The original work aimed to realize a programmable quantum anomalous Hall insulator using moiré flatbands in twisted crystalline materials, a topic in condensed matter physics.
method: The erratum corrects errors in the original experimental and theoretical study of twisted crystalline flatband devices; no new methodology is presented in this notice itself.
result: The erratum reports corrections to the published article but contains no substantive new scientific results relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.
conclusion: This paper falls outside the researcher's interests, as it concerns condensed matter phenomena (quantum anomalous Hall effect in moiré flatbands) without connection to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Strong-Field-Driven Intermolecular Coulombic Decay In No Dimers
authors: Jiujiang Wang, Yinsong Tang, Xintai Hao, Xiaorui Xue, Jiaqi Zhou, Xueguang Ren, Xiaoqing Hu, Yong Wu, Jianguo Wang, Yan Yang, Junyang Ma, And Zhenrong Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Jiujiang Wang, Yinsong Tang, Xintai Hao, Xiaorui Xue, Jiaqi Zhou, Xueguang Ren, Xiaoqing Hu, Yong Wu, Jianguo Wang, Yan Yang, Junyang Ma, and Zhenrong Sun

We report the observation of a kinetic-energy-release feature at 3.8 eV in the dissociative double ionization of NO dimers driven by intense femtosecond laser fields. This channel is separated from the 5.6 eV signature of direct Coulomb explosion and is absent under electron-impact ionization. Ab in…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 153202] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a 3.8 eV kinetic-energy-release feature in dissociative double ionization of NO dimers driven by intense femtosecond laser fields, attributed to strong-field-driven intermolecular Coulombic decay.
motivation: The study aims to understand ultrafast ionization and relaxation dynamics in molecular dimers under strong laser fields and to distinguish intermolecular Coulombic decay from direct Coulomb explosion pathways.
method: Intense femtosecond laser ionization combined with kinetic-energy-release spectroscopy was used, with comparison to electron-impact ionization and supporting ab initio calculations.
result: A distinct 3.8 eV feature appears separately from the 5.6 eV direct Coulomb explosion signature and is absent under electron-impact ionization, indicating a strong-field-driven intermolecular Coulombic decay channel.
conclusion: The observation identifies strong-field-driven intermolecular Coulombic decay in NO dimers, providing insight into non-local decay processes in molecular clusters under intense laser fields.

title: Signatures From Pion Condensation And Lepton Flavor Asymmetries In The Cosmological Gravitational Wave Background
authors: Osvaldo Ferreira, Eduardo S. Fraga, And Jürgen Schaffner-Bielich
abstract:
Author(s): Osvaldo Ferreira, Eduardo S. Fraga, and Jürgen Schaffner-Bielich

Large lepton flavor asymmetries at the QCD epoch could generate a pion condensation phase in the early Universe. For large enough tau lepton flavor asymmetries, the speed of sound can exceed the conformal value, leaving a distinctive imprint on the low-frequency gravitational wave (GW) spectrum from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 151001] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how large lepton flavor asymmetries at the QCD epoch can induce pion condensation and leave distinctive imprints on the low-frequency cosmological gravitational wave background.
motivation: The authors aim to connect early-Universe QCD phase transitions and lepton flavor asymmetries to potentially observable gravitational wave signatures.
method: They analyze the thermodynamics of pion condensation in the presence of large tau lepton flavor asymmetries, focusing on how the speed of sound can exceed the conformal value and affect the gravitational wave spectrum.
result: For sufficiently large tau lepton flavor asymmetries, the speed of sound exceeds the conformal value, producing a distinctive feature in the low-frequency gravitational wave spectrum.
conclusion: The work suggests that future gravitational wave observations could probe lepton flavor asymmetries and pion condensation in the early Universe.

title: Enhanced Magneto-optical Intensity Effect In A Helicity-preserving All-dielectric Metasurface At Mie Resonances And The Anapole State
authors: P. V. Zorina, D. O. Ignatyeva, A. E. Bezmenova, A. N. Kalish, S. Xia, Yi Shuai, L. Bi, And V. I. Belotelov
abstract:
Author(s): P. V. Zorina, D. O. Ignatyeva, A. E. Bezmenova, A. N. Kalish, S. Xia, Yi Shuai, L. Bi, and V. I. Belotelov

Nanophotonic structures provide an efficient route to enhancing magneto-optical effects by concentrating electromagnetic fields at subwavelength scales. In this work, we propose an all-dielectric metasurface that preserves the helicity of normally incident light and experimentally demonstrate the re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043509] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates an all-dielectric metasurface that enhances magneto-optical intensity effects by exploiting Mie resonances and the anapole state while preserving helicity.
motivation: Enhancing magneto-optical effects is important for nanophotonic devices, and all-dielectric metasurfaces offer a low-loss platform for field concentration at subwavelength scales.
method: The authors design a helicity-preserving all-dielectric metasurface and characterize its magneto-optical response at Mie resonances and the anapole state, supported by experiments.
result: The metasurface exhibits an enhanced magneto-optical intensity effect due to resonant field confinement and helicity preservation.
conclusion: All-dielectric metasurfaces at Mie and anapole resonances provide an efficient route to boosting magneto-optical effects for compact photonic applications.

title: Controllable Temporal Drift Of Soliton Rain And Its Internal Interaction Dynamics Under Birefringence Phase Regulation
authors: Xue-Peng Wang, Ze-Tian Wang, Hao-Yu Feng, Jun-Yi Ye, Zhi-Cheng Zhang, Hui-Jun Li, Yue-Yue Wang, And Chao-Qing Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Xue-Peng Wang, Ze-Tian Wang, Hao-Yu Feng, Jun-Yi Ye, Zhi-Cheng Zhang, Hui-Jun Li, Yue-Yue Wang, and Chao-Qing Dai

Soliton rain is a typical multipulse dissipative structure in passively mode-locked fiber lasers, where the drift direction of drifting solitons (DSs) reflects the balance among gain, nonlinearity, dispersion, loss, and intracavity filtering. Here, we show that the drift symmetry of soliton rain can…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043508] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies controllable temporal drift of soliton rain and its internal interaction dynamics in passively mode-locked fiber lasers under birefringence phase regulation.
motivation: Soliton rain is a multipulse dissipative structure whose drifting solitons reflect the balance among gain, nonlinearity, dispersion, loss, and intracavity filtering.
method: The authors regulate birefringence phase to control the drift symmetry of soliton rain and analyze the internal interaction dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that birefringence phase regulation can control the drift direction and symmetry of soliton rain, revealing internal interaction dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insight into controlling dissipative soliton structures in fiber lasers, but it is outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, and hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Analytical Phase Kurtosis Of The Constant Gradient Spin Echo
authors: Teddy X. Cai, Nathan H. Williamson, And Peter J. Basser
abstract:
Author(s): Teddy X. Cai, Nathan H. Williamson, and Peter J. Basser

The Gaussian phase approximation (GPA) underlies many standard diffusion magnetic resonance signal models, yet its validity is rarely scrutinized. Here, we assess the validity of the GPA by analytically deriving the excess phase kurtosis [MATH], where [MATH] is the [MATH] cum…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044113] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an analytical expression for excess phase kurtosis in constant-gradient spin-echo diffusion MRI to test the validity of the Gaussian phase approximation.
motivation: The Gaussian phase approximation is widely used in diffusion MRI signal models, but its range of validity is rarely assessed quantitatively.
method: The authors analytically compute the fourth cumulant (excess phase kurtosis) of the phase distribution for a constant gradient spin echo and compare it to the Gaussian prediction.
result: They obtain a closed-form expression showing when non-Gaussian phase effects become significant, providing a criterion for the breakdown of the Gaussian phase approximation.
conclusion: The analytical phase kurtosis offers a practical diagnostic for assessing the validity of the Gaussian phase approximation in diffusion MRI experiments.

title: Dimensional Formulation For The Pseudopotential Lattice Boltzmann Method
authors: Luiz Eduardo Czelusniak, Ivan Talão Martins, And Luben Cabezas Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Luiz Eduardo Czelusniak, Ivan Talão Martins, and Luben Cabezas Gómez

The lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) is commonly implemented in lattice units, requiring conversion procedures to relate simulation parameters to physical quantities. In the pseudopotential multiphase model, this conversion becomes particularly restrictive when attempting to reproduce real-fluid prope…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045302] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a dimensional formulation for the pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann method to improve the mapping between lattice-unit simulations and physical fluid properties.
motivation: The lattice Boltzmann method is often implemented in lattice units, and in pseudopotential multiphase models the conversion between simulation parameters and real-fluid properties is particularly restrictive and error-prone.
method: The authors develop a dimensional formulation that reformulates the pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann method directly in physical units, avoiding or simplifying traditional lattice-unit conversion procedures.
result: The formulation enables more direct reproduction of real-fluid properties in pseudopotential multiphase simulations, reducing the constraints imposed by conventional lattice-unit parameter mapping.
conclusion: The dimensional approach provides a practical route to more physically grounded pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann simulations, though it remains a classical computational fluid dynamics contribution.

title: Towards Critical Branching Mechanism In Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Feixiang Ren And Ling Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Feixiang Ren and Ling Feng

Criticality has been proposed as a key organizing principle in biological neural systems, yet its origin and relevance in artificial neural networks remain unclear. We analyze hidden-state dynamics in trained long short-term memory (LSTM) networks and show that small networks near their optimal trai…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045301] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes critical branching dynamics in trained LSTM recurrent neural networks, linking hidden-state criticality to optimal training in small networks.
motivation: Criticality is a proposed organizing principle in biological neural systems, but its origin and relevance in artificial neural networks remain unclear.
method: The authors examine hidden-state dynamics in trained long short-term memory (LSTM) networks and identify signatures of critical branching.
result: Small LSTM networks near their optimal training regime exhibit critical branching behavior in their hidden-state dynamics.
conclusion: The findings suggest a critical branching mechanism may underlie aspects of recurrent neural network computation, though broader relevance remains to be established.

title: Fully Coherent Soft X-rays From The Nitrogen K-edge To Beyond 1 keV
authors: G. Penco et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): G. Penco et al.

Externally seeded free-electron lasers (FELs) provide radiation with full longitudinal and transverse coherence in the extreme ultraviolet and soft x-ray spectral ranges, inaccessible to conventional laser sources. Until now, externally seeded operation has been limited to the extreme ultraviolet an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043019] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: Researchers demonstrate externally seeded free-electron laser operation producing fully coherent soft X-rays from the nitrogen K-edge to beyond 1 keV.
motivation: Conventional laser sources cannot provide full longitudinal and transverse coherence in the extreme ultraviolet and soft X-ray ranges, and externally seeded free-electron lasers had been limited to longer wavelengths.
