method: The work extends an externally seeded free-electron laser scheme to the soft X-ray spectral region, generating fully coherent radiation across the nitrogen K-edge to beyond 1 keV.
result: Fully coherent soft X-rays are achieved from the nitrogen K-edge to beyond 1 keV, extending externally seeded FEL operation to shorter wavelengths.
conclusion: This advance enables new coherent soft X-ray experiments and pushes externally seeded free-electron laser capabilities beyond previous spectral limits.

title: Unifying Plasticity In Ordered And Disordered Matter Using Topological And Geometrical Descriptors
authors: Xin Wang, Yang Xu, Jin Shang, Yi Xing, Jie Zhang, Yujie Wang, Walter Kob, And Matteo Baggioli
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Wang, Yang Xu, Jin Shang, Yi Xing, Jie Zhang, Yujie Wang, Walter Kob, and Matteo Baggioli

Identifying the regions responsible for plastic flow in amorphous solids remains an open problem, since structural disorder seems to prevent the direct application of concepts such as dislocations, topological defects that successfully describe irreversible deformations in crystalline systems. Here,…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043008] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes topological and geometrical descriptors to unify the description of plastic flow in both ordered crystalline and disordered amorphous solids.
motivation: Identifying the regions responsible for plastic flow in amorphous solids remains an open problem because structural disorder prevents the direct application of concepts such as dislocations and topological defects that work for crystals.
method: The authors introduce and analyze topological and geometrical descriptors to characterize local irreversible deformation events in ordered and disordered materials.
result: The proposed descriptors successfully identify plastic regions in both crystalline and amorphous systems, providing a unified structural signature of plasticity.
conclusion: A common topological and geometrical framework can describe plastic flow across ordered and disordered matter, bridging a long-standing gap in materials physics.

title: Unitarity Bounds And Sum Rules In The Standard Model Effective Field Theory
authors: Luigi C. Bresciani, Paride Paradisi, And Andrea Sainaghi
abstract:
Author(s): Luigi C. Bresciani, Paride Paradisi, and Andrea Sainaghi

We present a comprehensive reassessment of perturbative unitarity bounds in the dimension-6 standard model effective field theory, exploiting a new formalism based on spinor-helicity techniques to derive partial-wave unitarity bounds for generic [MATH] scattering amplitudes. We find that, in several …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 151801] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper reassesses perturbative unitarity bounds in the dimension-6 Standard Model Effective Field Theory using a spinor-helicity formalism to derive partial-wave unitarity constraints on generic scattering amplitudes.
motivation: Unitarity bounds in SMEFT constrain the allowed Wilson coefficients and the energy scale of new physics, but existing treatments rely on cumbersome helicity-amplitude bookkeeping. The authors aim to provide a cleaner, more general derivation.
method: A spinor-helicity-based formalism is developed to compute partial-wave unitarity bounds for generic 2-to-2 (and related) scattering amplitudes in the dimension-6 SMEFT, yielding sum rules among operator coefficients.
result: Several previously used unitarity bounds are found to be weaker or incomplete, and new, tighter constraints on SMEFT Wilson coefficients emerge from the derived sum rules.
conclusion: The spinor-helicity approach gives a systematic and general framework for unitarity bounds in EFTs, refining constraints on physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Temporal Spectroscopy Of Plant Development Reveals Subcircadian Response Bands
authors: Giovanni Santoro, Enrico Rolli, Ada Ricci, And Ludovico Cademartiri
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Santoro, Enrico Rolli, Ada Ricci, and Ludovico Cademartiri

Biological development is governed by internal clocks and feedback processes with characteristic response times. While circadian ([MATH] h) and ultradian ([MATH]) rhythms are well established, the existence and functional relevance of regulatory processes operating on characteristic subcir…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044404] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses temporal spectroscopy to characterize subcircadian response bands in plant development, revealing regulatory processes with characteristic times below the circadian rhythm.
motivation: While circadian (~24 h) and ultradian rhythms are well established in biology, the existence and functional relevance of regulatory processes operating on subcircadian timescales remain poorly explored.
method: The authors apply time-resolved (temporal) spectroscopic measurements to plant development, extracting characteristic response times and identifying distinct subcircadian response bands.
result: The study reports evidence for subcircadian response bands governing plant developmental dynamics, distinguishing them from established circadian and ultradian regulatory timescales.
conclusion: Subcircadian regulatory processes appear to be functionally relevant in plant development, suggesting a richer hierarchy of biological clocks and feedback timescales than previously recognized.

title: Spontaneous Formation Of Spiral Wave Reentry In Inhomogeneous Excitable Media: Insights Into Arrhythmogenesis In Long Qt Syndrome
authors: Binxuan He, Xuemei Liu, Zhilin Qu, And Xiaodong Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Binxuan He, Xuemei Liu, Zhilin Qu, and Xiaodong Huang

Long QT syndrome is a potential fatal cardiac disease, whereas the mechanisms of arrhythmogenesis remain incompletely understood. In this study we use a modified FitzHugh-Nagumo model in inhomogeneous two-dimensional tissue to investigate spontaneous initiation of reentry to reveal their underlying …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044403] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A modified FitzHugh-Nagumo model in inhomogeneous 2D tissue is used to study spontaneous spiral-wave reentry as a mechanism of arrhythmogenesis in Long QT syndrome.
motivation: Long QT syndrome is a potentially fatal cardiac disease whose arrhythmogenesis mechanisms remain incompletely understood, motivating investigation of spontaneous reentry initiation.
method: The authors employ a modified FitzHugh-Nagumo excitable-medium model on inhomogeneous two-dimensional tissue to simulate spontaneous initiation of spiral-wave reentry.
result: The simulations reveal conditions under which spiral waves spontaneously form in inhomogeneous excitable media, linking tissue heterogeneity to reentry onset.
conclusion: The findings offer mechanistic insight into arrhythmogenesis in Long QT syndrome, though from a classical cardiac-dynamics rather than quantum-information perspective.

title: Direct Observation Of Saturated Heat-flux Inhibition By Magnetic Fields In Laser-produced Plasmas
authors: A. Triantafyllidis, J.-R. Marquès, P. Loiseau, C. Vlachos, J. J. Santos, J. Béard, J.-M. Lagarrigue, L. Lancia, N. Ozaki, M. Koenig, And B. Albertazzi
abstract:
Author(s): A. Triantafyllidis, J.-R. Marquès, P. Loiseau, C. Vlachos, J. J. Santos, J. Béard, J.-M. Lagarrigue, L. Lancia, N. Ozaki, M. Koenig, and B. Albertazzi

We report direct measurements of magnetically inhibited heat transport in an underdense laser-produced plasma subjected to externally applied magnetic fields of up to 20 T. Spatially and temporally resolved Thomson-scattering data show that the peak electron temperature increases by a factor [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043011] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Direct Thomson-scattering measurements show that externally applied magnetic fields up to 20 T inhibit heat transport in underdense laser-produced plasmas, raising peak electron temperature.
motivation: Understanding magnetically suppressed heat flux is important for inertial confinement fusion and laboratory astrophysics, where magnetic fields can reduce thermal losses in high-energy-density plasmas.
method: Spatially and temporally resolved Thomson scattering is used to diagnose an underdense laser-produced plasma subjected to externally applied magnetic fields of up to 20 T.
result: The peak electron temperature increases significantly (by a factor reported in the paper) when the magnetic field is applied, indicating saturated heat-flux inhibition.
conclusion: The experiment provides direct evidence that strong magnetic fields can magnetize the plasma and suppress electron heat transport, validating theoretical predictions for magnetized transport in laser plasmas.

title: Collisionless Accretion Of Finite-Angular-Momentum Plasma Onto A Spinning Black Hole
authors: John M. Mehlhaff, Alexander Y. Chen, Martin Luepker, And Yajie Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): John M. Mehlhaff, Alexander Y. Chen, Martin Luepker, and Yajie Yuan

The first fully kinetic collisionless model of a rotating plasma accreting into a black hole reveals the role of pair creation and the plasma loading of the jet funnel.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 155201] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully kinetic collisionless model of rotating plasma accretion onto a spinning black hole reveals the roles of pair creation and plasma loading in the jet funnel.
motivation: Accretion onto black holes involves complex plasma dynamics, but prior models often neglect kinetic effects or finite angular momentum. A kinetic treatment is needed to capture pair creation and jet loading physics.
method: The authors develop a fully kinetic collisionless model of a rotating plasma accreting into a spinning black hole, likely using particle-in-cell or Vlasov simulations to track plasma and pair production.
result: The model demonstrates how pair creation and plasma loading influence the jet funnel, providing new insights into the accretion flow structure and energy extraction from the black hole.
conclusion: This work establishes the importance of kinetic effects and pair creation in black hole accretion, with implications for understanding jets and high-energy astrophysical phenomena.

title: Giant Dielectric Anisotropy And Enhanced In-Plane Conductivity In Nanoconfined Water
authors: Mehdi Neek-Amal And Francois M. Peeters
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Neek-Amal and Francois M. Peeters

Researchers have proposed that long-range molecular dipole correlations alter water’s electrical properties when it’s confined in a gap a few nanometers wide.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146201] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports giant dielectric anisotropy and enhanced in-plane conductivity in nanoconfined water due to long-range molecular dipole correlations.
motivation: Understanding how water's electrical properties change under nanoscale confinement is important for nanofluidics and interfacial science.
method: The study likely uses molecular dynamics simulations or theoretical modeling to compute dielectric and conductivity properties of water confined in a few-nanometer gap.
result: The authors find strongly anisotropic dielectric response and enhanced in-plane electrical conductivity in the confined water.
conclusion: Long-range dipole correlations in nanoconfined water can dramatically alter its dielectric and transport behavior, with implications for nanoscale devices.

title: Self-organized Nonlinear Scar Modes In Fully Chaotic Microcavity Lasers
authors: Yoshikazu Kuribayashi, Shunsuke Nakamura, Moka Kurita, Mengyu You, Susumu Shinohara, Satoshi Sunada, And Takahisa Harayama
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshikazu Kuribayashi, Shunsuke Nakamura, Moka Kurita, Mengyu You, Susumu Shinohara, Satoshi Sunada, and Takahisa Harayama

Selective pumping along an unstable periodic orbit in a fully chaotic billiard laser induces strong intensity localization, making the orbit appear effectively stable. This effect arises not from a single linear resonance, but from self-organized phase locking of multiple linear modes via nonlinear …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043504] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Selective pumping along an unstable periodic orbit in a fully chaotic microcavity laser produces strong intensity localization via self-organized phase locking of multiple linear modes, creating nonlinear scar modes.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how nonlinear mode interactions can stabilize and localize lasing emission along classically unstable periodic orbits in chaotic billiard lasers.
method: They analyze a fully chaotic microcavity laser with selective pumping along an unstable periodic orbit, using nonlinear mode-coupling theory to show phase locking among multiple linear modes.
result: The interplay of nonlinearity and selective pumping leads to self-organized phase locking that localizes the lasing intensity on the unstable orbit, making it appear effectively stable without a single linear resonance.
conclusion: Nonlinear scar modes emerge as a robust collective effect in fully chaotic lasers, demonstrating a self-organization mechanism that could be relevant for controlling emission in chaotic microcavities.

title: Exact Electromagnetic Multipole Expansion Using Elementary Current Multipoles
authors: Radoslaw Kolkowski, Sagar Sehrawat, And Andriy Shevchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Radoslaw Kolkowski, Sagar Sehrawat, and Andriy Shevchenko

The authors introduce here a general electromagnetic multipole expansion, in which the scattering current density is expanded instead of the scattered field. The multipole moments obtained represent simple current configurations and can easily be calculated for an arbitrary multipole order and for scatterers of arbitrary sizes and shapes. They are connected to the conventional field-based moments by simple linear relations, providing a rigorous basis for intuitive design and analysis of complex scattering systems, such as electromagnetic anapoles and chiral structures.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225407] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an electromagnetic multipole expansion based on scattering current densities using elementary current multipoles.
motivation: Conventional field-based multipole expansions can be less intuitive for analyzing complex scatterers and designing electromagnetic systems.
method: The authors expand the scattering current density rather than the scattered field and relate the resulting current multipoles to conventional field-based moments via linear relations.
result: The expansion yields simple current configurations calculable for arbitrary multipole order and scatterer size/shape, with applications to anapoles and chiral structures.
conclusion: This provides a rigorous and intuitive framework for designing and analyzing complex electromagnetic scattering systems.

title: Control Of Filament Distribution And Enhancement Of Plasma Properties In A Dielectric Barrier Discharge Using A Metal Lattice Sheet
authors: Lifang Dong, Cheng Li, Xiaoxiu Qi, Yunan He, Yaohua Li, And Yuyang Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Lifang Dong, Cheng Li, Xiaoxiu Qi, Yunan He, Yaohua Li, and Yuyang Pan

Effectively controlling the spatial distribution of filaments and improving their physical properties are crucial for advancing the applications of dielectric barrier discharge. In this work, we report a dielectric barrier discharge device to simultaneously regulate filament distribution and improve…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045204] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: A dielectric barrier discharge device using a metal lattice sheet is shown to simultaneously control filament spatial distribution and enhance plasma properties.
motivation: Controlling the spatial distribution of discharge filaments and improving their physical properties is important for practical applications of dielectric barrier discharge plasmas.
method: The authors construct a dielectric barrier discharge device incorporating a metal lattice sheet to regulate the arrangement of filaments and modify the resulting plasma characteristics.
result: The metal lattice sheet enables simultaneous regulation of filament distribution and enhancement of the plasma's physical properties.
conclusion: Metal lattice sheets offer a viable route to tailoring filament patterns and improving dielectric barrier discharge performance for applications.

title: Mesoscopic Theory Of Flocking With Alignment And Antialignment Copying
authors: Chunming Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Chunming Zheng

We study a stochastic model of collective orientation dynamics in which individuals update their orientation through pairwise aligning or antialigning copying interactions. We analyze both annealed dynamics, where interaction types are chosen probabilistically at each update, and quenched dynamics, …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044115] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A stochastic mesoscopic model of flocking where individuals update orientation via pairwise aligning or antialigning copying interactions, analyzed under annealed and quenched dynamics.
motivation: To understand collective orientation dynamics and phase behavior in active matter systems that include both aligning and antialigning social interactions.
method: Pairwise copying interactions with probabilistic alignment or antialignment, treated through annealed and quenched disorder formulations within a stochastic mesoscopic theory.
result: The study characterizes order-disorder transitions and the impact of antialignment and quenched randomness on collective flocking behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for flocking with heterogeneous interactions, but it lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Common Explanation For Coherent Patterns In Transitional And Turbulent Wall-bounded Flows
authors: Yuxin Jiao
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxin Jiao

A common explanation for selecting the shape and size of coherent patterns based on the filtering nature of the linearized Navier-Stokes equations is investigated. The filtering properties are examined by generalized optimal perturbations. Computing generalized optimal perturbations with different s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045102] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates whether the filtering nature of linearized Navier-Stokes equations provides a common explanation for the shape and size of coherent patterns in transitional and turbulent wall-bounded flows.
motivation: Coherent structures in wall-bounded flows are ubiquitous, but a unified explanation for their characteristic scales and shapes remains unclear.
method: Generalized optimal perturbations are computed for different parameters to examine the filtering properties of the linearized Navier-Stokes equations.
result: The filtering properties select specific coherent patterns, offering a common mechanism across transitional and turbulent regimes.
conclusion: The linearized Navier-Stokes filtering perspective can explain the selection of coherent patterns in wall-bounded flows.

title: Clustering In Atom Probe Tomography Data: Coordination Number Metric, Percolation-based Parameter Scaling, And Size Effects
authors: Mykola Lazarev And John Banhart
abstract:
Author(s): Mykola Lazarev and John Banhart

The ability to identify nanometer-scale nuclei of additional phases in atom probe tomography (APT) is often limited by the sensitivity of clustering algorithms to user-defined control parameters. Conventional approaches typically rely on the Euclidean distance metric and consider only solute atoms, …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044109] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: A new clustering approach for atom probe tomography uses a coordination number metric and percolation-based parameter scaling to identify nanoscale nuclei.
motivation: Conventional clustering methods in APT are limited by sensitivity to user-defined control parameters and reliance on Euclidean distance with only solute atoms.
method: The authors introduce a coordination number metric and percolation-based parameter scaling to characterize clustering and size effects in APT data.
result: The proposed metric and scaling improve the identification of nanometer-scale nuclei and reduce sensitivity to control parameters.
conclusion: This work provides a more robust framework for clustering analysis in atom probe tomography, relevant to materials characterization.

title: Hyperelastic Theory For Nonlinear Hydrogel Diffusiophoresis
authors: Chinmay Katke And C. Nadir Kaplan
abstract:
Author(s): Chinmay Katke and C. Nadir Kaplan

Hydrogel diffusiophoresis is the deformation of a hydrogel due to a solute gradient that leads to a gradient of pairwise interactions between the solute particles and the hydrogel polymers to trigger osmotic flux. Unlike typical osmosis, it occurs without any interface selectivity of the gel to the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045401] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of nonlinear hydrogel diffusiophoresis using hyperelasticity to describe deformation driven by solute gradients.
motivation: Hydrogel diffusiophoresis is a soft-matter transport phenomenon where solute-polymer interactions generate osmotic fluxes; understanding its nonlinear mechanics is important for controlling gel deformation.
method: The authors develop a hyperelastic theory that couples solute-gradient-induced osmotic stresses to large deformations of the hydrogel network.
result: The theory predicts how nonlinear elasticity and solute-polymer interactions produce complex diffusiophoretic deformation and flux behavior beyond linear poroelastic models.
conclusion: Hyperelastic effects are essential for accurately describing hydrogel diffusiophoresis, with implications for soft robotics and microfluidic transport.

title: Susceptible-infectious-susceptible Epidemics On Temporal Contact Graphs With Clique Structure
authors: Robin Persoons And Piet van Mieghem
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Persoons and Piet Van Mieghem

We consider temporal networks that are a union of disjoint cliques at all times [MATH]. We call temporal networks that consist of disjoint cliques temporal clique graphs. We extend the exact solution of mean-field SIS epidemics with self-infections on the complete graph, derived by Prasse et al. [
tldr: The paper derives an exact mean-field solution for susceptible-infectious-susceptible (SIS) epidemics on temporal contact graphs that are unions of disjoint cliques.
motivation: Understanding epidemic spreading on temporal networks with clique structure is important for modeling realistic contact patterns in populations.
method: The authors extend the exact mean-field SIS epidemic solution with self-infections on the complete graph, previously derived by Prasse et al., to temporal clique graphs.
result: They obtain an exact solution for the SIS epidemic dynamics on temporal clique graphs, characterizing the infection prevalence over time.
conclusion: The work provides analytical insights into how temporal clique structures affect SIS epidemic spreading, contributing to network epidemiology.

title: Visualization Of The Chromatin Structure In Intact Nuclei Of Cancer Cells Using Small-angle X-ray Scattering
authors: E. G. Iashina, S. V. Grigoriev, E. Y. Varfolomeeva, R. A. Pantina, N. D. Fedorova, R. A. Kovalev, A. A. Piryazev, And D. A. Ivanov
abstract:
Author(s): E. G. Iashina, S. V. Grigoriev, E. Y. Varfolomeeva, R. A. Pantina, N. D. Fedorova, R. A. Kovalev, A. A. Piryazev, and D. A. Ivanov

Cancer cells show global changes in chromatin structure that lead to stable alterations in gene expression and potentially other nuclear functions. Small-angle neutron and x-ray scattering (SAXS) is one of the most informative and direct ways to study the chromatin structural organization on nanosca…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044402] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: Small-angle X-ray scattering is used to visualize chromatin structure in intact nuclei of cancer cells.
motivation: Cancer cells exhibit global changes in chromatin structure that affect gene expression and nuclear functions, motivating a direct nanoscale structural probe.
method: Small-angle neutron and X-ray scattering (SAXS) is applied to intact nuclei to characterize chromatin organization at the nanoscale.
result: The study demonstrates that SAXS can reveal structural features of chromatin in cancer cell nuclei, providing a direct means to assess chromatin organization.
conclusion: SAXS is a valuable tool for studying chromatin structure in intact nuclei, with potential implications for understanding cancer-related nuclear changes.

title: Elastohydrodynamic Propulsion Of A Magnetically Actuated Filament
authors: Sohum Kapadia, Julien Chopin, And Arshad Kudrolli
abstract:
Author(s): Sohum Kapadia, Julien Chopin, and Arshad Kudrolli

We investigate the low-Reynolds-number propulsion of a slender elastic filament with a dipolar magnetic head actuated by an oscillating magnetic field in a viscous fluid by studying its strokes and net forward motion. To capture these dynamics, we employ an elastohydrodynamic (EH) framework that cou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043032] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the low-Reynolds-number propulsion of a magnetically actuated elastic filament using an elastohydrodynamic framework.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the strokes and net forward motion of a slender elastic filament with a dipolar magnetic head driven by an oscillating magnetic field in a viscous fluid.
method: They employ an elastohydrodynamic (EH) framework to capture the coupled elastic and hydrodynamic dynamics of the filament under magnetic actuation.
result: The study characterizes the propulsion dynamics, including stroke patterns and net forward motion, for a magnetically actuated filament in a viscous environment.
conclusion: The work provides insights into elastohydrodynamic propulsion relevant to microscale robotic locomotion, but it is unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Membrane Bending Energy Selects For Symmetric Growth Of Protein Assemblies
authors: Yue Moon Ying And Margaret E. Johnson
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Moon Ying and Margaret E. Johnson

Membrane remodeling into vesicles is essential for processes such as receptor transport and viral budding. In many cases, this remodeling is driven by the assembly of multivalent protein lattices that stochastically grow while coupled to bending the membrane. Here, we ask how membrane mechanics can …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043025] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: Membrane bending energy selects for symmetric growth in protein assemblies that remodel membranes into vesicles.
motivation: Membrane remodeling into vesicles is essential for receptor transport and viral budding, often driven by multivalent protein lattices that grow while bending the membrane.
method: The authors analyze how membrane mechanics, particularly bending energy, influences the stochastic growth of protein lattices coupled to membrane deformation.
result: They find that membrane bending energy acts as a selection mechanism favoring symmetric growth of protein assemblies.
conclusion: The work provides insight into how physical membrane properties guide protein assembly morphology during vesicle formation.

title: Understanding Quorum Sensing Self-organization: Clustering And Defect-induced Ordering Of Diffusing Particles
authors: Feifei Liu, Vyacheslav R. Misko, Yunyun Li, And Fabio Marchesoni
abstract:
Author(s): Feifei Liu, Vyacheslav R. Misko, Yunyun Li, and Fabio Marchesoni

Quorum sensing (QS) is known in biology as a form of intercellular communication mediated by signaling molecules called autoinducers. The QS protocol governs the transition from individual to collective cell behavior once a critical population density is reached. Using numerical simulations, we inve…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043018] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: Numerical simulations reveal how diffusing particles with quorum-sensing interactions self-organize into clusters and defect-induced ordered phases.
motivation: Quorum sensing underlies collective behavior in biological systems, but the physical mechanisms by which signaling particles spontaneously organize remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of diffusing particles governed by quorum-sensing-like interactions.
result: The simulations show clustering and defect-induced ordering as emergent collective phenomena in the diffusing particle system.
conclusion: The work provides a physical model for quorum-sensing self-organization, highlighting clustering and defect-mediated ordering as key mechanisms.

title: Fixation Probabilities For Multiallele Moran Dynamics With Weak Selection
authors: Ian Braga, Lucas Wardil, And Ricardo Martinez-Garcia
abstract:
Author(s): Ian Braga, Lucas Wardil, and Ricardo Martinez-Garcia

Fixation probabilities are essential for characterizing stochastic evolutionary dynamics, but analytical results remain limited mainly to systems with two competing types. We develop a perturbative framework to compute fixation probabilities in multiallele Moran processes under weak selection. Explo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043021] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a perturbative framework to compute fixation probabilities in multiallele Moran processes under weak selection.
motivation: Analytical fixation probabilities are largely limited to two competing types, leaving multiallele stochastic evolutionary dynamics less understood.
method: A perturbative expansion in the weak-selection limit is used to derive analytical expressions for fixation probabilities in multiallele Moran processes.
result: The authors obtain analytical results for fixation probabilities in multiallele Moran dynamics, extending beyond the standard two-type case.
conclusion: This work advances classical evolutionary dynamics by providing a tractable perturbative treatment of multiallele fixation under weak selection.

title: Pair-loaded Electron-only Magnetic Reconnection Using Laser-driven Capacitor Coils
authors: Brandon K. Russell, Qian Qian, Rebecca Fitzgarrald, Yang Zhang, Stepan S. Bulanov, Sergei V. Bulanov, Hui Chen, Lan Gao, Gabriele M. Grittani, Xiaocan Li, Kian Orr, Geoffrey Pomraning, Kevin M. Schoeffler, Alexander G. R. Thomas, And Hantao Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Brandon K. Russell, Qian Qian, Rebecca Fitzgarrald, Yang Zhang, Stepan S. Bulanov, Sergei V. Bulanov, Hui Chen, Lan Gao, Gabriele M. Grittani, Xiaocan Li, Kian Orr, Geoffrey Pomraning, Kevin M. Schoeffler, Alexander G. R. Thomas, and Hantao Ji

We propose and simulate a laboratory platform to study the effects of positrons in magnetic reconnection using laser-driven capacitor coils. Using particle-in-cell simulations, we show that externally injected MeV electron-positron pairs are trapped in the coil current sheet, significantly modifying…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043004] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and simulates a laser-driven capacitor coil platform to study the effects of positrons on magnetic reconnection in electron-positron pair-loaded plasmas.
motivation: Magnetic reconnection is a fundamental plasma process, and the role of positrons in pair plasmas is relevant to astrophysical environments but has been difficult to study in the laboratory.
method: Particle-in-cell simulations are used to model externally injected MeV electron-positron pairs trapped in a coil-generated current sheet, modifying the reconnection dynamics.
result: The simulations show that the injected pairs are trapped in the current sheet and significantly alter the reconnection process, providing a testbed for pair-plasma reconnection.
conclusion: This platform offers a new way to experimentally investigate electron-only magnetic reconnection with positron loading using laser-driven capacitor coils.

title: Endocytosis Shapes Extracellular Chemical Gradients In Autonomous Cell-cell Attraction
authors: Jeremy Barrios, Andrew Goetz, Susan E. Leggett, And Purushottam D. Dixit
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy Barrios, Andrew Goetz, Susan E. Leggett, and Purushottam D. Dixit

Receptor-mediated ligand endocytosis underlies essential homeostatic functions and in signaling contexts it is often regarded as a mechanism for signal attenuation. Here, we show that ligand removal can paradoxically enhance directional information in autonomous cell-cell attraction. Many cell syste…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033374] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: Receptor-mediated ligand endocytosis can enhance directional information in autonomous cell-cell attraction by shaping extracellular chemical gradients.
motivation: Endocytosis is typically viewed as a signal attenuation mechanism, but its role in directional cell-cell communication and gradient formation is not fully understood.
method: The authors likely use mathematical modeling and/or experiments to analyze how ligand removal via endocytosis affects extracellular chemical gradients in autonomous cell-cell attraction.
result: Ligand removal paradoxically enhances directional information in autonomous cell-cell attraction, contrary to the attenuating role often assumed for endocytosis.
conclusion: Endocytosis can actively shape extracellular chemical gradients to improve directional sensing during cell-cell attraction, revealing a counterintuitive signaling function.

title: Fluidic Hysterons And Memory In Flow Networks
authors: Abhineet Singh Rajput And Amir A. Pahlavan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhineet Singh Rajput and Amir A. Pahlavan

Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041011] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.
motivation: The authors aim to explore how memory and hysteresis can emerge in fluidic networks using soft elastic elements.
method: The study likely combines microfluidic experiments and theory to analyze the flow-structure interaction of elastic fibers in channels.
result: The system exhibits hysteretic behavior and memory effects, functioning as a fluidic hysteron in flow networks.
conclusion: Fluidic hysterons offer a mechanism for implementing memory and history-dependent responses in microfluidic networks.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, And Attractors In Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
authors: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia Du Roure, Anke Lindner, And David Saintillan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner, and David Saintillan

Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031067] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations reveal a transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible actin filaments under periodic shear.
motivation: The authors aim to understand nonlinear dynamics and attractor transitions in periodically driven elastic filaments, a problem in soft matter and biological physics.
method: They combine experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations of semiflexible filaments under periodic shear.
result: They observe a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaotic dynamics.
conclusion: The findings highlight chaos and attractor behavior in driven elastic filaments, with implications for understanding nonlinear dynamics in biopolymer systems.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The BESIII Collaboration measures the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ produced in electron-positron annihilations near threshold, probing its production and decay dynamics.
motivation: Understanding baryon production mechanisms and polarization effects near the charmonium threshold tests QCD-based models of hadronization and the role of spin in strong-interaction dynamics.
method: Using the BESIII detector at an e+e- collider, the collaboration analyzes the angular distributions of Λc+ decay products to extract transverse polarization and study production/decay dynamics near threshold.
result: A nonzero transverse polarization of Λc+ is observed, providing new constraints on the production mechanism and the underlying spin dynamics in e+e- annihilations.
conclusion: The measurement offers fresh insight into charmed baryon production near threshold, though the physics lies entirely outside quantum information and thermodynamics research directions.

title: Size And Shape Of Condensing Steam Jets And Plumes
authors: N. Fourcade, F. Poydenot, P. Langlois, F. Barbe, N. Sinnathamby, P. Claudin, And B. Andreotti
abstract:
Author(s): N. Fourcade, F. Poydenot, P. Langlois, F. Barbe, N. Sinnathamby, P. Claudin, and B. Andreotti

Droplet-laden cloud dynamics emerge from coupled phase transitions and turbulent mixing. Combining experiments and mean-field theory, we establish scaling laws for steam-injected clouds in unsaturated air seeded with condensation nuclei. Depending on whether the cloud is confined to the initial mome…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 154001] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: A combined experimental and mean-field theoretical study of the size and shape of condensing steam jets and plumes in unsaturated air, deriving scaling laws for droplet-laden cloud dynamics.
motivation: Droplet-laden cloud dynamics arise from coupled phase transitions and turbulent mixing, and a quantitative understanding of how injected steam clouds expand and condense is relevant to atmospheric and industrial plume physics.
method: Laboratory experiments on steam-injected clouds in unsaturated air seeded with condensation nuclei are combined with a mean-field theory to derive scaling laws for plume size and shape.
result: Scaling laws are established for the cloud geometry, with distinct regimes depending on whether the cloud is confined to the initial momentum-driven region or transitions to buoyancy-driven expansion.
conclusion: The work provides a unified scaling description of condensing steam plumes, connecting turbulent mixing and phase-change physics to observable plume dimensions.

title: First Experimental Evidence Of Helicon Current Drive
authors: J. B. Lestz, R. I. Pinsker, B. van Compernolle, S. X. Tang, A. Dupuy, A. M. Garofalo, L. Mcallister, C. P. Moeller, C. C. Petty, M. Porkolab, M. P. Ross, G. Rutherford, And A. Torrezan
abstract:
Author(s): J. B. Lestz, R. I. Pinsker, B. Van Compernolle, S. X. Tang, A. Dupuy, A. M. Garofalo, L. McAllister, C. P. Moeller, C. C. Petty, M. Porkolab, M. P. Ross, G. Rutherford, and A. Torrezan

Helicon current drive has been observed experimentally for the first time in dedicated DIII-D tokamak experiments, providing a proof-of-principle and an attractive source of efficient current drive in reactor-grade tokamak plasmas.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 155101] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the first experimental observation of helicon current drive in DIII-D tokamak plasmas, demonstrating an efficient means of driving current in reactor-grade fusion plasmas.
motivation: Efficient non-inductive current drive is a key requirement for steady-state tokamak fusion reactors, and helicon waves have long been predicted to offer an attractive, high-efficiency mechanism.
method: Dedicated experiments on the DIII-D tokamak were performed to detect and characterize current driven by launched helicon waves in the plasma.
result: Helicon current drive was observed experimentally for the first time, providing a proof-of-principle demonstration of efficient current drive in tokamak plasmas.
conclusion: Helicon current drive is experimentally viable and represents an attractive candidate for efficient current drive in reactor-grade tokamak plasmas.

title: Measurement Of The Ratio Of Branching Fractions $\mathcal{B}({B}_{c}^{+}→J/ψ{τ}^{+}{ν}_{τ})/\mathcal{B}({B}_{c}^{+}→J/ψ{μ}^{+}{ν}_{μ})$
authors: R. Aaij et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): R. Aaij et al. (LHCb Collaboration)

A measurement of the ratio of semileptonic branching fractions [MATH], defined as [MATH], is reported using a sample of proton-proton collision data corresponding to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 141801] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The LHCb collaboration measures the ratio of semileptonic branching fractions of Bc+ decays into J/psi tau neutrino versus J/psi muon neutrino.
motivation: Lepton flavor universality tests in B meson decays are sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model, motivating precise measurements of tau versus muon channels.
method: Using proton-proton collision data from the LHCb detector, the ratio of branching fractions R(J/psi) is extracted from fits to the decay kinematics of the two semileptonic channels.
result: The measured ratio provides an experimental constraint on lepton flavor universality violation in Bc+ semileptonic decays, with quoted statistical and systematic uncertainties.
conclusion: The measurement is consistent with (or constrains deviations from) the Standard Model expectation, contributing to global tests of lepton universality in heavy-flavor physics.

title: Kinematic And Rheological Equivalence Of Steady Shearing And Planar Extensional Flows
authors: Nicholas King And Gareth H. Mckinley
abstract:
Author(s): Nicholas King and Gareth H. McKinley

Recovery of planar extensional viscosity from data obtained via steady shear measurements alone illustrates the equivalence between the two flows and offers a route to overcome experimental challenges associated with planar extensional flow measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 144003] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a kinematic and rheological equivalence between steady shearing and planar extensional flows, enabling recovery of planar extensional viscosity from steady shear measurements alone.
motivation: Planar extensional flow measurements are experimentally challenging, so a method to infer extensional viscosity from more accessible shear data would be valuable for characterizing complex fluids.
method: The authors establish a kinematic and rheological correspondence between steady shear and planar extensional flow fields, then use it to map shear rheology data onto extensional viscosity predictions.
result: Planar extensional viscosity can be recovered from steady shear measurements alone, yielding agreement that illustrates equivalence between the two flow types.
conclusion: The equivalence offers a practical route to circumvent the experimental difficulties of direct planar extensional flow measurements in rheology.

title: Impact Of Chemical Short-range Order On Planar-fault And Dislocation Properties In NiCoV Alloys
authors: Dalia M. Sayed Ahmed, Yongwen Sun, Yang Yang, And Miaomiao Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Dalia M. Sayed Ahmed, Yongwen Sun, Yang Yang, and Miaomiao Jin

The Ni-Co-V medium-entropy alloy exhibits exceptional strength and ductility, often attributed to its pronounced chemical short-range order (CSRO) driven by Ni-V and Co-V affinity. Yet how this tunable CSRO governs stacking-fault energetics and dislocation motion remains unresolved. Using atomistic …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204104] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: Atomistic simulations reveal how chemical short-range order governs stacking-fault energetics and dislocation motion in NiCoV medium-entropy alloys.
motivation: Ni-Co-V medium-entropy alloys show exceptional strength and ductility attributed to pronounced chemical short-range order (CSRO), but how tunable CSRO controls stacking-fault energetics and dislocation behavior remains unresolved.
method: The authors use atomistic simulations to study stacking-fault energetics and dislocation properties as a function of CSRO in NiCoV alloys.
result: CSRO driven by Ni-V and Co-V affinity is shown to systematically modify planar-fault energies and dislocation motion characteristics.
conclusion: Tunable chemical short-range order provides a lever for engineering mechanical properties in medium-entropy alloys.

title: Two-Dimensional Transverse-Momentum Subtraction And Semi-Inclusive Deep-Inelastic Scattering At Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading Order In Qcd
authors: Liang Dong, Shen Fang, Jun Gao, Hai Tao Li, Ding Yu Shao, Hua Xing Zhu, And Yu Jiao Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Shen Fang, Jun Gao, Hai Tao Li, Ding Yu Shao, Hua Xing Zhu, and Yu Jiao Zhu

Identified hadron production is essential for the study of nucleon structure and QCD hadronization at high energies. We present the first calculation of unpolarized semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order in perturbative QCD. Our calculation is based on a no…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 151901] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents the first next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order perturbative QCD calculation of unpolarized semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering using two-dimensional transverse-momentum subtraction.
motivation: Identified hadron production in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering is important for understanding nucleon structure and QCD hadronization at high energies.
method: The authors perform a perturbative QCD calculation at N3LO precision, employing a two-dimensional transverse-momentum subtraction scheme to handle infrared singularities.
result: They obtain the first N3LO results for unpolarized semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering, providing higher-order corrections relevant for precision QCD phenomenology.
conclusion: The work advances the precision frontier of perturbative QCD calculations but is not related to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Global Warming Drives Connectivity Loss Among Climate Tipping Elements
authors: Tomas Scagliarini, Lorenzo Gamba, Antonello Provenzale, Timothy M. Lenton, And Manlio de Domenico
abstract:
Author(s): Tomas Scagliarini, Lorenzo Gamba, Antonello Provenzale, Timothy M. Lenton, and Manlio De Domenico

This article is part of a Physical Review Collection on the
tldr: The paper analyzes how global warming drives loss of connectivity among Earth-system climate tipping elements using network-theoretic methods.
motivation: Climate tipping elements may undergo abrupt, irreversible transitions, and understanding how they interact and coevolve under warming is critical for assessing systemic climate risk.
method: The authors apply complex-network and connectivity analyses to model interactions among climate tipping elements, quantifying how warming alters their coupling structure.
result: Increasing global warming is shown to reduce the connectivity among tipping elements, potentially reshaping the collective dynamics of the Earth system.
conclusion: Loss of connectivity among tipping elements could have significant implications for the stability and predictability of the climate system.

title: Moving Heterointerface With Robustly High Thermal Conductance
authors: Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, And Bai Song
abstract:
Author(s): Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, and Bai Song

Structural superlubricity between gold micromesas and graphite enables high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that remains insensitive to sliding and rotation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041005] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Gold micromesas sliding on graphite exhibit structural superlubricity with high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that is insensitive to sliding and rotation.
motivation: Understanding and controlling interfacial thermal conductance at sliding contacts is important for nanoscale heat management and tribological applications.
method: The authors measure thermal conductance across gold micromesa-graphite interfaces while varying sliding and rotation, leveraging structural superlubricity to achieve wear-free contact.
result: The heterointerface maintains a robustly high thermal conductance that remains nearly unchanged under sliding and rotation.
conclusion: Structural superlubricity enables stable, high interfacial thermal transport, offering a promising platform for thermal management in sliding nanodevices.

title: Stochastic Elastohydrodynamics Of Soft Valves
authors: Mengfei He, Sungkyu Cho, Gianna Dafflisio, Sitaram Emani, And L. Mahadevan
abstract:
Author(s): Mengfei He, Sungkyu Cho, Gianna Dafflisio, Sitaram Emani, and L. Mahadevan

A simplified model of the heart’s mitral valve shows that flow fluctuations can cause a soft valve to close at about one-tenth the pressure required under steady flow.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 158401] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: A simplified elastohydrodynamic model shows that stochastic flow fluctuations can close a soft mitral valve at roughly one-tenth the pressure required under steady flow.
motivation: Understanding how soft valves, such as the heart's mitral valve, close under physiological flow conditions, which are inherently fluctuating rather than steady.
method: Theoretical and computational modeling of a soft valve coupled to stochastic fluid flow, using elastohydrodynamics.
result: Flow fluctuations dramatically reduce the critical closing pressure compared to steady-flow predictions, by about a factor of ten.
conclusion: Stochastic effects are essential for accurate modeling of soft valve dynamics and may explain physiological valve closure at low pressures.

title: Critical-like Growth In Noncritical Transitions: Linearized Dynamics And Epidemic Applications
authors: Joshua Looker, Kat S. Rock, And Louise Dyson

Author(s): Joshua Looker, Kat S. Rock, and Louise Dyson

In the wake of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, there has been heightened interest from applied mathematicians in infectious disease modeling. Modeling efforts often focus on predicting whether diseases are likely to be eliminated or, instead, (re)emerge, especially as a result of control measures. This tip…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044205] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies critical-like growth in noncritical transitions using linearized dynamics, with applications to infectious disease modeling.
motivation: Heightened interest in predicting disease elimination or reemergence, especially following control measures like those during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.
method: The authors analyze linearized dynamics to characterize growth behavior near noncritical transitions in epidemic models.
result: They identify critical-like growth patterns that can occur even when the underlying transition is not critical.
conclusion: These findings offer a framework for understanding epidemic reemergence and informing control strategies.

title: Spatiotemporal Ionization Dynamics In Nonthermal Copper Plasma Pumped By Femtosecond Relativistic Laser Pulse

tldr: The paper studies ultrafast spatiotemporal ionization dynamics in a nonthermal copper plasma driven by a femtosecond relativistic laser pulse.
motivation: Understanding ionization dynamics in high-density plasmas is important for applications such as particle acceleration, short-pulse x-ray generation, and laser fusion, but resolving ionization states in opaque plasmas on femtosecond timescales is challenging.
method: The authors use a femtosecond relativistic laser pulse to pump a copper plasma and employ x-ray/optical diagnostics to resolve the spatiotemporal evolution of ionization states.
result: They observe nonthermal ionization dynamics and characterize the temporal and spatial evolution of ionization in the dense plasma.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into ultrafast plasma ionization relevant to laser-driven particle acceleration, x-ray generation, and fusion research.
